### ai-cmd-customer-6.12 — “Bulk-like” batch semantics (no REST bulk routes)

Customer APIs encode **multi-record** work inside single calls — AI should mirror with **array params** or **compounds**, not dashboard `bulk_`* intents.


| Batch pattern                     | API shape                             | Current AI                                                             | Proposed                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Multi-add cart**                | Client loops or single preview        | `add_services_to_cart` accepts `serviceNames[]`/`serviceIds[]` already | ✅ Already covered — `resolveServices` + `extractServiceNamesFromPrompt` resolve multiple names from one prompt ("add X and Y to cart") |
| **Multi-service book**            | `POST multi-service/book` one payload | `book_multi_service` shipped                                           | ✅ Promoted (**6.2.6**); "compound with quote" superseded — see **6.12.5**                                                              |
| **Package multi-line reschedule** | `lines[]` on package reschedule       | `reschedule_package_visit_self`, `reschedule_package_lines`            | ✅ Shipped — `reschedule_package_lines` parses "visits N and M" into an explicit `lines[]` array                                        |
| **Intake multi-answer**           | Repeated `POST …/answers`             | `submit_intake_answers` shipped (**6.4.1**)                            | ✅ Already batches in one compound step; eval-harness wiring gap closed — see **6.12.6**                                                |
| **Cancel all upcoming**           | `POST me/bookings/bulk-cancel` (new)  | `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings` (new)                                    | ✅ Shipped — two-step confirm (preview then confirm=true), see **6.12.7**                                                              |
| **Export all data**               | Single `GET me/data` dump             | `privacy_export`                                                       | ✅ single-shot “bulk read”                                                                                                              |
| **Delete account**                | Single `DELETE me/data`               | `privacy_delete`                                                       | ✅ single-shot “bulk delete”                                                                                                            |

"Compound with quote": investigated and found **superseded**, not a gap — `handleBookMultiServiceLogic` (`ai-self-service-booking.logic.ts`) never calls a booking-creation API directly; it resolves the selected services and returns a `navigate: { path: 'checkout', ... }` handoff with the services pre-loaded into the session cart, exactly the same shape as `handleBookPackageLogic` and every other booking-creation intent in this codebase (single-service `book_appointment`/`book_with_cash`, packages) — none of them compound-chain an explicit quote step before booking, because pricing is shown natively on the checkout screen the customer is navigated to. **Goal:** Make `provider-app/` the fastest path for stylists and floor managers between appointments — voice-friendly, one-sentence actions, minimal typing. **Provider mobile only** (`ProviderAiCommandService` / `PROVIDER_INTENT_SCHEMA`); dashboard admin stays under **ai-cmd-ext**.

**Principle:** Session context first (`bookingId` from open detail modal, `lastPush`, today’s timeline). Prefer **mutate + confirm** for irreversible actions (cancel, mark paid). Mirror every **prov-exp** UI action in `PROVIDER_EXP_UI_AI_PARITY` (`provider-exp-ai-parity.fixtures.ts`).

**Pain themes from product:** check-in while greeting client, “who’s next” on busy floor, mark paid at chair, fill cancellation gaps, retail upsell without leaving booking, running late SMS, offline queue after spotty Wi‑Fi, push confirm/mark paid from notification, clinic draw queue, end-of-day sweep, pending confirmations, in-progress vs complete status, multi-service spa days, gift card fulfillment queue, patient lookup before draw, tax line on payment breakdown, team view vs own calendar scope, hands-free voice between clients.

**Baseline (already wired — harden, don’t re-build):** `summarize_client`, `check_in_client`, `mark_running_late`, `mark_paid`, `payment_sweep`, `add_retail_to_booking`, `send_client_message`, `block_my_time`, `request_time_off`, `team_floor_status`, `team_whos_next`, `suggest_waitlist_for_gap`, `confirm_booking_from_push`, `explain_last_push`, clinic collection queue — see `provider-ai-command.service.ts` switch + **ai-cmd-ext-3**.

Reused `PROVIDER_REVIEWS_INBOX_LOW_RATING_MAX` (rating ≤ 3) from the existing dashboard util for the "low rating" flag, so both surfaces agree on what counts as a bad review. Added detector/formatter/period-inferrer to `ai-provider-exp-2.util.ts`, dispatch case + LLM enum entry, 10 EN + 10 HY/RU fixtures (locale-parity counts bumped 45→55).

  **Design note — architectural discovery**: this section was substantially larger in true scope than any prior `ai-cmd-provider-5.x` sub-section, and required a genuine design decision before any code could be written. The existing pre-classifier compound machinery (`decomposeProviderMobileCompoundPrompt` / `handleProviderMobileCompound` in `ai-provider-mobile-hints.util.ts`) only supports **literal multi-clause text splitting** on `; `/` and `/` then ` with a narrow verb whitelist, and its segment classifier only recognizes a handful of push/booking-read actions. None of the 9 recipes' TODO-listed step chains were reachable through it, and — more importantly — most of the TODO's own canonical example prompts ("Fill my 3pm gap from waitlist", "Brief me before Jane at 2", "Next draw — open chart and mark collected") are **single natural-language sentences with no explicit "and"/"then" connector**, not literal multi-clause commands. Forcing them through clause-splitting would have required rewording every canonical example and still wouldn't match how a provider would actually phrase these requests.

  Given that, each of the 9 recipes was built as its **own dedicated top-level intent** (new action names: `chair_closeout`, `running_late_notify`, `gap_waitlist_fill`, `cancel_and_recover`, `pre_visit_brief`, `end_of_day_close`, `reschedule_and_notify`, `clinic_draw_flow`, `push_confirm_check_in` — none previously existed as action names anywhere in the classifier enum), each with its own detector (`ai-provider-compound-recipes.util.ts`, all 9 detectors + a shared `rescueProviderCompoundRecipeIntent`) and its own **orchestrator handler** (9 new private methods on `ProviderAiCommandService`) that calls the *exact same, already-shipped* single-action private methods/service calls used by the plain single-step actions (`handleMarkVisitComplete`, `handleCancelBookings`, `providerClientContext.handleIntent('summarize_client', …)`, etc.) in sequence, short-circuiting on the first failed/clarify-needed step and merging summaries + details at the end. No new mutate business logic was written anywhere — every recipe is pure orchestration over code that was already independently tested in earlier `ai-cmd-provider-5.x` sections, including confirm-gating (bulk-mutate steps like `cancel_bookings`/`mark_no_shows`/`payment_sweep` still honor `context?.confirmed === true` exactly as they do standalone, so an unconfirmed compound correctly short-circuits into the same "confirm this bulk action?" clarify response a lone call would produce).

  Dispatch is wired at **two points** for defense in depth: (1) a new `dispatchProviderCompoundRecipe` pre-classifier check runs first in `executeCommand`, alongside the 4 existing pre-classifier compound checks (`providerBooking`/`pushNotifications`/`giftFulfillment`/`providerMobile` compounds) — this is the primary, always-correct path since it runs before the LLM ever sees the prompt; (2) the 9 action names were also added to the classifier enum + a matching `case` in the main dispatch switch, as a robustness fallback in case a paraphrase slips past the deterministic pre-check and the LLM classifier ends up emitting the action name directly.

  Verification-time collision found and fixed: `isRescheduleAndNotifyPrompt` originally accepted bare "push" as a move/reschedule cue (matching the TODO's own "push this to 5" phrasing), which risked colliding with the heavily-overloaded push-*notification* vocabulary elsewhere in the same file (e.g. "notify me about new push notifications" would have matched both the move-cue and the notify-cue). Narrowed to require "push" only in an explicit "push this/it/her/him/them appointment/booking/visit" construction, dropping the bare TODO example in favor of safety — consistent with this session's established narrow-the-new-detector-first collision hierarchy.

  Scope note: fixture coverage for this section is intentionally lighter than the `~10 EN + 10 HY/RU` bar used for atomic single-step intents elsewhere in this audit. Each recipe's *constituent* actions (mark_paid, cancel_bookings, summarize_client, etc.) already carry their own full linguistic fixture coverage from the `ai-cmd-provider-5.1`–`5.13` sections that built them; this section's job is orchestration correctness (does the right sequence of already-tested calls fire, in the right order, with results merged correctly), not re-proving each constituent step's own language robustness. Coverage here is 1 canonical-example detector test + 1 full-stack integration dispatch test per recipe (9 + 9 = 18 tests), plus a shared "already-classified" rescue no-op test and an intents-count test.

New domain tests: 21/21 passing (`ai-provider-compound-recipes.util.spec.ts` detector unit tests + `ai-provider-compound-recipes.integration.spec.ts` full-stack dispatch tests, one per recipe). Broader sweep (`provider-ai-command`, `provider-mobile.*integration`, `ai-cmd-eval`, `ai-provider-mobile-hints`): 447/449 passing — the 2 failures are the same pre-existing/unrelated pair confirmed in **5.12**/**5.13**'s verification (`ProviderMobileService booking customer context`, `Sprint 22 provider AI intelligence integration`), neither in files touched this section. Full deterministic eval suite: clean except the 1 long-standing known baseline failure (`meta-guide-rescue-provider-swipe-approval`).

## ai-cmd-provider-6 — Provider app API ↔ AI coverage audit

**Audit (2026-06):** Map every `provider-app/` REST call to a provider AI intent (or document `no-ai`). Sources: `provider-mobile.controller.ts`, `gift-cards.controller.ts` (`GiftCardProviderController`), `upload.controller.ts`, `POST /invitations/:token/accept`, `provider-app/src/`** API wrappers.

**Totals:** ~~**69** HTTP operations → **~~32 covered** (handler in `ProviderAiCommandService` or delegated service), **~22 partial** (registry intent exists but dashboard-only handler or deferred eval), **~15 gaps** (no provider intent / no handler wire).

**Bulk note:** Provider has **no** REST paths named `bulk_`*. Bulk behavior is:


| Pattern                 | Where                                                              | AI today                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Bulk cancel**         | AI `cancel_bookings` matches N bookings → internal `executeCancel` | ✅ intent; uses service layer not `PUT …/cancel` per row                                                                |
| **Bulk status/paid**    | AI `update_bookings`, `payment_sweep`, `mark_no_shows`             | ✅ with `BULK_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD=2` swipe confirm                                                                        |
| **Bulk retail replace** | `PUT …/bookings/:id/retail-sales` `lines[]` replaces full cart     | ✅ `set_retail_sales_lines` — full cart bulk replace, done **ai-cmd-provider-6.6.1**                                    |
| **Bulk push read**      | `POST …/push/notifications/read-all`                               | ✅ `mark_all_notifications_read` — bulk-marks all unread in one call, done **ai-cmd-provider-6.8**/**6.13.2**           |
| **Bulk gift queue**     | List queues + mark one-by-one                                      | ✅ `gift_card_creation_queue`/`mark_card_ready`/`delivery_queue`/`accept_delivery`/`mark_out_for_delivery`/`mark_delivered`/`capture_delivery_proof`/`notify_delay` all wired into `ProviderAiCommandService` too (not dashboard-only) |

## ai-cmd-dashboard-6 — Dashboard admin API ↔ AI coverage audit

**Audit (2026-06):** Map every `frontend/` dashboard REST call to a dashboard AI intent (or document `no-ai` / UI-only). Sources: `frontend/src/`** (`api.get/post/put/patch/delete` via `lib/api.ts`), excluding `public-api.ts` (see **ai-cmd-customer-6**) and `app/provider/*` pages (see **ai-cmd-provider-6**). Backend route reference: controllers under `backend/src/modules/`**.

**Totals:** ~~**229** HTTP operations → **~~52 covered** (registry intent + handler in `AiCommandService` or delegated domain service), **~68 partial** (read/explain OK but mutate path missing, or intent exists without REST wire), **~58 gaps** (no intent), **~51 N/A** (auth bootstrap, file upload bytes, export downloads, analytics telemetry).

**Registry context:** **252** dashboard intents in `DASHBOARD_INTENTS` — many are **AI-native** (no 1:1 REST button): `bulk_smart_cancel`, `cancel_bookings`, `fill_unused_slots`, compounds. This audit is **REST → intent**, not intent count.

**Bulk note:** Dashboard has **no** REST paths named `bulk_`*. Bulk behavior is:


| Pattern                          | REST example                                             | AI today                                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Bulk cancel/update bookings**  | Repeated `PUT …/bookings/:id`                            | ✅ `cancel_bookings`, `update_bookings`, `bulk_smart_cancel` (internal matcher) |
| **Bulk catalog seed**            | `POST …/onboarding/apply-catalog`, playbook seed         | ✅ `apply_onboarding_catalog` (**6.2.2**, replaces the false-equivalence originally proposed with `bulk_create_catalog`), `apply_clinic_playbook`, and `import_clinic_catalog_csv` (**ai-cmd-dashboard-6.9**) — CSV import now wired |
| **Bulk schedule delete**         | `DELETE …/schedules/templates` + `{ templateIds[] }`     | ✅ `delete_schedule_templates` — shipped **ai-cmd-dashboard-6.5.1**, re-confirmed **6.18.1**; this row was a stale duplicate |
| **Bulk schedule apply**          | `POST …/schedules/templates/apply`                       | ✅ `apply_schedule`                                                             |
| **Bulk agent rebook/undo**       | `POST …/agents/tasks/:id/rebook-all`, `…/undo-latest`    | ✅ `rebook_all_from_agent_task`, `undo_latest_agent_task` — shipped **ai-cmd-dashboard-6.1.1**/**6.1.2**, re-confirmed **6.18.3**; this row was a stale duplicate |
| **Bulk retail cart replace**     | `PUT …/bookings/:id/retail-sales` `lines[]`              | ✅ `set_retail_sales_lines` — full cart bulk replace, done **ai-cmd-dashboard-6.3.1**  |
| **Bulk product recommendations** | `PUT …/inventory/recommendations/…` + `{ productIds[] }` | ✅ `set_recommended_products` — shipped **ai-cmd-dashboard-6.12.1**, re-confirmed **6.18.2**; this row was a stale duplicate |
| **Bulk locale strip**            | (no REST — service layer)                                | ✅ `bulk_strip_disabled_locale_translations`                                    |
| **Bulk service currency**        | (no REST — service layer)                                | ✅ `bulk_update_service_currency`                                               |

All 5 target prompts were Armenian (hy) imperatives — "Բացիր billing settings" (open), "Բացիր invoice և payment method settings", "Բացիր subscription settings", "Բացատրիր loyalty program settings-ը" (explain), "Բացատրիր loyalty points-ը այստեղ" — and all 5 were being swallowed by `hasHoursCue` in `ai-explain-business-hours-and-location.util.ts`, which had a bare, unqualified `բաց` (meaning "open") substring check intended to catch phrases like "Երբ եք բաց" ("when are you open"). The bug: Armenian "բացիր" (imperative "open [it]") and "բացատրիր" ("explain") BOTH contain "բաց" as their literal word root — a linguistic false-positive, not a copy-paste collision like the rest of this session's fixes. Fixed with a negative lookahead, `բաց(?!իր|ատրիր)`, so the cue still matches standalone "բաց" (open, adjective) but not when it's the root of these two unrelated derived verbs (verified against the one existing hy business-hours fixture, "Երբ եք բաց շաբաթ օրը", which still matches correctly since "բաց" there is followed by a space, not "իր"/"ատրիր"). tsc holds at known baseline (1362, no new-file diffs); targeted sweep of `ai-explain-business-hours-and-location`/`ai-billing-loyalty-dashboard`/`ai-intent-rescue` (208 tests): only the one already-known pre-existing `reschedule_booking` vs `find_soonest_appointment` failure remains. Confirmed via full golden-eval-set diff (94 → 88 failures) that exactly these 5 target ids disappeared, plus 1 bonus (`business-currency-hy-explain-settings`, the identical "բացատրիր" root collision hitting a different domain), with zero new ids added.

### consumer-app-e2e-bugs.1 — Manual E2E pass over the consumer-app, bugs found

Scope per explicit user request ("test the app e2e every possible feature and report bugs in todo", clarified to **consumer-app only**, later extended twice with "do all possible tests"/"continue to do e2e qa tests"): drove the real consumer-app UI in a browser against a local backend + Postgres, using a forged local customer JWT session for `test-cancel-sub@example.com`, and — with separate explicit user authorization per action, re-confirmed each time a token expired across a mid-session dev-server restart — a forged local business-owner JWT to (a) seed working-hours for one employee via the real `POST .../schedules/templates` + `.../templates/apply` REST endpoints (not raw SQL) so booking-completion could actually be tested, and (b) temporarily flip `settings.giftCards.purchaseEnabled` to `true` to test the gift-card purchase flow (reverted back to `false` afterward, confirmed via a follow-up `GET`). Covered: welcome/salon-home, single- and multi-service booking **all the way through to a real confirmed appointment**, account page (profile, data & privacy, rewards, notification prefs, referral, gift-code redemption, gift cards, bookings, subscriptions), the AI booking assistant, package browsing, gift-card purchase, subscription-plan selection at checkout, guest manage-booking-via-token, and the provider-review browse/submit UI. **Not fully exercised** (blocked by legitimate environment/business-config gaps, not skipped): completing a subscription purchase past Stripe checkout, and submitting a review before a booking has actually completed — see below.

**P0 — crashes the whole app / hammers the backend**

- [x] **e2e-bug.1 — Booking assistant crashes with a 500 on (at least) the first message of a session.** **Fixed:** broke the circular import that left `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` undefined — extracted `mapAccessTierToRoleProfile` to `ai-role-profile.util.ts`, moved empty-state intent membership to `ai-product-guide-empty-state-intent.util.ts` (so `access-control.matrix` no longer pulls session→platform), and switched platform to a live registry binding instead of a snapshot assign. Regression in `ai-platform.util.spec.ts`; browser-verified `"What's the cheapest service?"` and `"What services do you offer?"` both return `201` with replies (no 500). Original report: Clicking any suggested prompt ("What's the cheapest service?") or typing free text and hitting Send returns `Request failed with status code 500` in the chat UI. Backend log shows an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')` at `validatePublicAssistantAction` (`backend/src/modules/ai/ai-platform.util.ts:448`), called via `gatePublicAssistantActionLogic` → `AiPlatformService.gatePublicAction` → `PublicBookingAssistantService.chat` → `CustomerAiCommandService.runPublicAssistant` → `AiGatewayService.execute` → `PublicBookingController.assistant`. Root cause: `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` (`ai-platform.util.ts:68`, re-exported from `ai-command-registry.build.ts`) is `undefined` at the moment `validatePublicAssistantAction` first runs, so `.includes(action)` throws on the array itself, not on `action`. `npx madge --circular` confirms `ai-platform.util.ts` sits on a real circular-import cycle with `ai-command-registry.build.ts` (via `access-control.matrix.ts` → …product-guide chain… → `guide-flow.merge.util.ts` → `ai-platform.util.ts` → `ai-command-registry.build.ts` → back to `access-control.matrix.ts`), which is consistent with a module-init-order race populating the constant late. However, empirically **a second identical request in the same running process succeeds (`201 Created`)** — the failure is not permanently frozen for the process lifetime, so the exact trigger (first-ever hit of this code path per process vs. per something else) needs closer isolation before a fix; flagging with full repro evidence rather than guessing at the fix. This blocks the AI assistant — a headline feature of the consumer app — for what looks like every fresh session's first turn. **Update (two further live repros this session, both confirming the scope is action-specific and process-persistent, not a one-time first-message fluke):** "What's the cheapest service" and "What services do you offer?" both crash with this exact error, reliably, repeatedly, including in brand-new sessions — never self-resolving on retry for these two prompts specifically. Root-caused precisely why: both resolve to intents inside `PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` (`customer-ai-command.util.ts:269-284` — `list_services`, `find_services_under_budget`, `business_info`, etc.), the exact set gated by `validatePublicAssistantAction`'s `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS.includes(action)` check. Confirmed via full trace that `list_services` (what both prompts resolve to) IS correctly present in `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` under normal module init (seeded in `PUBLIC_ANONYMOUS_INTENTS` → `SURFACE_INTENT_LISTS.public` → unioned into `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS`, all in `ai-command-registry.build.ts`) — so this isn't a registry gap, it's that the array itself is `undefined` for this process's entire lifetime because the circular-import cycle resolved unfavorably at boot. Confirmed the cycle closes via a slightly different path than originally suspected: `ai-platform.util.ts` → `ai-command-registry.build.ts` → `access-control.matrix.ts` → `ai-product-guide-empty-state.util.ts` → `ai-product-guide-session.util.ts` → back to `ai-platform.util.ts` (importing `mapAccessTierToRoleProfile`). **Practical characterization, refined**: once a dev-server process boots with this cycle resolved badly, every prompt whose intent falls in the small `PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` allowlist crashes identically and permanently for that process's lifetime — it is not per-session or first-message-only, it's per-process and per-action-category. Prompts resolving to actions outside that allowlist (e.g. `create_booking`, most self-service intents) are unaffected, which is why "book a facemassage" works fine in the same broken process while any services/pricing/business-info question always 500s. A dev-server restart would very likely clear it for that new process (until the cycle resolves badly again), but the actual fix must break the circular import so this state can't recur.
- [x] **e2e-bug.6 — Gift-card checkout page enters an infinite render/fetch loop for any signed-in customer, hammering the backend with duplicate requests.** **Fixed:** memoized `customer` (`getStoredCustomerProfile`) and `serviceIds` (`parseGiftCardServiceIdsFromSearch`) in `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx`, and made the prefill `setForm` a no-op when values are unchanged — stops the render→quote storm. Regression: `GiftCardCheckoutPage.integration.spec.tsx` (monetary/package/subscription). Browser-verified one `POST .../gift-cards/quote` on mount (not 150+). Original report: Reproduced by opening `/s/:slug/gift-cards/checkout` while signed in: within seconds the console fills with React's `"Maximum update depth exceeded"` error and 40+ duplicate `POST .../gift-cards/quote` requests fire back-to-back (confirmed via `read_network_requests`, not an artifact of any single click). **Root cause, fully traced in `consumer-app/src/pages/GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx`:** line 93, `const customer = slug ? getStoredCustomerProfile(slug) : null;`, is called directly in the render body with no memoization — if this reads from `localStorage` via `JSON.parse` (consistent with the rest of the customer-session code in this app), it returns a **new object reference on every render**. A `useEffect` at lines 127–138 lists `customer` itself (the object, not a primitive) in its dependency array, so React sees it as "changed" on every render and unconditionally calls `setForm(prev => ({...prev, ...}))` — which always produces a new `form` object even when every field value is unchanged. The quote-fetching `useEffect` at lines 182–199 depends on `form`, so it re-fires on every one of those renders, calling `quotePublicGiftCardPurchase` (POST `/gift-cards/quote`) again — closing the loop: new `customer` reference → `setForm` → new `form` reference → re-quote → re-render → new `customer` reference → … This is a correctness bug independent of anything the user clicks — it starts as soon as the page mounts for a signed-in customer — and is a real backend-load/DoS-adjacent concern since it fires unbounded duplicate requests as fast as the event loop allows. **Fix direction:** memoize `customer` with `useMemo(() => (slug ? getStoredCustomerProfile(slug) : null), [slug])`, and/or depend on primitive fields (`customer?.name`, `customer?.email`, `customer?.phone`) instead of the object itself in the line-127 effect. **Update (re-confirmed during the "package"/"subscription" gift-type checklist pass):** reproduced this live, unauthenticated even, and confirmed it's completely independent of card type (happens for `monetary` too) — but there is a **second, independently-sufficient root cause in the same file that must also be fixed, or the loop will persist even after the `customer` fix above lands.** Line 87, `const serviceIds = parseGiftCardServiceIdsFromSearch(params);`, is also called unmemoized in the render body and (per `gift-card-purchase.util.ts:35-42`) returns a brand-new array literal every single render regardless of whether `params` changed. That array is a dependency of `buildPayload`'s `useCallback` (line 176), so `buildPayload` gets a new function reference every render on its own; the quote-fetching effect (lines 182-203) depends on `buildPayload`, so it re-fires every render through this path too, with no dependency on `customer`/`form` at all. **Regression-test note: after applying the `customer` memoization fix above, re-verify the loop is actually gone — if `serviceIds` isn't also wrapped in `useMemo(() => parseGiftCardServiceIdsFromSearch(params), [params])`, the console will still show `"Maximum update depth exceeded"` and the quote-request storm will still fire, just via the second mechanism.** Live-verified via `read_network_requests`: with an empty form the loop burns CPU silently (blocked by `canQuoteGiftCardPurchase`'s guard before any fetch), but the instant a purchaser email is filled in, dozens of duplicate `POST /gift-cards/quote` calls fire back-to-back, several failing outright with `net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` (the browser's own per-origin connection-pool exhaustion) — this is a real request-storm/backend-load risk, not just console noise. **Re-confirmed still unfixed, live, on a fresh re-enable pass (`grep`-verified `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx` unchanged since this was written, and reproduced from scratch):** re-enabled `giftCards.purchaseEnabled` for this business plus the same real package (`570ca68d-…`, "Massage Package") and subscription plan (`22222222-…`, "Monthly Massage Plan"), then hit both checkout URLs directly (`?cardType=package&packageId=…` and `?cardType=subscription&subscriptionPlanId=…`) as the already-signed-in test customer — **the loop fires on page load alone, with zero interaction required**, since the purchaser email auto-fills from the signed-in profile the instant the page mounts. `read_network_requests` captured **150+ `POST /gift-cards/quote` + matching `OPTIONS` preflight pairs within about 2 seconds** for the package type alone, roughly half already failing with `net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`; the subscription type reproduced the identical `"Maximum update depth exceeded"` console spam just as fast. Both card types are equally and fully broken. Test config reverted immediately after (`giftCards` settings restored to the original `{"purchaseEnabled": false}`, confirmed via follow-up `SELECT`).

**P1 — booking funnel blocking / broken UX**

- [x] **e2e-bug.2 — Fixed CTA bar renders behind the bottom tab bar on the Services page after a hard navigation or reload.** **Fixed:** `useSalonTabOverlaysVisible` now defaults overlays to visible on mount and applies `salon-tab-active` via `useLayoutEffect` + ref-counted acquire/release (no longer waits for Ionic `useIonViewDidEnter`, which skips hard loads). Regression in `use-salon-tab-overlays-visible.spec.tsx`. Browser hard-load of `/services`: class present; CTA `elementFromPoint` hits "Select date & time", not the tab bar. Original report: `.consumer-fixed-action-bar` (`theme/variables.css`) is `position: fixed; bottom: 0; z-index: 90` and relies on `body.salon-tab-active { bottom: var(--consumer-tab-bar-total-height) }` to sit above the tab nav (`nav`, `z-index: 100`). The `salon-tab-active` class is toggled by `useSalonTabOverlaysVisible()` (`hooks/use-salon-tab-overlays-visible.ts`) via Ionic's `useIonViewDidEnter`, which only fires on **in-app (client-side router) navigation**. Confirmed via `document.body.className` + `elementFromPoint`: navigating to `/s/:slug/services` by clicking the "Book" tab sets `salon-tab-active` correctly and the button renders above the nav bar; hard-reloading or directly loading that same URL leaves the class unset, so the "Continue with selected services" button visually and functionally collides with the tab bar — `elementFromPoint` at the button's coordinates returns the tab bar's "Book" label, not the button. Real-world triggers: page refresh mid-booking, a bookmarked/shared link, or an external link (QR code, SMS, email) landing directly on `/services`. Fix direction: derive the tab-active state from the current route on mount (not just view-lifecycle events), so a fresh/hard page load computes the same visibility state a client-side navigation would.
- [x] **e2e-bug.7 — Packages become completely unreachable in the UI once a business enables multi-service booking, with no alternative entry point.** **Fixed:** (1) `shouldShowServicesCatalogEntry` keeps the Services "Packages" button visible when `hasPackages` even if multi-service is on; (2) `App.tsx` `/book/:serviceId` route guards the reserved `any` segment so IonRouterOutlet cannot land on BookPage ("Service not found"). Helpers/tests in `package-booking` + `multi-service-booking`. Browser: Packages CTA on `/services` → `/book/any` shows Massage Package; hard-load `/book/any` also works. Original report: Confirmed for `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, which has both a real package ("Massage Package", $344.25) and `multiService.enabled: true`. `ServicesPage.tsx:73`, `const showLegacyBookingEntry = services.length > 0 && !multiEnabled;`, gates the **only** button (`legacyBookingLabel`, linking to `/book/any` → `MultiServicePickerPage`, which renders the package cards via `ConsumerPackageCards`) that lets a customer reach packages — so the button never renders at all once multi-service is on. Confirmed no other link, card, or nav entry anywhere in the app points at `/book/any` or a packages catalog for human users (grepped the whole consumer-app source); the only other code path that can reach `PackageConfirmPage`/`PackageCheckoutPage` is the AI booking assistant's own internal navigation helper (`consumer-assistant-navigate.util.ts`) — which is itself broken by **e2e-bug.1**. Compounding this: hard-navigating directly to `/s/:slug/book/any` (bypassing the missing button, e.g. via a shared deep link) doesn't even render the right page — `IonRouterOutlet` resolves it to `BookPage`'s "Service not found" state (treating `"any"` as a literal, non-existent `serviceId` for the also-registered `/s/:slug/book/:serviceId` route) instead of `MultiServicePickerPage`, even though the more specific route is declared first in `App.tsx`. Net effect: for this business configuration, package purchase is unreachable through the UI by any means. Once unblocked by seeding schedule data and manually navigating past the missing button, the actual package purchase flow itself was not further exercised this pass (time-boxed) — worth a dedicated retest once the entry point is fixed.

**P2 — data/UX quality**

- [x] **e2e-bug.3 — Raw axios error strings are shown to users instead of the backend's actual message, in at least 5 places across unrelated pages.** **Fixed:** `formatFriendlyNetworkError` unwraps Nest/axios `response.data.message` (string or validation array) and suppresses bare "Request failed with status code NNN"; wired on the original 5+ sites plus gift-card order cancel, assistant send failure, My Results / Documents / Lab-to-book query errors. Specs: `consumer-network-ux.util.spec.ts`. Browser: bad manage-token shows "This manage link is invalid or expired." with no axios status string. Original report: Pattern: frontend catch-blocks surface `err.message` (e.g. `"Request failed with status code 400"` / `"...403"` / `"...404"`) instead of parsing the JSON error body's `message` field (which the backend already sends correctly in every case checked). Confirmed instances: (1) multi-service booking's date/slot page shows this instead of `"No available block found for the selected services"` when `GET .../multi-service/suggest-block` 400s; (2) account page → "Redeem a gift you received" shows this instead of a friendly "invalid or already-used code" message when `POST .../gift-cards/claim` 404s; (3) same generic-error pattern reproduced on the Services page for a legitimate `400` (services with no shared provider); (4) guest manage-booking page (`/s/:slug/manage?bookingId=…&token=…`) shows this instead of `copy.manageBookingInvalidLink` when the token is wrong (`POST` returns a correct `403`) — root-caused precisely here: `ManageBookingPage.tsx`'s render does `message={error ?? copy.manageBookingInvalidLink}`, but the catch block that sets `error` always populates it with the raw axios message first, so the intended friendly fallback is dead code, never reachable; (5) the provider-profile review form shows this instead of `"Reviews are available after you complete an appointment with this specialist"` when `POST .../providers/:id/reviews` correctly 400s for a not-yet-completed booking. Five independent call sites, same failure shape — strongly suggests a shared root cause (whatever HTTP client wrapper the consumer-app uses for these calls isn't unwrapping `error.response.data.message` before showing it to the user) and a single shared fix (e.g. in the axios error interceptor / `public-api.ts` helper) rather than 5 separate patches.

By contrast, the same pages' checkboxes and notification-preference switches *do* expose correct `checkbox`/`switch` roles, and the AI assistant's own suggestion chips *do* expose `button` roles — so this isn't a wholesale app-wide gap, it's localized to whatever shared "primary CTA" / "text button" component several pages reuse. Worth auditing that shared component for a missing `role="button"`/native `<button>` element.

The language picker itself works correctly (`ConsumerLanguagePicker.tsx` updates its own label to "Հայերեն"/"Русский" immediately), and a large fraction of **in-flow** copy translates correctly — specialist/time/service selection instructions, date formatting (`14/07/2026` `DD/MM/YYYY`), review-section labels, promo/pricing labels, and primary CTA buttons ("Ամրագրել այց", "Հաստատել ամրագրումը", "Выберите специалиста" all render properly. Still a real bug worth fixing (it signals a genuine unstable-dependency issue somewhere in the shared root, and dumping 100+ console errors on every cold load is bad hygiene/would look alarming in production error monitoring), just not an ongoing battery/CPU drain as originally suspected. Checked the most likely per-page offenders on the `SalonTabRoute` side and ruled them out — `useTenantBootstrap`'s two effects have correctly stable dependency arrays; `useConsumerNativePush`/`useHomeScreenWidgetSync`'s effects both early-return on `!Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` (true in-browser). Root cause not pinned to an exact line — would need a React DevTools Profiler "why did this render" trace on a cold-loaded `/`, since it never reproduces on in-app client-side navigation, only a fresh/hard page load. **Fix direction:** profile a hard-loaded `/`, find the component stuck re-rendering during mount, likely a `setState` inside a `useEffect` with a non-memoized dependency in one of the always-mounted `App.tsx` wrappers (candidate: `useMobileAppVersionPolicy`'s effect, whose deps come from `AppVersionGate`'s inline, unmemoized `consumerCopyForLocale(...)` call).

- [x] **e2e-bug.16 — The consumer-app's entire offline-mutation-queueing mechanism is dead code: built, unit-tested, but never wired into the real network layer, so it can never actually engage.** **Fixed:** `attachConsumerOfflineAxios(http)` in `public-api.ts` registers a response interceptor that calls `tryQueueConsumerOfflineAxiosError` on failed mutating requests (cancel/reschedule allowlist), returns a 202 `{queued, offline}` payload so existing UI (`isOfflineQueuedPayload` / `offlineMutationQueued`) can show a queued notice, and flushes via `replayConsumerOfflineQueue` on successful responses and the window `online` event (dispatches `consumer:offline-queue-changed` so `ConsumerOfflineBanner` can show syncing). Specs: `consumer-api-offline.util.spec.ts` (`e2e-bug.16-*`). Original: ~~Traced end-to-end: `tryQueueConsumerOfflineAxiosError()` (`consumer-api-offline.util.ts:47-63`) is the only function that would catch a failed mutation and queue it for later replay — but it is referenced **nowhere** in the actual application source, only in its own spec file (`consumer-api-offline.util.spec.ts`). Confirmed the real HTTP client (`services/public-api.ts:34`, `axios.create({...})`) registers **zero** request/response interceptors — there is no code path anywhere that could ever call `tryQueueConsumerOfflineAxiosError` on a real network failure. Same story for the write side (`enqueueConsumerOfflineMutation`/`enqueueMutation` are only called from within this same dead module) and the read/replay side (`shouldReplayConsumerOfflineQueue`, meant to trigger re-sending queued mutations once back online, has zero call sites anywhere, including its own spec). The one part that *does* work: `ConsumerOfflineBanner.tsx` correctly shows a "you're offline" banner via the browser's native `online`/`offline` events and a "viewing cached data" banner — but its "N items syncing" banner state can never actually appear, because nothing can ever get added to the queue it reads from (`loadQueue().length` will always be `0`). Net effect: if a booking/cancel/reschedule/etc. request fails mid-flow due to a real network drop, the customer gets whatever raw error the calling code happens to show (per **e2e-bug.15**'s pattern) — not graceful offline queueing, despite there being a fully-built, tested subsystem sitting unused in the codebase for exactly this purpose. **Fix direction:** add a response interceptor to the `axios.create()` instance in `public-api.ts` that calls `tryQueueConsumerOfflineAxiosError` on every rejected mutating request, and wire an `online` event listener (probably alongside the existing one in `ConsumerOfflineBanner`) to actually replay/flush the queue via `shouldReplayConsumerOfflineQueue`.~~

For a real native consumer-app build this would be worse: the customer would be dumped on a generic web page with no way back into their native app (consistent with this session's earlier finding that the deep-link router and `consumer-checkout-return.util.ts` have no native-scheme pattern for single-service checkout, only a web one). **Fix direction:** thread a `returnApp`/`clientOrigin` parameter through the checkout-creation call chain (from the consumer-app's own requests) and branch the success/cancel URL construction accordingly, or give the consumer-app its own dedicated `CONSUMER_APP_URL` config distinct from `FRONTEND_URL`.~~

### consumer-app-api-sweep.1 — Direct API sweep of all 91 consumer-app endpoints, module by module

Per explicit user request ("let's have a plan to test every single module separately every single api call... consumer app api calls all"): enumerated every exported function in `consumer-app/src/services/public-api.ts` (91 functions, the app's entire HTTP surface — confirmed no other file makes HTTP calls), grouped into 20 modules, and hit each one directly via `curl` (with the same forged customer JWT, re-authorized after a token expiry) rather than through the UI — this pass is about endpoint/contract correctness, not UX (already covered by `consumer-app-e2e-bugs.1`). Happy path + realistic error cases (bad IDs, missing fields, business-rule violations, wrong auth) tested per endpoint. All 20 modules covered; results below.

**P0 — breaks a mainstream, everyday feature for every user**

- [x] **api-bug.1 — Rescheduling ANY booking crashes with a 500, both for signed-in customers and guests via manage-link.** **Fixed:** `BookingService.resolvePhiAuditActor` now treats `customer:<uuid>` actors (from `PublicCustomerBookingService.actorUserId`) as `{ role: 'customer', userId: null }` instead of calling `BusinessService.ensureMember` with a non-UUID string that Postgres rejects. Non-UUID actors fall back to `{ role: 'public', userId: null }`. Specs: `booking.service.multi-service.spec.ts` (`api-bug.1`), `booking-phi-compliance.integration.spec.ts` (`api-bug.1`). Original: ~~`POST .../reschedule` and manage-token reschedule 500 with `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "customer:…"` because `update()` always called `resolvePhiAuditActor` → `ensureMember` on the synthetic actor; cancel was fine (no PHI actor resolve); package-visit reschedule uses `rescheduleSameVisitBlock` and was already OK.~~
- [x] **api-bug.2 — `bookPublicPackage` previously bypassed multi-service max-duration while discovery enforced it (inconsistent).** **Superseded by e2e-bug.107 policy:** curated packages intentionally skip `maxDurationMinutes` on **both** discovery (`resolvePackageBlockContext` / suggest / slots) and `bookPackage` via `{ skipDurationCap: true }` — ad hoc multi-service carts still enforce the cap. Spec: `public-booking-package.spec.ts` (`e2e-bug.107`). Original inconsistency (discover reject / book accept) is closed by exempting packages end-to-end rather than rejecting both.
- [x] **api-bug.4 — `createBooking` double-books the same employee under a genuine race: two simultaneous requests for the identical service+employee+startTime both succeed with `201`.** **Fixed:** `BookingService.create()` now claims micro-slots via `claimSlotsInWindowForUpdate` (SELECT … FOR UPDATE on every slot in the window, then increment capacity) and always re-checks overlapping active bookings under `pessimistic_write` *inside* the same transaction — so the second concurrent create blocks on the row lock and then 409s instead of both inserting. Reschedule’s `findSlotsInRepo` also takes FOR UPDATE. Spec: `booking.service.multi-service.spec.ts` (`api-bug.4`). Original: ~~pre-transaction `findSlotsInWindow` + `validateBookingWindow` both saw “free”, then both committed confirmed bookings for the same employee/time/slot; sequential retries correctly 409’d.~~
- [x] **api-bug.5 — Concurrently cancelling the same booking twice crashes the second request with a raw, unhandled 500 instead of a clean idempotent response.** **Fixed:** (1) `cancelBookingInternal` returns the already-cancelled booking as a no-op (no re-cancel / re-notify / refund). (2) `NotificationsService.saveNotificationLog` treats Postgres unique violations on `(booking_id, kind, channel)` as "already logged" so concurrent cancel notifications cannot 500 with a leaked constraint name. Specs: `postgres-error.util.spec.ts`, `notification-log-save.spec.ts`, `public-customer-booking.service.spec.ts` (`api-bug.5`). Original: ~~two simultaneous manage/cancel both passed the pre-check, both wrote cancellation notification logs, second hit `IDX_f60ed9c21a25fdc91a8d092d2b` as an unhandled 500.~~
- [x] **api-bug.6 (minor, incidental) — `createBooking` returns a `manageToken` in its JSON response that doesn't match what's actually persisted, under the same race as api-bug.4.** **Fixed:** (1) `BookingService.create` stamps `metadata.manageToken` atomically with the booking row. (2) `ensureBookingManageToken` now runs inside a transaction with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, so concurrent create-response + confirmation-email callers serialize and return the same persisted token instead of minting competing ones. Specs: `booking-manage-token.util.spec.ts` (`api-bug.6`). Original: ~~response `manageToken` could disagree with `metadata.manageToken` in DB after concurrent ensure/save races; guest manage link in the confirmation response then 404'd.~~
- [x] **api-bug.7 — Combining two or more services into one visit (multi-service booking or a package) forces full online prepayment for the ENTIRE combined total, completely ignoring each service's individually configured `prepaymentMode`, even when every single constituent service is explicitly configured to require no online payment at all.** Traced by comparing the single-service booking path against both "combine services into one visit" paths. Single-service (`public-booking.service.ts:3118-3157`, the real `bookSingleService`-style flow): computes `prepaymentRequired = paymentsReady && service.prepaymentMode !== PrepaymentMode.NONE` — correctly gated on that one service's own prepayment configuration, so a `prepaymentMode: 'none'` service can always be booked without online payment. Multi-service (`bookMultiService`, `public-booking.service.ts:2650-2657`) and packages (`bookPackage`, `public-booking.service.ts:2220-2225`) both instead do simply `if (paymentsReady && pricing.amountDue > 0 && !dto.markPaid) throw new BadRequestException('Online payment is required...')` — **no reference to `prepaymentMode` anywhere.** Traced the pricing side too: `resolveMultiServiceCheckoutPricing()` (`booking-payment.service.ts:494-531`) passes `prepaymentAmount: totalPrice` — the full raw sum of every selected service's price (via `previewTotals()`, `multi-service-bookings.service.ts:106-138`, which uses plain `svc.price` with zero prepayment-mode-aware adjustment) — completely bypassing `calculatePrepaymentAmount()`/`requiresPrepayment()`, the helpers that correctly do this per-service math for the single-service path. **Reproduced live** (this business, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, has all 15 active services set to `prepaymentMode: 'none'` — confirmed via DB — so Stripe Connect readiness was the only missing precondition; temporarily set a fake `settings.integrations.stripe.connectAccountId` to flip `isConnectReady()` true, a reversible local-only DB edit, reverted immediately after): `POST /public/:slug/bookings` for one `prepaymentMode: 'none'` service (Neck Massage, $40) with no `markPaid` succeeded cleanly with `201 confirmed`, no payment friction — correct. `POST /public/:slug/multi-service/book` for **two services from that exact same all-`none` catalog** (Neck Massage + facemassage), same business, same missing `markPaid`, was rejected outright: `{"statusCode":400,"message":"Online payment is required for this booking. Complete payment at checkout."}` — a direct contradiction of both services' own configured policy, and a stark behavioral divergence from the single-service booking of the identical service moments earlier. Test booking cancelled and the fake Stripe Connect config fully reverted afterward. **Practical impact, both directions:** (1) a business that intentionally marks every service "no online prepayment" (pay in person) — exactly this business's real configuration — cannot let a customer book *any* multi-service visit or package at all once Stripe Connect is configured, even though not one of the selected services was ever supposed to require it; (2) more subtly, a business that mixes `prepaymentMode: 'none'` services with `'deposit'`/`'full'` ones would have the "none" service's price silently folded into the same forced-online-payment total as the ones that legitimately require it, since `totalPrice`/`prepaymentAmount` sums every line's full price with no per-line distinction — the customer ends up prepaying 100% of the combined visit online regardless of what any individual line was configured to need. **Fix direction:** compute prepayment requirement/amount per line in both `resolveMultiServiceCheckoutPricing`/`bookMultiService` and the equivalent package path — sum `calculatePrepaymentAmount(service)` across only the lines that actually require it (mirroring the single-service helper), and only throw "online payment required" when that per-line-aware sum is `> 0`, not whenever the raw combined `totalPrice` is nonzero.

**P2 — data/UX quality**

- [x] **api-bug.3 — `GET /public/:slug/providers/:employeeId/reviews` 500s with a leaked raw Postgres error for a non-UUID `employeeId`, instead of a clean 400.** `{"statusCode":500,"message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"nonexistent-emp-id\""}"`. Missing input validation on the path param before it reaches the query builder — the same class of issue as **api-bug.1**, but triggered by user-supplied input rather than internal server logic. Low real-world impact (a UI never sends a malformed employee ID; only a direct API caller would hit this), but it's a real crash + minor information disclosure (reveals column type/DB engine) worth a quick `IsUUID` validation guard.

**Confirmed clean across the sweep (no issues found):** discovery/profile (M1, all 6 endpoints + correct 404 on bad slug), auth (M2, clean 401/400 error shapes), single-service booking (M4 — correct date-format/missing-field validation and a correct `409` on double-booking the same slot+employee), multi-service booking (M5, all validations correct including a clean rejection for an unknown service ID), subscriptions (M7, idempotent re-cancel, correct null response for no active subscription), rewards/referral/loyalty (M11 — correct self-referral and invalid-code detection, rate-limited share-reward claims), account settings (M12 — correct locale allowlist validation; `deletePublicCustomerData` intentionally **not** exercised, permanent deletion, out of scope per safety policy), clinic vertical (M13, correctly 403s — this business isn't a clinic vertical type), pre-visit intake (M14, correctly gated — not a lab-test service), waitlist (M15 — full join/status/leave cycle works correctly end-to-end, reconfirming **e2e-bug.12** is purely a frontend-wiring gap, not a backend one), checkout recommendations (M16), push notifications (M18), support tickets (M19, correctly reports Zendesk not configured for this business), analytics ingestion (M20, correctly validates/allowlist-filters event payloads). Gift-card endpoints (M10) confirmed the backend itself correctly validates `purchaseEnabled` server-side with a clean message — the misleading UI message for this state is **e2e-bug.9** (frontend-only). One minor non-bug inconsistency noted: `fetchNearestBookableSlot` returns `200 {data: null}` for a nonexistent `serviceId` rather than a `404` like most other by-ID lookups in this API — harmless, just inconsistent.

**Auth/IDOR boundary sweep — executed, no vulnerability found (all 8 sub-cases pass).** Minted a fresh customer JWT for Customer A (`11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111`) on business `09ac3b07-6c07-4976-8684-324fce4d4296` (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`), then hit every mutating ID-taking endpoint with Customer A's token against real resource IDs belonging to a different customer, "Gevorg Gasparyan" (`efbe35c2-a9e2-4810-8823-70ef8e02b700`, 34 real bookings on this business). Two resource kinds this customer didn't already have (an active subscription, a gift-card order) were backfilled as plain SQL test fixtures tied to their `customer_id`/`purchaser_customer_id`, exercised, then deleted after the test. Results, all correctly scoped:
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/cancel` (plain booking) → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/reschedule` (plain booking) → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/running-late` → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/review` (on a `completed` booking) → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/package/cancel` (package-linked booking) → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/package/reschedule` (package-linked booking, correct `{lines:[{bookingId,startTime}]}` shape) → `404 Booking not found`
  - `POST /me/subscriptions/:id/cancel` → `404 Subscription not found`
  - `POST /gift-cards/orders/:id/cancel-request` → `404 Gift card order not found`

  Every one of these endpoints scopes its lookup by the authenticated customer's own ID before ever reaching the resource, so a mismatched ID reads as "doesn't exist" rather than "exists but isn't yours" — the correct, information-minimal behavior (no leak of "this ID is valid but not yours"). No IDOR here. Note: none of these hit **api-bug.1**'s reschedule crash, because the ownership check 404s before the code path that crashes is ever reached — so this sweep doesn't confirm or refute whether `rescheduleCustomerPackageVisit` crashes the same way api-bug.1 does *for the owning customer* (still open, see the `e2e-test-plan.full` checklist item on this).

**Cross-business token reuse sweep — executed, no vulnerability found, but one design inconsistency worth flagging.** Reused Customer A's token (minted with `businessId` = `09ac3b07-...` / `gevgas-operations-7c299253`) against the only other real business in seed data, `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8` (`66aa9d76-dc83-44b5-86c4-78980eefa43d`), which has its own distinct customers and bookings. Root cause understood via source read first: `PublicCustomerJwtStrategy.validate()` (`public-customer-jwt.strategy.ts:23-39`) only checks that the token's `sub`+`businessId` pair is internally consistent (customer really belongs to that business) — it never compares the token's `businessId` to whatever business the URL `:slug` resolves to. Authorization instead happens per-endpoint, by re-deriving the business from the URL slug and re-scoping every lookup to `(businessId-from-slug, customerId-from-token)`. Tested 4 representative cases:
  - `GET /me/bookings` (business B's URL, business-A token) → `401 Customer session expired` — `getCustomerById(businessB.id, customerA.id)` correctly finds no such customer, safe.
  - `POST /me/bookings/:id/cancel` on business B's real booking (owned by a real business-B customer) → `404 Booking not found` — same pattern, safe.
  - `GET /me/clinic-lab-booking-requests` (one of a handful of endpoints with an explicit manual guard) → `403 Customer session does not match this business` — cleanest of all, an explicit, purpose-built check (`public-booking.controller.ts:737,757,778,800,822,845`).
  - `GET /me/data` (`exportMyData`) → **`200`**, but returned Customer A's own business-A data, not business B's — because this endpoint (and 4 siblings: `deleteMyData`, and all 3 `me/push/*` endpoints) don't declare a `:slug` param at all and resolve business purely from `user.businessId` in the token (`public-booking.controller.ts:1249-1293, 1361-1377`). The URL's business slug is silently ignored for these 5 endpoints — not a leak (you always get/mutate only your own true business's data), but a real inconsistency: hitting `/public/pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8/me/data` with a `gevgas-operations` token silently operates on the `gevgas-operations` account with no error, when every sibling endpoint would 401/403/404 on the same mismatch. Confirmed by code read only (not executed, since it's a permanent-delete endpoint, out of scope per safety policy): `deleteMyData` has the identical slug-less pattern — worth fixing for consistency/defense-in-depth even though no live vulnerability was demonstrated (a valid token is already scoped to one business; the only way to hit this is deliberately typing a different business's slug in the URL while already authenticated as that business's own customer).
  - **Fix direction:** either add `@Param('slug')` + the same `businessService.findBySlug` + `user.businessId !== business.id` guard already used by the 6 clinic endpoints to these 5 endpoints, for consistency; or, more robustly, move the businessId/slug cross-check into `PublicCustomerAuthGuard` itself so every endpoint gets it uniformly instead of it being copy-pasted per-controller-method.

**Tampered/expired JWT handling — executed, no vulnerability found, clean on both surfaces.** Both auth surfaces (`PublicCustomerJwtStrategy` for customers, `JwtStrategy` for dashboard/owner) are built on `passport-jwt`'s standard `ExtractJwt.fromAuthHeaderAsBearerToken()` + `secretOrKey`, which delegates to `jsonwebtoken`'s `verify()` — signature and `exp` are checked before the strategy's own `validate()` ever runs, and neither strategy passes `ignoreExpiration`. Tested 4 cases directly against real protected endpoints:
  - Customer token, past `exp` (a token that had organically expired earlier in this session) → `GET /public/gevgas-operations-7c299253/me/bookings` → `401 Unauthorized`.
  - Customer token, tampered signature (valid, unexpired token with its signature segment reversed) → same endpoint → `401 Unauthorized`.
  - Owner token, past `exp` → `GET /businesses/my` → `401 Unauthorized`.
  - Owner token, tampered signature (fresh valid owner token, signature reversed) → same endpoint → `401 Unauthorized`.

**Concurrency sweep — executed, 2 real bugs found (createBooking double-books; concurrent cancel crashes), plus one incidental related bug and one race-prone-but-passed case.** Fired genuinely simultaneous (backgrounded, `wait`-joined) request pairs at 5 operations:
  - `createBooking` (identical service+employee+startTime) → **both requests succeeded, 2 confirmed bookings created for the same employee/time/slot** — see **api-bug.4** above (double-booking race) and **api-bug.6** (a related manage-token mismatch surfaced by the same race).
  - `cancelCustomerBooking`-equivalent (`bookings/manage/cancel`, same bookingId+token, fired twice) → first cancelled cleanly, **second crashed with an unhandled 500** — see **api-bug.5** above (notification-log unique-constraint collision, not caught).
  - `claimReferralCode` (same code, same claiming customer, fired twice) → **passed**: exactly one request returned `attached: true`, the other cleanly returned `attached: false, reason: already_attached`. No double-attach, no crash. Note: `ReferralProgramService.claimReferralCode` (`referral-program.service.ts:102-148`) is still a plain read-then-write (`findOne` the referee, check `readReferredByCustomerId`, later `customerRepo.save()`) with no transaction or row lock — this trial resolved correctly, but the code shape doesn't structurally guarantee that under different timing/load, so it's flagged as a lower-confidence "passed empirically, not provably race-free" result rather than a clean bill of health.
  - `claimPublicGiftCard` (same code, fired twice) → **not meaningfully exercised**: the only gift cards seeded on this business are `cardType: 'monetary'`, which `GiftCardClaimService.assertClaimable` rejects outright ("redeemed at booking checkout") before reaching the claim logic — both concurrent requests cleanly 400'd identically, no crash. `GiftCardClaimService.claimCard`/`markClaimed`/`markLinked` (`gift-card-claim.service.ts:40-153`) has the identical read-then-write shape as the referral-code path (`findOne` → later `save()`, no lock) for the `service`/`bundle`/`package`/`subscription` card types, which this business has none of — flagged as an untested code-review risk of the same shape as the (passing) referral case, not a confirmed bug.
  - `joinMyWaitlist` (two different service params, fired simultaneously) → **passed, by design**: this endpoint always unconditionally overwrites the customer's single `metadata.waitlistRequest` (no "first join wins" invariant exists — the feature intentionally supports switching what you're waitlisted for). Both requests succeeded, final state was a clean last-write-wins with no corruption or partial state.

  **Net: the concurrency sweep found the two most severe confirmed bugs of this entire security-testing pass (api-bug.4, api-bug.5) — both stem from the same general pattern (read-then-write availability/idempotency checks executed outside any transaction or row lock), and both are real production risks under ordinary concurrent load, not just adversarial timing.**

  All 4 return the generic Nest/passport `401 {"statusCode":401,"message":"Unauthorized"}` shape — no stack trace, no crash, no distinction leaked between "expired" vs. "bad signature" vs. "malformed" (passport's default `AuthGuard` unauthorized response supersedes any custom logic in `validate()` for these failure modes, since `validate()` is never reached). No bypass, no information disclosure, no crash. Clean.

### e2e-test-plan.full — Complete e2e test plan across the whole platform (planning only, not yet executed)

Per explicit user request ("plan 100% e2e cases then we will think about execution"). Inventoried the repo's actual app structure — it's larger than the "3 apps" framing used so far. Confirmed 4 top-level app codebases exist; one (`clinic-app`, package name `pollin-web`) is an **unrelated project** — not referenced in `docker-compose.yml` or `README.md`, has its own separate Cypress suite, different naming/tooling conventions — **excluded from this plan**. The other 3 are all genuinely part of this platform:

1. **`consumer-app`** (Ionic/Capacitor, native mobile) — the app tested in `consumer-app-e2e-bugs.1` and `consumer-app-api-sweep.1`.
2. **`frontend`** (Next.js, web) — bundles **three distinct surfaces in one codebase**: the staff/admin dashboard (`/(dashboard)/dashboard/*`, 23 pages), a **second, separate implementation** of the consumer booking flow (`/book/[slug]/*`, 20 pages, its own 1496-line `lib/public-api.ts` — likely to have *different* bugs than `consumer-app` despite serving the same purpose, since it's not shared code), and a web provider view (`/provider/*`, 5 pages), plus auth pages and misc marketing/embed pages.
3. **`provider-app`** (Ionic/Capacitor, native mobile) — the individual staff/provider's own app (calendar, schedule, patient chart, lab tasks), 16 pages, never tested this session.

**Planning note on methodology:** `consumer-app`'s API surface was small enough (91 calls, one file) to sweep exhaustively by endpoint before touching UI. `frontend` and `provider-app` don't centralize their API calls the same way (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` and `provider-app/src/services/api.ts` are both thin shared axios setup, not endpoint catalogs — their calls are scattered per-page/hook), so for those two, **page/flow is the practical planning unit**; a proper endpoint inventory would be the first execution step, not something plannable up front without opening ~70 more files.

No IDOR found.
