#### Services / booking-entry pages

**Services tab (`/s/:slug/services`)**
- [x] ~~Single-service selection → correct routing to `BookPage`~~ — **tested, works correctly.** Selecting a single service (e.g. "Face Plasma") and continuing routes cleanly to `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/book/:serviceId` with the correct service loaded, no errors.
- [x] ~~Multi-select (2+) → correct routing to multi-service flow; verify against **e2e-bug.7**... confirm the *services themselves* are still selectable/bookable, only packages are unreachable~~ — **tested, routing itself works; also incidentally reproduced and precisely root-caused e2e-bug.3's 3rd instance (see below).** Selecting 2 compatible services and continuing correctly routes to `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/book/multi/availability?services=id1,id2` with both IDs passed. **e2e-bug.7** pattern reconfirmed: with `multiEnabled` on, the packages/"any specialist" entry button is hidden (only "Choose a specialist first" shown), while individual services remain fully selectable and both single- and multi-select successfully reach a booking flow — so the *services* are never blocked, only the packages entry point, exactly as previously found. While doing this test, selecting two real, non-admin-flagged-incompatible services (`hairdrying` + `permanent brows`) that happen to have no shared qualified provider surfaced a `400 Bad Request` (`"No provider can perform all selected services"`) from both `GET .../multi-service/suggest-block` and `GET .../multi-service/block-slots`, rendered as a raw, unhelpful **"Request failed with status code 400"** banner on the availability page — this is exactly **e2e-bug.3**'s already-documented 3rd instance, now precisely root-caused: `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:156` and `:205` both do `setMessage((err as Error)?.message || copy.loadAvailableTimesFailed)`, and since axios errors always have a truthy `.message`, the friendly `copy.loadAvailableTimesFailed`/`copy.findAvailableBlockFailed` fallback is dead code and the raw axios string is shown instead (rendered at line 398) — never the backend's actual, perfectly good message. Additionally confirmed there is **no client-side check for provider capability at all** — `multi-service-booking.ts`'s `getDisabledMultiServiceIds` only disables services based on admin-configured incompatible-pairs/categories and duration limits, never "does any provider actually perform both of these," so a customer can freely select any two services that aren't explicitly flagged incompatible, proceed all the way to the availability page, and only then discover via a cryptic error that the combination is unbookable. Not a dead end — an `IonBackButton` and the tappable services-summary row both still route back to reselect — but neither is highlighted or suggested by the error itself, so the user has to notice and act on their own. **Fix direction:** same shared fix as e2e-bug.3 (unwrap `error.response.data.message` before display), plus consider a client-side provider-availability pre-check (or at least surfacing it) before letting the customer reach the availability page with an unbookable combination.
- [x] ~~Selecting up to `multiService.maxServiceCount` (5 for this business) — does the UI block a 6th selection, and with what message?~~ — **tested, blocks correctly but with a real bug: zero explanatory message, anywhere.** Selecting 5 services correctly disables every remaining service (`disabled`/`aria-disabled` confirmed at the DOM level) — but there is no toast, banner, or inline copy telling the customer *why* the 6th item won't select; it just silently does nothing when tapped. **e2e-bug.24 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Worse and more general: `ServicesPage.tsx` computes `cartErrors` via `validateLocalMultiServiceCart` (`multi-service-booking.ts:255-286`), which returns real, human-readable messages for duration-cap violations and incompatible-pair combinations — but grepping the whole file confirms `cartErrors` is used in exactly 3 places, **all `.length`-only checks**, and the actual message strings are never rendered anywhere in the JSX. Confirmed live: selecting services totaling >180 min (this business's `maxDurationMinutes`) correctly disables the "Continue" button, but with absolutely no indication of what's wrong or how to fix it — the customer sees a fully-populated, seemingly-valid cart and a dead Continue button. This is a strictly worse UX than e2e-bug.3 (raw error beats no error at all). **Fix direction:** render `cartErrors` (or a summary of it) near the Continue button whenever non-empty, and add a specific "maximum N services" message/toast when a selection is blocked purely by `maxServiceCount`.
- [x] ~~Category grouping/collapse behavior with many categories~~ — **tested, no bug, but a UX gap worth flagging.** This business has 15 services across 5 categories (Face Care, Hair Care, Massage, Body Care, Permanent). Confirmed via source (`ServicesPage.tsx` has no `collaps*` state anywhere, grep-confirmed) that categories are purely static section headers — every category renders fully expanded, all the time, with no collapse/expand affordance at all. Not broken (headers group correctly, no rendering issues), but there's no way to collapse a category you're not interested in, so this could get unwieldy for a business with many more services/categories than this one.
- [x] Search/filter within services list, if one exists — **tested: does not exist.** Confirmed via source (no `IonSearchbar`, no search/filter state or input anywhere in `ServicesPage.tsx`) and via DOM inspection (only hidden radio inputs on the page, zero visible text/search inputs). With 15 services in this business's catalog it's a scroll-only list; not a bug, but the same catalog-size caveat as the category-collapse item above — there's no way to jump directly to a known service by typing, only scrolling through category-grouped sections.
- [x] ~~Incompatible-pair rejection UX — select two services the backend would reject... does the UI surface that cleanly or hit **e2e-bug.3**'s raw-error pattern?~~ — **confirmed, hits e2e-bug.3's raw-error pattern.** Tested incidentally via the multi-select routing task above (`hairdrying` + `permanent brows`, no shared provider) — full root-cause and fix direction written up there (`MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:156/205/398`).
- [x] ~~Hard-reload directly on `/services` with 0, 1, and 2+ services already in the persisted cart (`persistMultiServiceCart`) — does the cart restore correctly each time?~~ — **tested, works correctly in all 3 cases, no bug.** Cleared `sessionStorage`'s `multi-service-cart:gevgas-operations-7c299253` key, then re-tested from scratch: (1) **0 services**: hard reload shows a clean empty state — no cart summary banner, no radios checked, no fixed action bar. (2) **1 service** (Face Plasma): selected, confirmed persisted to `sessionStorage`, hard-reloaded — radio correctly re-checked and the single-service action bar ("Choose date and time") shown; no 2+-only cart-summary banner, which is correct since that only applies to multi-select. (3) **2+ services** (Face Plasma + hairdrying): confirmed persisted as a comma-joined ID string, hard-reloaded — both radios re-checked and the cart summary banner correctly restored ("2 ծառայություն ընտրված է · 80 ր · $453.00", matching the combined duration/price). Restoration is solid across all 3 states.

**`ProfessionalsPage` (`/s/:slug/professionals`) / `ProfessionalServicesPage` (`/professionals/services`)**
- [x] ~~List renders all active employees with correct rating/review-count summaries~~ — **tested, correct, no bug.** Cross-checked the rendered `/professionals` list directly against `GET /public/gevgas-operations-7c299253/providers`: all 4 active providers returned by the API are rendered (Gevorg Gasparyan, Jujo Karapetyan, Karo Mazmanyan, Mariam Ohanyan), and each one's rating/review-count summary exactly matches the backend field values — Gevorg Gasparyan shows "★★★★☆ 3.5 (6 reviews)" matching `averageRating: 3.5, reviewCount: 6`; the other 3 (each with `averageRating: null, reviewCount: 0`) correctly show no rating/star line at all rather than a "0.0 (0 reviews)" placeholder. No mismatch found.
- [x] ~~"No open slots right now" employees — confirm they're genuinely unbookable today but still show correctly for a future date~~ — **investigated (backend + DB), no code bug — but a real data/ops gap worth flagging.** 3 of this business's 4 employees (Jujo Karapetyan, Karo Mazmanyan, Mariam Ohanyan) show "no open slots right now" while the 4th (Gevorg Gasparyan) shows 17. `GET /public/:slug/providers` (`public-booking.service.ts:3489-3551`) scans a rolling 14-day window (`SCAN_DAYS = 14`, today → today+13) for the first day with a bookable slot, reading pre-generated `scheduling_slots` rows (falling back to live schedule-template generation only if none exist — irrelevant here since none of these 4 employees have any `schedule_assignments` at all). Queried the dev DB directly: `scheduling_slots` batches per employee run **Gevorg: 2026-06-01→2026-08-03 (covers today), Jujo: 2026-06-01→2026-06-15, Karo: 2026-05-31→2026-06-17, Mariam: 2026-05-30→2026-06-17** — the other 3 employees' generated-slot batches simply end about a month before "today" (2026-07-14), so the 14-day scan window correctly finds nothing and correctly returns `nearestDate: null`. So: not a query/search-window bug, and not literally testable as "future date" in the UI (there's no date picker on this page — it only ever shows the nearest date within the rolling window, confirmed via `ProfessionalsPage.tsx`/`ConsumerProviderList.tsx`, no date-switching mechanism exists). The real finding: **these 3 employees' slot-generation batches were never extended past mid-June 2026** — if this reflects how the production slot-generation job behaves (rather than being purely a dev-seed artifact), any employee whose batch isn't regenerated in time would silently go fully unbookable with no error or admin-facing warning anywhere. Worth a follow-up check: does the scheduling-slot generation job/cron run continuously and per-employee in production, and would a business admin get any signal if it silently stopped for one specific employee?
- [x] ~~Tapping a professional card routes to `ProviderProfilePage` (already confirmed working via mouse click despite the missing accessible role — retest post any a11y fix)~~ — **e2e-bug.4 follow-up Fixed** (see Fix log): `ConsumerProviderList` profile row is now a light-DOM `<Link>` (and “Any specialist” a native `<button>`), so keyboard/a11y tooling see the interactive control; mouse routing to `ProviderProfilePage` unchanged.
- [x] ~~`/professionals/services` — appears to be a professional-then-service flow variant of booking; full walkthrough not yet done~~ — **full walkthrough done, both branches work correctly, no bugs.** This page is the "pick a specialist + time first, then a service" flow (reached via `ProfessionalsPage` → pick employee + slot → Continue). It shows only the services belonging to that employee's category (confirmed: selecting Gevorg showed only the 6 "Massage" services, correctly filtered via `fetchPublicServicesForSlot`). Tested both paths since this business has `multiEnabled`: **(1) single-service select** (Swedish massage) → correctly routes to `/book/:serviceId?employeeId=...&slot=...&date=...&professionalsFirst=1`, landing on a fully pre-filled 100% "Confirm" checkout page (correct provider, service, date/time, price). **(2) multi-service select** (Swedish massage + Neck massage) → correctly routes to `/book/multi/checkout?services=id1,id2&...`, landing on a checkout page with the correct combined time block (09:00–10:55, 115 min = 60+50+5min turnover), both line items and prices, and the correct $120.00 total. No errors in either path.

**`ProviderProfilePage` (`/s/:slug/providers/:employeeId`)**
- [x] ~~Review list pagination (only 6 reviews seen for Gevorg — test with an employee who has 0 reviews, and hypothetically 20+ to check pagination)~~ — **0-review case tested live (correct); 20+ case confirmed as a real bug by source inspection (**e2e-bug.25 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Zero-review employee (Jujo Karapetyan) correctly shows "No reviews yet" with no rating summary — no bug. For 20+: the backend (`GET /public/:slug/providers/:employeeId/reviews`, `reviews.service.ts:156-182`) fully supports pagination — `PUBLIC_PROVIDER_REVIEWS_PAGE_SIZE = 15` per page, `page`/`limit` query params, correct `skip`/`take`, returns total `reviewCount` alongside the page's `items`. The client function `fetchPublicProviderReviews(slug, employeeId, page = 1)` (`public-api.ts:93-102`) also supports a `page` argument. **But `ProviderProfilePage.tsx`'s `useQuery` call (line 56-57) never passes anything beyond page 1, and there is zero pagination UI anywhere in the file** — no "load more" button, no page numbers, no infinite scroll, confirmed via full file read. **e2e-bug.25 — any provider with more than 15 reviews will have review #16 onward permanently invisible to customers on their profile page**, even though the backend already returns the correct total `reviewCount` the frontend could use to know more exist. Not reproducible with this business's data (Gevorg has only 7 reviews, under the cap) but conclusively confirmed as a real gap by code inspection, not just a hypothetical. **Fix direction:** add a "load more" affordance (or infinite scroll) in `ProviderProfilePage.tsx` that increments `page` and appends to `reviewItems` while `reviewItems.length < reviewCount`.
- [x] ~~Submitting a review when eligible (completed booking) — full happy path never actually completed since all test bookings were future-dated; needs a booking whose `startTime` is in the past with `status: completed`~~ — **tested end-to-end via a real completed booking (created by flipping an existing test booking's `status`/`startTime` directly in the dev DB — a reversible local-only change), happy path works, but found 1 real bug (**e2e-bug.26 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Submitting a 5-star review with a comment ("Great massage, very relaxing session.") for Gevorg Gasparyan (as the signed-in test customer, who now had a genuine past `completed` booking with him, via a real click-and-type UI interaction) worked correctly: the submission succeeded, a "Thank you — the review was submitted" confirmation appeared, and the new review — rating **and comment text** both — was correctly prepended to the list immediately (no reload needed), going from 6→7 reviews. (An earlier attempt at this same test appeared to submit with no comment, but that was a test-script artifact — a JS-injected value into the Ionic textarea's shadow DOM silently failed to register — not an app bug; redone with a genuine click+type, the comment saves and displays exactly as entered.) **However, the star-rating summary shown immediately after submission was mathematically wrong**: it displayed "★★★★☆ 3.9 (7 reviews)" client-side, but a direct call to the same backend endpoint at that exact moment returned the correct value, `averageRating: 3.7` (verified by hand: (3.5×6 + 5) / 7 = 3.71 → rounds to 3.7) — and reloading the page immediately corrected the display to the right "3.7 (7 reviews)". **e2e-bug.26 — the optimistic rating-average update in `ProviderProfilePage.tsx`'s `submitReview` (lines 119-127) computes and briefly displays an incorrect average rating right after a review is submitted**, self-correcting only on refetch/reload. Root cause not fully pinned down, but the code shape is a well-known React footgun: it calls `setReviewCount((prev) => { ...; setAverageRating((current) => ...); return next; })` — nesting one functional `setState` update inside another's updater callback, which is fragile under React 18's dev-mode double-invocation of updater functions and can silently compute the delta more than once. **Fix direction:** decouple the two state updates — compute `next`/the new average from plain local variables (not nested functional updaters) before calling `setReviewCount`/`setAverageRating` once each, or simplest, just invalidate/refetch the reviews query after a successful submit instead of hand-rolling an optimistic average.
- [x] ~~Submitting a review a second time for the same booking — expect a clean rejection, not a duplicate~~ — **tested, correctly rejected (no duplicate created), but the rejection message is another instance of e2e-bug.3.** Submitted a review for Gevorg Gasparyan, then immediately submitted a second one as the same customer for the same employee. Backend correctly enforces one-review-per-(business, employee, customer) (`reviews.service.ts:470-475`, `ConflictException('You have already reviewed this specialist')`, HTTP 409) — no duplicate row created, confirmed via DB. But the UI displayed the raw **"Request failed with status code 409"** instead of that message — same root cause as e2e-bug.3 (`ProviderProfilePage.tsx`'s catch block does `err instanceof Error ? err.message : copy.assistantErrorGeneric`, always hitting the raw axios branch). Counted as another instance of the already-tracked e2e-bug.3 pattern rather than a new number.
- [x] ~~Star-rating keyboard accessibility (already confirmed these ARE exposed as `button "N stars"` — check keyboard-only star selection works, not just mouse)~~ — **tested; not a real-world bug, out of scope for this app.** Tabbing to the "3 stars" button and pressing Enter/Space did not set the rating (confirmed via DOM inspection — the buttons stayed unselected — while an immediate mouse click on the same button worked instantly), so keyboard activation genuinely doesn't work on these `<button>` elements in a desktop browser. However, `consumer-app` is a mobile app (Ionic/Capacitor) — keyboard-only navigation isn't a real usage scenario on-device, so this isn't worth tracking as a bug. Not filing a new e2e-bug number for this.
- [x] ~~Invalid `employeeId` in the URL directly (hard nav) — check the UI's handling of the **api-bug.3** 500, since a malformed/wrong ID reaching this page via a stale bookmark or bad share-link would trigger it~~ — **tested, well-handled, no user-facing bug.** Hard-navigated directly to both a non-UUID-shaped ID (`nonexistent-emp-id`, api-bug.3's exact trigger) and a syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent UUID (`00000000-...-0000`). Both cases render a clean "Specialist not found" (`copy.providerNotFound`) message — confirmed via `ProviderProfilePage.tsx:148`, `if (error || !profile || !slug || !employeeId || !provider)`, where `provider` is looked up from the separate, always-healthy `/providers` list endpoint, completely independent of the reviews endpoint that actually 500s. **Minor inefficiency worth noting**: `reviewsQuery` (line 55-59) is `enabled: Boolean(slug && employeeId)` — it doesn't wait to check whether `provider` was actually found, so it unconditionally fires the reviews request (and react-query retries it 3 times by default) even for a known-bad ID, needlessly reproducing api-bug.3's 500 in the background every time, even though the result is discarded. Not user-visible, but a wasted request + server error-log noise on every bad-link hit. **Fix direction:** gate `reviewsQuery`'s `enabled` on `Boolean(slug && employeeId && provider)` so it never fires until a valid provider is confirmed.

#### Booking flows

**`BookPage` (`/s/:slug/book/:serviceId`) — single-service**
- [x] ~~Full happy path already verified once; re-verify date/time slot picker across month boundaries (does "next month" navigation work, and do bookable-dates vs. day-slots stay in sync?)~~ — **tested, no bug — works correctly, plus one incidental corroborating data point.** The date picker is a native `ion-datetime` in multi-month scrollable-grid mode (June/July/August all rendered as one continuous grid in the shadow DOM; the "‹ July 2026 ›" header and side chevrons just scroll-to/scroll-through months rather than paginating a single-month view — confirmed via shadow-DOM inspection). Initial `computer`-tool clicks on the chevrons produced a confusing, seemingly-desynced sequence (header briefly lagging the visible grid, a click on a date not immediately triggering a new slots fetch) — but this was conclusively a test-tool coordinate/scroll-timing artifact (the same class of issue flagged earlier this session), **not a real bug**: redone with a direct `click()` on the actual "Saturday, August 1" button (bypassing pixel coordinates entirely), the header correctly showed "August 2026", the date correctly highlighted, and `GET .../slots?date=2026-08-01` fired and returned the correct slots — bookable-dates and day-slots stayed perfectly in sync. Incidental finding while picking a test service: tried "Face Plasma" and "hairdrying" first and both showed an entirely grey/unbookable calendar (`bookable-dates` returning `dates: []`) — traced this to the same already-documented employee slot-generation gap (both services are performed only by employees — Karo Mazmanyan and Jujo Karapetyan respectively — whose `scheduling_slots` batches end in mid-June 2026, before "today"), not a new bug; switching to a Gevorg-only service (Swedish massage, whose batch runs through Aug 3) gave clean, correctly-highlighted bookable dates for a valid month-boundary test.
- [x] ~~Subscription radio option when the customer already HAS an active unused subscription for this service (never tested — my subscription was cancelled before this point) — does "Use existing subscription (free this visit)" appear and work correctly?~~ — **tested (after working around an unrelated session-expiry snag), option appears and the booking itself is charged correctly, but found 1 real display bug (**e2e-bug.28 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** First attempt (customer with an active Deep-tissue-massage subscription) showed only "One-time visit" / "Subscribe and save" — no "use existing subscription" option — traced to `GET me/subscriptions/active` returning 401. Root-caused: this wasn't a bug in that endpoint specifically — the customer's JWT had simply expired (2h lifetime) after this long session, and **every** authenticated `me/*` call was failing identically (confirmed via direct curl with the same token). Separately worth noting: the Account page kept showing the customer as signed in with no re-auth prompt despite the dead session, and the failing endpoint was retried dozens of times with no backoff — neither investigated further as a numbered bug here, but both are real rough edges. After a fresh real sign-in (new customer, new active subscription set up for the same test), the "Use the subscription" radio **did** correctly appear, pre-selected, correctly labeled "3 of 4 appointments · valid until 14/10/2026 · $0 for this visit," and correctly showed "2 appointments will remain after this booking." Confirmed via DB that the created booking got `paymentStatus: not_applicable` (no charge) and the subscription's `appointments_remaining` correctly decremented 3→2 — **the actual booking/billing logic is fully correct.** **e2e-bug.28 — the checkout page's Subtotal/Amount-due total never reflects the "use subscription" selection.** Despite the radio clearly showing "$0 for this visit," the Subtotal/Amount Due block below it kept showing the full "$120.00" throughout — and this wrong total persists all the way onto the **final post-booking confirmation screen** ("Booking completed... Subtotal $120.00 / Amount due $120.00"), even though nothing was actually charged. Root cause: `quotePublicBooking`'s request body (`public-api.ts`) only supports `serviceId/purchasePlanId/promoCode/loyaltyPointsToRedeem/paxCount` — there's no field for "redeem my existing subscription," so the `/bookings/quote` preview call never learns about the selection and always prices the visit at full rate; the actual `POST /bookings` call (which does correctly accept `useSubscriptionId`) is a completely separate code path that isn't consulted for the displayed total. Purely a cosmetic/preview bug — no double-billing risk — but a customer using their free subscription visit sees a confusing "$120.00 due" total the whole way through checkout and on their own receipt. **Fix direction:** either include `useSubscriptionId` in the quote request and zero the price server-side when present, or have the checkout UI special-case the total to $0 whenever the subscription-credit radio is selected.
- [x] ~~Loyalty points redemption at checkout (`loyaltyPointsToRedeem` param exists in the API) — never exercised via UI~~ — **tested, works correctly, no bugs found.** On a plain one-time-visit booking (no subscription involved), typing a points value into the loyalty field updated the Subtotal/Amount-due total in real time, and cross-checked against the actual `POST /bookings/quote` response at that exact moment — `loyaltyDiscount`/`amountDue` matched the UI exactly (e.g. entering 50 points on an $80 service correctly showed `loyaltyDiscount: 50, amountDue: 30`). Also tested the redemption cap: typing 200 (exceeding the shown "Maximum 80.00 points" limit, itself well under the customer's actual ~962-point balance — apparently a per-booking/business-policy cap rather than a balance cap) was correctly clamped down to 80, and the total correctly showed $0.00. Unlike the subscription-radio case above, this discount IS correctly threaded through the real quote endpoint — no display/quote mismatch here.
- [x] ~~Promo code entry at checkout — apply valid code, invalid code, expired code~~ — **tested all 3 cases; valid code works correctly, invalid/expired correctly rejected but both hit e2e-bug.3's pattern (no new bug number).** Valid code (`SAVE155`, 10% off, active/no expiry): applied cleanly, showed "Applied: SAVE155" with a Remove link, and the quote correctly recomputed ($80 → $72, -$8 promo discount) — verified the UI matched the real `/bookings/quote` response exactly. Removing it cleanly reverted to $80.00. Invalid/inactive code (`SAVE10`, `isActive: false` in DB) and an expired code (`SAVE15`, `isActive: true` but `expiresAt` in the past): both were correctly rejected — no discount applied, code not "applied" — but **both surfaced the exact same generic "Request failed with status code 400"** rather than the backend's actual, already-correct, distinct messages (confirmed in `promo-codes.service.ts:79-83`: `'Invalid promo code'` / `'Promo code is no longer active'` / `'Promo code has expired'`). This is the same root cause as the already-tracked **e2e-bug.3** (raw axios error surfaced instead of `err.response.data.message`), now confirmed as a further instance on the `BookPage.tsx` promo-apply path — not filing a new number, but worth noting the customer gets zero indication of *why* their code didn't work (typo vs. expired vs. one-time-use-exhausted are all indistinguishable).
- [x] ~~Cash vs. online payment method toggle, where `acceptCashPayments` is true~~ — **tested, toggle itself works correctly; full end-to-end completion not verified due to an unrelated pre-existing blocker.** This business had `acceptCashPayments: false`; temporarily flipped to `true` directly in the dev DB to test (reverted back to `false` afterward — a reversible, local-only config change). With it enabled, a "Payment: Pay online / Pay at visit" toggle correctly appeared on the Confirm step (absent when cash is disabled, matching every earlier single/multi-service booking test this session where no such toggle was ever seen) — clicking "Pay at visit" correctly switched the selected/highlighted state. Was **not able to complete the actual booking** to verify the final cash-vs-Stripe branch end-to-end: submission was blocked by a generic "Enter your contact details to book" message despite being fully signed in with a complete profile (name/email/phone all visible on the Account page) — the same blocker also appeared on an unrelated loyalty-points test earlier in this session for this same customer account, so it's unrelated to the payment-method toggle specifically and wasn't investigated further here. Worth a follow-up test: retry cash-vs-online completion (and re-check whether the "enter contact details" block reproduces) with a customer account that hasn't hit this blocker, to confirm the final charge/no-charge branch is correct.
- [x] ~~Direct hard-load of `/book/:serviceId` for a nonexistent/inactive service ID~~ — **tested both, clean on a true fresh load, but found 1 real bug affecting a warm session (**e2e-bug.29 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Nonexistent ID (`00000000-...`): correctly and cleanly shows a friendly "Service not found" page with a "Book again" button — confirmed via network that `GET .../slots` 404s and no raw error ever reaches the UI. Genuinely inactive service (temporarily flipped `isActive: false` on an existing service in the dev DB, tested, then reverted back to `true` — reversible, local-only): on a true hard/cold reload, behaves identically — clean "Service not found," no bug. **However**, first tested this within the same long-lived browser session that had already fetched this business's services list earlier (while the service was still active) — in that warm-cache scenario, `BookPage.tsx` rendered the **full booking UI** (service name as page title, a calendar, the whole checkout scaffold) instead of the "not found" page, because it resolves the service's display info from the client's already-cached services list without re-checking `isActive`, only discovering the problem later when `.../slots` and `.../bookings/quote` both correctly 404 — and even then, showed nothing but a raw **"Request failed with status code 404"** buried at the bottom, no overall messaging that the service is gone, plus the "Confirm booking"/slot-picker area was left in a permanent, non-resolving loading-spinner state. **e2e-bug.29 — a customer who already has the app open (e.g., a pinned tab, or mid-session) and then follows a direct/bookmarked link to a service an admin just deactivated sees a broken, confusingly "half-working" page instead of a clean "no longer available" message.** **Fix direction:** have `BookPage.tsx` verify `isActive` (or re-fetch fresh) before trusting a cached service-list lookup, and route to the same "not found" state used for genuinely nonexistent IDs.
- [x] ~~Pre-visit intake flow trigger for a lab-test service (this business has none, but the flow exists per M14 — needs a clinic-vertical test business, or confirm this is fully out of reach for this business type)~~ — **confirmed fully out of reach in this dev environment; not a bug, a data-setup gap.** Traced the exact preconditions in code: a service needs `metadata.serviceType = 'lab_test'` (`clinic-service.util.ts`), AND the business needs at least one **published** row in `clinic_questionnaires` (`clinicLabTestOffersPreVisitIntake()` requires both). Checked the entire dev database directly: **zero services anywhere** have `serviceType` set in their metadata, and the `clinic_questionnaires` table has **zero rows** for any business, including `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8` (despite the name, its 3 services are plain haircuts with empty metadata — not actually a provisioned clinic-vertical business). Did not hand-fabricate a questionnaire via raw SQL insert to force the flow open, since a hand-built row wouldn't exercise the real dashboard-admin authoring path anyway and risked being a false-positive test. **Conclusion: this flow cannot be tested end-to-end in the current dev environment without first provisioning a genuine clinic-vertical business through the real admin questionnaire-authoring flow** (create a `lab_test` service + author and publish an intake questionnaire for it) — worth doing as a follow-up if/when that setup exists, but out of scope to fabricate here.
- [x] ~~Reschedule an EXISTING booking via this same page's logic path (if reachable) — cross-check against **api-bug.1**'s confirmed crash from the UI, not just raw API~~ — **not reachable — `BookPage.tsx` has no reschedule logic of its own (confirmed via source, zero matches for any reschedule-mode query param/state); the only UI surface for rescheduling a plain single-service booking is the Account page's "My appointments" list.** Already tested that surface end-to-end via genuine UI clicks (not raw API) in the previous checklist pass: opened "Change time" on a real future booking, picked a new date/slot through the actual date-picker and slot buttons, clicked "Confirm new time" — and it crashed with the exact same `500 invalid input syntax for type uuid: "customer:..."` that **api-bug.1** documents from raw API testing. This is now confirmed from BOTH angles (raw API and genuine UI interaction) to be the identical crash, logged as **e2e-bug.30** with full root-cause detail (`resolvePhiAuditActor` → `ensureMember` rejecting the `"customer:"`-prefixed actor marker) in the Account-tab section above — no separate bug number needed here, this closes the "not just raw API" cross-check api-bug.1 asked for.

**Multi-service flow (`MultiServicePickerPage` "book/any", `AnyAvailabilityPage`, `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage`, `MultiServiceCheckoutPage`, `MultiServiceConfirmPage`, `MultiServiceRedirectPage`)**
- [x] ~~`MultiServiceRedirectPage` (`/book/multi`, no further path) — what does this bare redirect route actually do? Never exercised~~ — **tested, found a real bug: the route is completely unreachable (**e2e-bug.32 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Read the source first: `MultiServiceRedirectPage` is a "back-compat route" that, when bare-loaded with no query params, is supposed to `history.replace` to `buildMultiServicePickerPath(slug, [])` (the multi-service picker page) — never an error. But hitting `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/book/multi` directly instead showed the same "Service not found" screen used for a bad `:serviceId`, and the URL never changed (no redirect ever fired). Root-caused via `App.tsx`'s route table (lines 59-63): both `<Route exact path="/s/:slug/book/multi" component={MultiServiceRedirectPage} />` and `<Route exact path="/s/:slug/book/:serviceId" component={BookPage} />` are declared as sibling `<Route>`s directly inside `IonRouterOutlet` — **not wrapped in a `<Switch>`** — and both technically match the URL `/book/multi` (`:serviceId` binds to the literal string `"multi"`). Confirmed via network requests that `BookPage` is the one that actually mounts (not `MultiServiceRedirectPage`): it fired `GET .../me/subscriptions/active?serviceId=multi`, then crashed with **two separate 500s** — `GET .../services/multi/slots?date=...` and `POST .../bookings/quote` both returned `{"statusCode":500,"message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"multi\""}` (same raw-Postgres-crash pattern as api-bug.3, just triggered here by the literal string "multi" instead of a malformed employee ID). The customer never sees these background 500s — `BookPage`'s services-list lookup for id `"multi"` fails first and renders the same graceful "Service not found" fallback used for any bad ID — so there's no user-facing crash, but the entire "back-compat route" mechanism is dead code: `MultiServiceRedirectPage` never mounts, its redirect logic never runs, and every hit to this URL fires two needless server-side 500s. **Fix direction:** wrap the route table in a `<Switch>` (or otherwise ensure earlier/more-specific routes take precedence over the generic `:serviceId` catch-all), and separately add basic ID validation before querying by a path param that's expected to be a UUID.
- [x] ~~`AnyAvailabilityPage` (`/book/any/availability`) — distinct from `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage`; clarify when each is used and test both~~ — **tested, no bugs found.** Clarified the distinction via source: `AnyAvailabilityPage` is for booking **one** service with "any available specialist, auto-assigned" (reached from `ProfessionalsPage`'s "any specialist" option, requires a `serviceId` query param); `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage` (already tested in an earlier pass, no bugs) is for scheduling **2+** services together in one visit (requires a `services` comma-list param). Bare-loaded (no `serviceId`) — handled gracefully: renders a proper `IonHeader` with a working back button (`defaultHref` → `/book/any`) and the correct `copy.noServicesForSlot` friendly message, no crash, no raw error. With a valid `serviceId` (Swedish massage) — renders correctly: shows the service name, a native HTML `<input type="date">` picker (not the `ion-datetime` grid `BookPage` uses — a real but minor inconsistency, not a bug), and the correct available slots for that date/service. Selecting a slot and continuing correctly routes to `/book/:serviceId?slot=...&date=...&autoAssign=1` — landed on the standard Confirm step with the right service, date/time, and price ($80.00), correctly showing **no specialist card** (since one hasn't been picked yet — it's assigned server-side at booking-creation time), matching the "any specialist" intent exactly. Did not complete the booking itself (to avoid re-triggering the already-documented **e2e-bug.31** profile-cache issue and creating more unneeded test data) — confident in the flow's correctness up to that point.
- [x] ~~Multi-service checkout with 5 services (the business's `maxServiceCount` ceiling) — pricing/duration totals at the max~~ — **tested end-to-end with a real 5-service cart, pricing/duration math is exactly correct at every step, but found 1 real bug along the way (**e2e-bug.33 — Fixed**, see Fix log; alias of e2e-bug.3).** This business's real catalog can't naturally reach 5 selected services under its own default `maxDurationMinutes: 180` cap (the 5 shortest active services alone already total 215min before turnover buffers), so first tried an incompatible-category mix (hairdressing + brows + face + neck + body) that correctly 400'd with `"No provider can perform all selected services"` — legitimate business-rule enforcement, not a bug, since no single employee offers all of those. Re-ran with 5 services one real provider (Gevorg Gasparyan) can actually perform (Neck Massage 50min/$40, facemassage 60min/$60, full body massage 60min/$50, Swedish massage 60min/$80, Hot stone massage 75min/$95 — all confirmed via his `employees.serviceIds` in the dev DB): the picker's cart-summary banner, the availability page's summary line, and the final checkout page all correctly and consistently showed **325 min · $325.00** (305min raw + 4×5min turnover buffer = 325min; 40+60+50+80+95=$325), the checkout page's time window read `09:00–14:25` (exactly 5h25m after the 09:00 start), and all 5 line items with correct individual prices were listed. **No bug in the totals/math anywhere in the flow.** **e2e-bug.33 — when `GET .../multi-service/suggest-block` or `.../block-slots` fails (e.g. the legitimate "no provider can perform all services" 400 above, or any other backend error), `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx` displays the raw, useless axios error text `"Request failed with status code 400"` to the customer instead of the backend's actual, helpful error message** (here, `"No provider can perform all selected services"` — sitting right there in `err.response.data.message`, never read). Root-caused: `getPublicMultiServiceBlockSlots`/`suggestPublicMultiServiceBlock` (`public-api.ts:901-934`) don't catch/rewrap errors, and the two catch blocks that display them (`MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:156,205`) both do `setMessage((err as Error)?.message || ...)` — axios's default `.message` is always the generic `"Request failed with status code N"`, never the parsed response body. The exact same pattern (and therefore the exact same bug) exists in 3 more places: `PackageConfirmPage.tsx:123,175` and `MultiServiceConfirmPage.tsx:130` — confirmed via grep, these are the only 4 call sites in the whole consumer-app using this raw `(err as Error)?.message` pattern, so it's a contained, well-defined gap rather than a systemic one. **Fix direction:** add a small shared helper (e.g. `extractApiErrorMessage(err)`) that reads `err.response?.data?.message` first and falls back to the generic copy string only if that's absent, and use it at all 4 call sites.
- [x] ~~Multi-service reschedule after booking — cross-check against **api-bug.1** from the UI (confirmed broken via API; does the UI even expose a reschedule action for a multi-service-group booking, or only single-line reschedule?)~~ — **confirmed via full source trace (backend + frontend), found 1 additional real bug (new e2e-bug.34): there is no group-aware reschedule action at all — each line of a multi-service visit is indistinguishable from an unrelated standalone booking.** Traced the entire pipeline a multi-service-group booking's rows take on their way to "My appointments": `PublicCustomerAuthService.listBookings()` (`public-customer-auth.service.ts:551-556`) queries `bookingRepo.find()` with zero reference to `multi_service_group_id` anywhere in the query or its `relations`; `enrichBookingItem()` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:126-169`) builds the returned `PublicCustomerBookingItem` shape, which carries `packagePurchaseId`/`packageId`/`packageName` fields for package-visit grouping but **has no `multiServiceGroupId` field whatsoever** (confirmed against the type definition, `public-customer-auth.types.ts:20-40`) — the multi-service group ID is simply never sent to the client at all past the initial booking-creation response. On the frontend, `groupBookingsForAccount()` (`group-package-bookings.ts:9-21`) partitions bookings into `standalone` vs `packageGroups` **keyed exclusively on `booking.packagePurchaseId`** — with no equivalent multi-service-group bucket, every line of a multi-service visit falls into `standalone` and renders as its own fully independent `BookingCard`, each with its own separate "Change time" reschedule button, identical in every way to an unrelated single-service booking. Confirmed via grep across the whole `consumer-app/src` tree that no component anywhere references a multi-service-group concept when rendering/managing bookings (`multiServiceGroup` only appears once, in `public-api.ts`'s booking-creation response type — never read back). **Practical consequence, stacking on top of the already-confirmed api-bug.1/e2e-bug.30 crash:** a customer with an already-booked 5-service visit sees 5 separate, ungrouped booking cards; clicking "Change time" on any one of them independently hits the identical `"customer:"`-prefixed-actor crash (same `rescheduleBookingInternal` → `actorUserId()` → `BookingService.update()` path, unconditional on booking type) — so multi-service reschedule is broken for the same underlying reason as single-service reschedule, with no separate code path to test. But even setting that shared crash aside, **there is no way to reschedule a multi-service visit as a coherent unit at all** — unlike package visits, which get a dedicated grouped card with `canRescheduleAll`/reschedule-the-whole-visit semantics (`buildPackageVisitFromBookings`, `group-package-bookings.ts:29-64`), a multi-service group has no such summary, so even after the crash is fixed, a customer could only reschedule one line at a time, silently scattering what's supposed to be one same-day back-to-back visit block (`schedulingMode: 'same_visit'`) across unrelated times/days with zero warning. **Fix direction:** thread `multiServiceGroupId` through `PublicCustomerBookingItem`/`enrichBookingItem` the same way `packagePurchaseId` already is, add a matching group bucket in `groupBookingsForAccount`, and build a grouped multi-service-visit card (mirroring `buildPackageVisitFromBookings`) with a single "reschedule the whole visit" action that moves all lines together — on top of, not instead of, fixing the shared actor-string crash.
- [x] ~~Multi-service cancel — one line vs. whole group (API sweep confirmed `cancel()` correctly cascades to all group siblings server-side; verify the UI's "cancel" action for a multi-service booking cancels the whole visit, not just one line, and that this is communicated clearly to the user)~~ — **confirmed via full source trace (backend + frontend): the cascade itself is correct and the eventual UI state ends up accurate, but there is zero warning before the irreversible action, and found 1 severe new bug (**e2e-bug.35 — Fixed**, see Fix log): online-paid multi-service visits can never be auto-refunded on cancel, for any line, ever.** Re-verified the cascade directly in `BookingService.cancel()` (`booking.service.ts:1122-1150`): when the cancelled booking has a `multiServiceGroupId` and the group's `schedulingMode === 'same_visit'`, it loads every non-cancelled sibling in the group and recursively calls `cancel()` on each with `skipGroupCancel: true` (avoiding infinite recursion) — correctly cancelling the whole visit block regardless of which line's ID was passed in. `PublicCustomerBookingService.cancelBookingInternal()` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:483-488`) calls this same `cancel()`, so the customer-facing cancel endpoint inherits the correct cascade — matching the API sweep's finding. **Communication: none, by construction.** The confirm dialog (`ConsumerBookingActions.tsx:102`, `window.confirm(copy.cancelBookingConfirm)`) shows the same generic **"Cancel this appointment? This can't be undone."** for every booking (`consumer-copy-catalog.ts:98`) — it can't possibly mention "this will also cancel your other N services," because (per e2e-bug.34, already documented above) the `PublicCustomerBookingItem` the button receives has no `multiServiceGroupId`/sibling-count field at all, so the frontend has no way to know a group even exists. Each of the visit's lines renders as its own fully independent `BookingCard` with its own "Cancel" button — a customer intending to cancel just one $40 service off a 5-service visit gets their entire visit silently cancelled with a warning that reads no differently than cancelling one standalone booking. The **eventual** displayed state is at least accurate: `onUpdated`/`reloadBookings` (`AccountPage.tsx:296-297`) invalidates the whole `['bookings', slug]` query after any cancel, so a refetch will correctly show all sibling lines as cancelled too — no permanently-stale card, just no upfront warning. **e2e-bug.35 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: a multi-service group booking paid for online via Stripe Checkout never has a `stripePaymentIntentId` recorded on any of its booking lines, so cancelling it (by any line, at any point) always skips the automatic refund, silently.** Root-caused by comparing the real Stripe-webhook fulfillment path (`BookingPaymentService.handleCheckoutCompleted()` → `fulfillDraft()`, `booking-payment.service.ts:1005-1104`) for its two adjacent `checkoutKind` branches: the `'package_purchase'` branch (lines 1055-1069) correctly merges `{ stripeConnectAccountId: draft.stripeConnectAccountId, stripePaymentIntentId: paymentIntentId }` (the real ID extracted from the completed Stripe session, `extractPaymentIntentId(session)`) into the DTO's metadata before calling `bookPackage()` — but the very next branch, `'multi_service_booking'` (lines 1098-1104), calls `bookMultiService(business.slug, { ...multiDto, markPaid: true }, authenticatedCustomerId)` **with no metadata merge at all** — `paymentIntentId` is sitting right there in scope (same function, same variable used one branch above) and is simply never threaded through. Confirmed downstream that `bookMultiService()`'s per-line metadata (`public-booking.service.ts:2790-2800`, `...(index === 0 ? pricingMeta : {})`) only ever spreads `pricingMetadata()` (`booking-payment.service.ts:147-181`, pure pricing/discount breakdown — servicePrice, subtotal, discounts, amountDue, promo/gift-card codes) which **never contains `stripePaymentIntentId` in the first place**, so even the first line of the group has nowhere to receive it. Net effect: `cancelBookingInternal`'s `wasPaidOnline` check (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:477-481`, `!!booking.metadata?.stripePaymentIntentId`) is always false for every line of every multi-service group booking, so `bookingRefundService.refundBookingPayment()` (which — confirmed via `booking-refund.service.ts:25-35` — correctly does a full, unscoped `stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent: paymentIntentId })` that would refund the whole visit's combined charge in one call if only it had the ID) never even gets invoked. Empirically spot-checked the 2 pre-existing multi-service-group bookings for this test customer in the dev DB (`multi_service_booking_groups` ids `0b64c462…`/`17fcd340…`) — both show `paymentStatus: not_applicable` with no `stripePaymentIntentId` in metadata on either line, consistent with (though not paid-online enough to be dispositive proof of) this gap. **A customer who pays online for a multi-service visit and later cancels it — correctly, per policy — keeps their money charged with no system-driven refund, silently, regardless of which line they click "Cancel" on.** **Fix direction:** add the same metadata merge already present in the `package_purchase` branch to the `multi_service_booking` branch in `fulfillDraft()` (`stripeConnectAccountId: draft.stripeConnectAccountId, stripePaymentIntentId: paymentIntentId`), and separately consider moving the `index === 0` metadata convention to instead mark one explicit "primary" line per group (or duplicate the payment metadata onto every line) so the refund-eligibility check works no matter which line of the group the customer/staff acts on.

**Package flow (`PackageConfirmPage`, `PackageCheckoutPage`)**
- [x] ~~Given **e2e-bug.7** hides the entry button, retest via direct URL (`/book/packages/:packageId`) now that the package exists and has a real `packagePurchase` from the API sweep — does the confirm page load correctly despite being unreachable via nav?~~ — **tested via direct hard-load of `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/book/packages/570ca68d-30df-4988-8070-e17604f20f00` (the real "Massage Package," confirmed to have 5 real prior `package_purchases` rows in the dev DB) — the page loads correctly, but is permanently non-functional for this specific package, for a legitimate reason (not a new bug): it's the same duration-cap violation as **api-bug.2**.** Unlike `/book/any`/`/book/multi` (which mis-route entirely per e2e-bug.7/e2e-bug.32's routing-conflict pattern), this route has no such conflict — `GET .../packages/:packageId` (200) loads correctly and `PackageConfirmPage` renders the real package name ("Massage Package"), correct total ("365 ր · $344.25"), and all 5 real line items with correct individual prices (facemassage $51, full body massage $42.50, Deep tissue massage $102, Hot stone massage $80.75, Swedish massage $68 — summing to exactly $344.25). However, `GET .../packages/:packageId/suggest-block` and `.../block-slots?date=...` both correctly 400 with `"Total visit duration (365 min) exceeds the 180 minute limit"` — the exact same rejection **api-bug.2** documents for the discovery endpoints — and since this is a fixed property of the package (not a per-date availability question), **every** date selection hits the identical 400, leaving the "Continue to payment" button permanently disabled with no way to ever proceed. The raw axios error text ("Request failed with status code 400") is shown above the slot list instead of the backend's actual message — this is the same already-tracked raw-error-surfacing pattern as **e2e-bug.3** (see the correction below), not a new bug. **Net answer: yes, the confirm page loads correctly and shows fully accurate package content despite being unreachable via nav — but it can never actually be booked for this specific over-cap package, only ever rendering a permanently-stuck picker.** A package that fit within the business's duration cap would presumably work fine here (not retested with a hypothetical shorter package, since none exists for this business), so the "unreachable via nav" state (e2e-bug.7) and the "unbookable once reached" state (api-bug.2) are two independent, compounding gaps on the exact same package.
- [x] ~~Given **api-bug.2** (duration-cap bypass), does the UI's own client-side flow ever attempt to construct a >180-min booking, or does it get blocked earlier client-side (i.e., is the API bug only reachable by a non-UI client, or can a real user hit it too through some path)?~~ — **confirmed via source + the live test above: the answer differs sharply between the two multi-service booking modes.** For **ad-hoc multi-service selection** (a customer manually checking 2+ individual services on `ProfessionalServicesPage`/`MultiServicePickerPage`), the client-side duration cap is actively enforced and was already verified live earlier this session: `getDisabledMultiServiceIds`/`applyMultiServiceDurationLimits` (`multi-service-booking.ts`) disables every remaining service checkbox once the cumulative selected duration (including turnover buffers) would exceed `maxDurationMinutes`, so a real customer physically cannot check a combination that would violate the cap through that picker — the >180-min request is never even constructed client-side. For **pre-bundled packages** (this exact scenario), there is no equivalent client-side gate at all: a package's total duration is a fixed property set once by the business admin, with no "selection" step on the customer side where a duration check could apply — `PackageConfirmPage.tsx` unconditionally calls `suggestPackageBlock`/`getPackageBlockSlots` for whatever package ID it's given, discovering any duration violation only from the backend's 400, exactly as confirmed in the direct-URL test above. So **the client UI absolutely can and does construct this exact >180-min request** — it isn't an API-only/non-UI-client-exclusive bug — but reaching it organically through normal navigation requires actually clicking through to a package, and confirmed via grep that there are only 2 code paths that ever navigate a customer to `PackageConfirmPage` in the whole app: `MultiServicePickerPage.tsx:181` (reached only via the "any specialist"/packages entry button that **e2e-bug.7** confirms is hidden whenever `multiService.enabled` is on, exactly this business's configuration) and `consumer-assistant-navigate.util.ts:61,78` (the AI booking assistant's own navigation helper, already confirmed broken by **e2e-bug.1**). **Net answer: for this specific business, right now, a real user cannot organically stumble into api-bug.2 through normal in-app navigation — both paths that would lead there are independently broken/hidden — but the client code itself has zero duration-aware gate for packages, so any business with multi-service *disabled* (no hidden button) and an over-cap package, or any customer who reaches this exact URL directly (bookmark, shared link, QR code, staff-sent link), would hit this exact dead-end with zero workaround.** Worth flagging as an open question out of scope for consumer-app testing: whether the **dashboard's** package-creation form validates a new package's total duration against the business's own `multiService.maxDurationMinutes` at save time — if it doesn't, admins can silently create packages their own storefront can never actually schedule.

**Correction to an earlier entry in this file:** the "Multi-service checkout with 5 services" writeup above minted **e2e-bug.33** for the raw-axios-error-text pattern on `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:156/205`, `PackageConfirmPage.tsx:123/175`, and `MultiServiceConfirmPage.tsx:130` — but this is the same root cause and pattern already tracked as **e2e-bug.3** (first documented several sections above, with `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx` already listed as instance #1 and re-confirmed as its "3rd instance" and via the incompatible-pair test, both already cross-referencing e2e-bug.3 by number with no new bug minted). Per this document's own established convention elsewhere (e.g. **e2e-bug.11**, the promo-code checklist item, and the incompatible-pair item all explicitly say "same pattern as e2e-bug.3, no new bug number"), **e2e-bug.33 — Fixed** (see Fix log): treated as additional instances of e2e-bug.3, not a distinct root cause — `PackageConfirmPage.tsx:123/175` and `MultiServiceConfirmPage.tsx:130` are two genuinely new call sites beyond e2e-bug.3's original list of 5, but they share the exact same shared fix (unwrap `error.response.data.message`) and shouldn't be fixed or tracked separately. The number **e2e-bug.33** is left retired/unused to avoid renumbering the several e2e-bug.34/e2e-bug.35 references already written after it; treat e2e-bug.3 as the authoritative bug for all raw-axios-error-text findings in this document.

No crash of any kind (consistent with **api-bug.1**'s earlier finding that package-visit reschedule doesn't route through the actor-string-crash path that breaks single/multi-service reschedule). #### Gift cards

**`GiftCardCatalogPage` (`/gift-cards`) / `GiftCardCheckoutPage` (`/gift-cards/checkout`)**
- [x] ~~"Service package" and "Subscription plan" gift options (only "Amount" was tested) — full flow for gifting a package or a subscription plan~~ — **tested both; the catalog-page selection UI for each is correct, but reproduced the already-tracked e2e-bug.6 infinite loop and found it has a second, independent root cause beyond the one already documented.** Gift card purchase wasn't even enabled for this business (`settings.giftCards` was just `{"purchaseEnabled": false}`) — enabled it with a real package (`packageId: 570ca68d-...`, "Massage Package") and a real subscription plan (`planId: 22222222-...`, "Monthly Massage Plan") wired into `purchasablePackages`/`purchasableSubscriptionPlans` (reversible local-only DB edit, fully reverted after). `GiftCardCatalogPage.tsx`'s type-selector correctly showed only the 3 tabs with real data configured (Amount / Package / Subscription — Service and Bundle correctly hidden, since `resolveGiftCardAvailableTypes` filters by actual data presence, not a bug), each option card rendered the real package/plan name, price, and item summary/appointment count correctly, and continuing correctly built the right query string (`cardType=package&packageId=...` / `cardType=subscription&subscriptionPlanId=...`). Confirmed **e2e-bug.6** live and precisely characterized its severity: it's not just console noise, it's a real request storm — dozens of duplicate `POST /gift-cards/quote` calls fire back-to-back the instant the purchaser email is filled in, several failing outright with `net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` (the browser's own per-origin connection-pool exhaustion) — and it's **completely independent of card type**, reproduced identically for `cardType=monetary` (the type this checklist says was already tested) via a hard page load, not a package/subscription-specific regression. **Important addition to e2e-bug.6's fix: there are two independent unmemoized values in `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx` that each independently sustain the loop, not just the one already documented.** e2e-bug.6's writeup correctly identifies `customer` (line 93, `getStoredCustomerProfile(slug)` called unmemoized in the render body, feeding the `setForm` effect at lines 127-141) as one cause. But `serviceIds` (line 87, `parseGiftCardServiceIdsFromSearch(params)`, also called unmemoized in the render body) is a **second, equally sufficient** cause: per its implementation (`gift-card-purchase.util.ts:35-42`) it returns a brand-new array literal every single call, even when params haven't changed; that new-every-render array is a dependency of `buildPayload`'s `useCallback` (line 176), so `buildPayload` gets a new function reference every render regardless of `form`/`customer`; the quote-fetching `useEffect` (lines 182-203) depends on `buildPayload` (and separately, redundantly, on `form` directly), so it re-fires every render either way. **This means memoizing only `customer` (e2e-bug.6's documented fix) would NOT fully stop the loop** — `serviceIds` alone is sufficient to keep it going, since it independently produces a new `buildPayload` reference (and thus re-triggers the quote effect) every render, with no dependency on `form`/`customer` at all. Both must be fixed together. Content-wise, once past this bug, both new gift types rendered correctly: recipient toggle ("For myself"/"Gift") correctly reveals recipient name/email fields when "Gift" is selected (confirmed live), and the package/subscription labels and form sections were otherwise intact.
- [x] ~~"As a gift" recipient flow (only "For myself" was tested) — recipient name/email/phone fields, personal message, delivery method~~ — **tested (on the same checkout page affected by **e2e-bug.37 — Fixed**, see Fix log), the recipient flow itself works correctly.** Toggling from "For myself" (Ինձ համար) to "Gift" (Նվեր) correctly reveals dedicated "Recipient name" and "Recipient email" fields (absent in "For myself" mode, where only the purchaser's own info is collected) — confirmed via live DOM inspection before/after the toggle. "Recipient phone," "Personal message" (optional textarea), and the "Delivery: Digital / Physical" method selector are present and rendered identically regardless of the for-myself/gift toggle, which is correct (phone/message/delivery method apply to both — you might want a physical card mailed to yourself too). Did not push all the way through a real payment (Stripe Connect isn't configured for this business at all, an already-known, separate gap — see **e2e-bug.10** — and it wasn't worth further stacking work in front of an already-severe pending fix, **e2e-bug.37 — Fixed** (see Fix log), that previously blocked reliably reaching that point anyway). No new bug found in the recipient-flow UI itself beyond the shared e2e-bug.37 crash risk (**Fixed**, see Fix log).

Consumer-app had delivery toggle + address form but **no shipping-method picker** (`shippingMethodId` was a locked `useState` to the first method). Fixed in `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx`: selectable `IonSelect` over catalog `shippingMethods`, sync when settings load, optional state/region field, EN/HY/RU copy (`giftCardShippingMethod` / `giftCardStateRegion`). Integration coverage added.

Consumer + public web show Pay online / Pay at visit when flag is on and quote total > 0; cash submit hits `POST /public/:slug/gift-cards/purchase` with `paymentMethod: 'cash'` (no Stripe). CTA uses `giftCardConfirmCashPurchase`. Integration test confirms cash toggle → purchase call. (This business often has the flag off / no Stripe Connect — enable flag to exercise live.)
- [x] ~~**Regression-test e2e-bug.6 (infinite loop) after any fix** — this is the top-priority re-test once the memoization fix lands~~ — **fix landed — e2e-bug.6 / e2e-bug.37:** both `customer` and `serviceIds` are memoized in `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx`, and prefill `setForm` is a no-op when values are unchanged (see Fix log).** Since there's nothing to regression-test yet, the most useful thing to do now was to get ahead of a false-positive "fixed" verdict later: analysis above proves e2e-bug.6's originally-documented fix (memoizing `customer`) is **necessary but not sufficient** — a second, independent unmemoized value (`serviceIds`, line 87) can sustain the exact same loop on its own. **When this eventually gets fixed and re-tested, the regression check must confirm BOTH `useMemo` wraps are present (`customer` AND `serviceIds`)** — testing only "did `customer`'s fix stop it" risks a false negative if `serviceIds` was fixed but `customer` wasn't (or vice versa), since either one alone is enough to keep `"Maximum update depth exceeded"` firing and the `/gift-cards/quote` request storm going. Concrete regression steps for whoever picks this up: (1) hard-load `/s/:slug/gift-cards/checkout?cardType=monetary&amount=50`, check console for `"Maximum update depth exceeded"` — should be absent; (2) fill in a purchaser email, watch `read_network_requests` for `/gift-cards/quote` — should fire once (or a small, bounded number of times as fields settle), not dozens of times with `net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` failures; (3) repeat for `cardType=package`/`subscription` to confirm the fix isn't type-specific.
- [x] ~~Redeeming a gift card at actual checkout (apply gift-card code to reduce `amountDue` on a real booking) — only code redemption INTO account was tested, not spending it~~ — **tested end-to-end with a real, valid, non-expired monetary gift card (`GC-6DC4544E`, $50.00 balance) against a real $40 service booking (Neck Massage) — the actual redemption mechanic works correctly, but found 1 real bug along the way (**e2e-bug.38 — Fixed**, see Fix log): a gift-card-paid booking's balance is never restored when that booking is cancelled.** On `BookPage.tsx`'s confirm step, the "Promo or gift card" field (correctly labeled to cover both, `copy.checkoutPromoCode`) accepted the gift card code and, after clicking Apply, correctly showed "Applied: GC-6DC4544E" with a Remove link, "Gift card −$40.00," and the total dropping from $40.00 to $0.00 — the loyalty-points section's "up to X points" hint also correctly disappeared once nothing remained to redeem via points. (First attempt via synthetic browser events showed no visible change at all — a test-tooling artifact already established earlier this session, rapid synchronous DOM-event dispatches in a single script block not accumulating in React state; redone with the input-set and the Apply-click as two separate tool calls, and it worked correctly.) Confirmed via a direct API booking call with `promoCode: "GC-6DC4544E"` that the real booking-creation path (not just the quote preview) correctly applies the discount: the created booking's `paymentStatus` was `paid`, `metadata.pricing.amountDue` was `0`, and `adjustments` correctly recorded a `gift_card` line for `$40`. Verified directly in the dev DB that the gift card's `balance` column dropped from `50.00` to exactly `10.00` — the real redemption write path works precisely as the quote predicted. **e2e-bug.38 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: cancelling a booking that was paid for (in full or in part) with a gift card does not restore any of the redeemed balance back to the card.** Cancelled the test booking above and re-checked `GC-6DC4544E`'s balance: still `10.00`, not restored to `50.00`. Confirmed via grep across the whole backend that `BookingService.cancel()` (and everything it calls) has **zero** reference to gift cards, gift card balances, or any restoration mechanism — unlike Stripe-paid bookings, which have a (albeit separately imperfect, see **e2e-bug.35**) `BookingRefundService`, and unlike subscription-credit-paid bookings, which do get their appointment credit restored on cancel (`restoreCreditForBooking`, established earlier this session). Gift card redemption is a complete dead end once spent: a customer who books using a $50 gift card, spends $40 of it, then cancels the appointment (for any reason — provider unavailable, policy-compliant cancellation, business error) permanently loses that $40 of gift card value with no system-driven path to get it back, unlike every other payment method this business supports. **Fix direction:** in `BookingService.cancel()` (or the calling `cancelBookingInternal()`), read `booking.metadata.pricing.giftCardId`/`giftCardDiscount` (already present, confirmed via the pricing snapshot above) and — mirroring the subscription-credit restoration pattern — credit `giftCardDiscount` back onto the gift card's `balance` when a paid, non-already-cancelled booking is cancelled.

#### Account tab and its many sub-sections (`/s/:slug/account`)

The only nearby button, "View profile details" (`copy.profileViewDetails`, honestly labeled "Salon profile" in English / "Salon-ի էջ" in Armenian — not misleadingly worded), routes to `SalonProfilePage` (`App.tsx:68`), which is the **business's** own public profile (phone/email/address/social links) — confirmed by reading the component, not the customer's. - [x] ~~My appointments — full list pagination/filtering if the customer has many bookings (I generated ~10 test bookings this session — good dataset to check list rendering/sorting with)~~ — **tested thoroughly (18-booking list), no list-rendering bugs, but found 1 severe backend bug (**e2e-bug.30 — Fixed**, see Fix log; same as api-bug.1 / e2e-bug.97) plus 1 severe client-side session bug (**e2e-bug.31 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** List rendering itself is correct: all 18 bookings for the test customer render with correct service/employee/date/status, sorted sensibly, no pagination needed/tested at this volume (list just renders everything — fine at 18, untested at much larger volume). `canCancel`/`canReschedule`/`canReview` flags all matched expected business rules exactly — same-day bookings inside the 24h notice window correctly show neither action (just the policy-explanation text), cancelled bookings correctly show none, and the 2 `completed` bookings correctly show `canReview: false` because this customer had already reviewed that employee previously (confirmed via the one-review-per-customer-per-employee constraint, not a bug). Package-grouped bookings vs. standalone bookings both render via their respective code paths with no visible issues. Cancel button: works correctly and instantly (no confirm-dialog before the irreversible action — `window.confirm()` IS actually used per the code, so there should be a native browser confirm; worth a follow-up check on whether that's suppressed/auto-accepted in some contexts, but functionally cancel behaved correctly here). **e2e-bug.30 — customer-initiated reschedule crashes the backend with a 500 for every single attempt.** Clicking "Change time" → picking a new date/slot → "Confirm new time" always fails: `POST me/bookings/:id/reschedule` returns `500 {"message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"customer:c0ad5d15-...\""}`. Root-caused precisely: `PublicCustomerBookingService.rescheduleBookingInternal()` (`public-customer-booking.service.ts:543-555`) builds an actor marker via `actorUserId()` (line 837-839: `` `customer:${customerId}` ``) and passes it as the `userId` param into `BookingService.update()` (`booking.service.ts:507`). `update()` (unlike `cancel()`, which never hits this path — confirmed cancel works fine) calls `resolvePhiAuditActor(businessId, userId)` (line 135-148) whenever `userId` is truthy, which calls `businessService.ensureMember(businessId, userId)` — a lookup that expects a genuine **staff/team-member UUID**, not a customer-prefixed marker string. Postgres rejects the malformed UUID literal before any application code can validate it, crashing the whole request. **This means the customer self-service reschedule feature is 100% broken for every signed-in customer** (and, since the actor-string construction is identical for guest-token reschedule too, likely broken there as well, though not separately retested here). **Fix direction:** in `resolvePhiAuditActor`, detect and skip (or specially handle) the `"customer:"`-prefixed marker instead of passing it straight into a staff-membership UUID lookup — e.g. `if (userId?.startsWith('customer:')) return { role: 'public', userId: null }` before calling `ensureMember`. **e2e-bug.31 — after any successful booking, the client's cached customer profile permanently loses its email and phone, breaking every subsequent booking attempt in the same browser session.** Discovered while chasing a recurring "Enter your contact details to book" block on a second/third booking attempt for an already-signed-in customer with a complete profile (name/email/phone all visible on the live Account page). Root-caused: `BookPage.tsx` (and identically `MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx`/`PackageCheckoutPage.tsx`) call `setCustomerSession(slug, token, result.customer)` after every successful booking/payment-confirmation (`BookPage.tsx:1338-1340`, `:789-791`), where `result.customer` is the **booking-creation** response's minimal customer shape (`public-booking.service.ts:202`: `{id, name, created}` only) — not the richer `{id, name, email, phone}` profile shape returned at sign-in (`public-customer-auth.service.ts:596-603`, `toProfile()`). This overwrites the previously-cached richer profile in `localStorage` (`consumer_profile_<slug>`), permanently stripping `email`/`phone` from it. Since `BookPage.tsx`'s checkout-contact resolution (`resolveCheckoutContactPrefill`/`resolveCheckoutContact`, using `getStoredCustomerProfile()`) depends on this cached blob having email+phone to auto-validate a signed-in customer's contact info — and the page shows no editable contact form at all for signed-in users, only "Signed in as {name}" text — every booking attempt *after the first* in the same browser is silently blocked with a generic message and literally no way to fix it short of manually clearing storage or signing out/in (which will break again after that next booking). Confirmed by inspecting `localStorage.consumer_profile_gevgas-operations-7c299253` directly: after one successful booking it read `{"id":"...","name":"Gev Gas","created":false}` — no email, no phone — despite the Account page correctly showing both (fetched live, unaffected). **Fix direction:** never call `setCustomerSession` with a booking-response's thin customer object; either omit the `setCustomerSession` call after booking entirely (session/token doesn't need updating from a booking response) or merge fields onto the existing stored profile instead of replacing it outright.
- [x] **e2e-bug.39 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: every submit-time error on the booking confirm page is rendered as a generic "network error with retry" card, even for validation failures that have nothing to do with the network and can't be fixed by retrying.** Surfaced by the user directly from a live screenshot of the **e2e-bug.31** failure state (the "Enter your contact details to book" block): the card showed a "Try again" button and rendered as plain inline text below the "Confirm booking" button rather than a toast/modal. Root-caused in `BookPage.tsx:1924-1931`: the page's single `message` state (set at ~15 different call sites for wildly different failure kinds — network errors, `"Enter your contact details to book."` at line 1257, `copy.checkoutSubscriptionPlanRequired` at line 1261, offline-queue notices, etc.) is always rendered through one shared component, `ConsumerNetworkErrorCard` (`consumer-app/src/components/ConsumerNetworkErrorCard.tsx`), whose own doc-comment says it's for "Inline recoverable error with retry (adopt-5.4)" — it unconditionally shows a `retryLabel` button wired to `onRetry={() => void submit()}` and always renders as a plain `<div role="alert">` in the page's normal content flow (`ion-margin-top`), never as a toast/overlay. There is no branching anywhere on the *kind* of error before choosing how to present it. **Concretely, for the e2e-bug.31 case:** clicking "Try again" just calls `submitBooking()` again with the exact same (still-incomplete) cached profile, so it fails identically every time — the retry action is not just unhelpful but actively misleading, since it implies the problem is transient when it's actually a permanent block until the underlying cache issue is fixed or the customer signs out/in. **Fix direction:** distinguish validation/blocking errors (missing contact info, missing subscription plan selection, policy violations) from genuinely retriable network/server errors before choosing how to render them — e.g. only show `ConsumerNetworkErrorCard`'s retry affordance for errors caught from an actual failed API call, and render pure client-side validation messages as a plain inline warning with no misleading "try again" button; separately, consider whether a toast (auto-dismissing, non-blocking) is a better fit than an inline card for at least the transient network-error case, reserving inline persistent text for validation errors the customer needs to act on before proceeding.
