### e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-ai-assistant — Deep test case breakdown for the AI Booking Assistant

Deep-dive specifically on the AI assistant, grounded in reading `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` (906 lines) plus its supporting `lib/*.ts` files and the 11 guide-flow JSON definitions in `assets/guide-flows/customer/`. This component is far richer than "type a prompt, get a reply" — it has a chat mode AND a guide mode, voice I/O, client-side side-effects triggered by server responses, and a slot-picker sub-panel.

**Blocking dependency, stated up front:** every single case below that requires an actual assistant reply is currently blocked by **e2e-bug.1** (the `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` undefined crash) — this whole test area is un-executable until that's fixed. Cases that only exercise client-side UI state (opening the panel, toggling modes, dragging the FAB) can be tested independently right now.

#### Entry point / floating button (testable now, no backend dependency)

- [x] ~~FAB renders at the default bottom-inset position on first load; drag it and confirm the new position persists per-slug (`consumer-ai-position-${slug}` storage key) across a reload~~ — **tested live twice this session (see note), works correctly, no bug found.** On first load the FAB's fixed-position container measured `right: 24px`, `bottom: 64px` — an exact match to `getConsumerFabDefaultBottomInset()` in `consumer-tab-bar-layout.util.ts` (`CONSUMER_TAB_BAR_CORE_HEIGHT_PX(52) + CONSUMER_FAB_MARGIN_ABOVE_TAB_PX(12) = 64`) and the hook's own `DEFAULT_MARGIN = 24` (`use-draggable-floating-position.ts`). Dragged the FAB to a new screen position; `localStorage['consumer-ai-position-<slug>']` was written immediately with an anchor object whose `x`/`y` matched `anchorFromPosition()`'s math for the drop coordinates (right/bottom-relative, not raw x/y, confirming the anchor-flipping logic that keeps the FAB pinned to its nearest edge). Hard-reloaded the page (full navigation, not HMR) and the FAB re-rendered at the exact same dragged position, read back via `readStoredAnchor()` and converted back through `positionFromAnchor()` — pixel-for-pixel identical to the pre-reload position. **Process note:** this exact item's write-up was lost/reverted back to unchecked at least twice earlier in this session (once between the initial test and a later identical re-request, and apparently again after that redo — this file showed it still unchecked, with no trace of either prior write-up, when re-examined during the close-mechanism test below); root cause undetermined (possibly a tool/edit race), flagging here in case it recurs a third time.
- [x] ~~FAB drag vs. tap-to-open disambiguation — does a quick tap always open the panel, and does a drag never accidentally open it mid-drag?~~ — **tested live, works correctly, no bug found.** With instrumented `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` listeners confirming genuine input reached the FAB: (1) a quick tap (`left_click`, no intervening movement) correctly opened the "Booking assistant" panel every time, both from the default position and again from a post-drag position; (2) a real drag (multiple `pointermove` events, cumulative movement of hundreds of pixels, far past the 5px `DRAG_THRESHOLD` in `use-draggable-floating-position.ts:28`) moved the FAB to the drop point and the panel **never** opened — confirmed both by the end-state screenshot and by static read of the hook: `setOpen(true)` is only ever invoked via the `press` callback inside `finishDrag`, which is gated `!moved` (`use-draggable-floating-position.ts:266,284-285`) — once `active.moved` flips true on the first qualifying `pointermove` (`:318-321`), no code path anywhere in `onMove` can open the panel, so "opens mid-drag" is structurally unreachable, not just empirically absent; (3) tap-to-open correctly still worked immediately after a drag at the FAB's new position, confirming no lingering `isDragging`/drag-ref state leaks between interactions. One harmless testing artifact noted, not a bug: after the panel toggled open→closed once, the FAB `<button>` is unmounted/remounted (open renders a `<div>` panel, closed renders a fresh `<button>`), so a `button`-reference captured before the toggle no longer strictly-equals the new element — purely a test-instrumentation quirk (stale JS reference), not an app defect.
- [x] ~~Opening the panel — size computation at different viewport widths (`Math.min(400, viewport.width - 32)`) — check on a narrow phone width where 400px would overflow~~ — **tested live at two narrow widths, works correctly, no bug found.** At `375px` viewport (iPhone-class width, where a flat 400px panel would overflow by 25px): opened the panel and measured the actual rendered fixed-position container via `getBoundingClientRect()` — width `343px`, exactly matching `Math.min(400, 375-32)=343`; confirmed `document.documentElement.scrollWidth (375) === window.innerWidth (375)`, i.e. zero horizontal overflow/scrollbar. At an even narrower `320px` viewport: rendered width `288px`, exactly matching `Math.min(400, 320-32)=288`, again zero horizontal overflow. In both cases the panel's `left` position (`8px` at 375px, `8px` at 320px) was consistent with reusing the FAB's persisted `right: 24` anchor for the panel's own (larger) size, and the panel rendered fully on-screen with correct margins — no clipping, no illegible squashed content, no double scrollbars. The height side of the same size computation (`min(80vh, 560px)`) was cross-checked incidentally and was also consistent with the observed rect at 375×812 (`560px` tall, `= 0.8×812 rounds to 650 → capped at 560`).
- [x] ~~Closing via the X button, via Escape key, and via a message's own navigate-triggered auto-close — confirm all three reset `messages`/`sessionContext`/`voiceError` identically~~ — **tested live, X and Escape both fully reset; navigate-close's own reset code is provably incomplete but the gap is unreachable in this app today — no live-visible bug, but a real latent one.** Populated both pieces of state through means independent of the still-blocked (`e2e-bug.1`) AI reply path: `voiceError` via a real mic-permission denial (clicking the mic button in `ConsumerAiVoiceControls.tsx` — the Browser pane blocks device capture, so `useSpeechRecognition`'s `onerror` fires with `not-allowed` for real, setting `handleVoiceError`'s "Microphone access was denied." — `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx:451-464`); `messages` via the optimistic client-side append in `submit()` (`:286-289`), which runs before any network call. With both populated: (1) clicking the **X** button (`onClick={closeAssistant}`, `:553`) closed the panel; reopening showed a completely blank initial state — no chat bubble, no voice-error text. (2) Repopulated both, pressed **Escape** (window `keydown` listener, `:251-258`, calling the same `closeAssistant`); identical full reset on reopen. Both match the static read of `closeAssistant` (`:239-249`): `setOpen(false); setMessages([]); setSessionContext({}); setVoiceError(null);`. (3) For the navigate-triggered path, static reading of all three call sites (`followNavigate` at `:264-272`, the guide panel's `onNavigate` at `:761-772`, and the "Open guide" button's `openNativeGuide` at `:239-241`) confirms **none of them reset `messages`/`sessionContext`/`voiceError`** — they only do `history.push(...); setOpen(false);`. This is a real, confirmed code asymmetry. **However**, live-testing the actual consequence (via `openNativeGuide` as a live-clickable proxy, and separately via a full audit of every `navigate.path` target in `consumer-assistant-navigate.util.ts`) showed it has no observable effect in this app **today**: every single navigation target the assistant can ever produce — `guide`, `professionals`, `services`, `packages`, `checkout`, `account`, `login`, `manage`, `home`, `profile`, `gift-cards`, etc. — resolves to its own distinct top-level `<Route>` in `App.tsx` (confirmed by reading the full route table, lines 52-101), none of which are nested inside `SalonTabRoute`. Since each is a structurally different React element in the router's `Switch`, navigating to any of them always fully unmounts the current `ConsumerBookingAssistant` instance and mounts a brand-new one with fresh initial state — which trivially "resets" `messages`/`sessionContext`/`voiceError` by destruction, not by the missing code path ever running. Confirmed this directly: populated `messages`+`voiceError`, clicked "Open guide" (same `history.push`+`setOpen(false)` pattern as the real navigate calls), and separately confirmed via the route-change test below that any destination reliably shows a fresh assistant with no leaked state. **Net verdict:** not filing this as a numbered `e2e-bug` — the missing reset is real but currently dead code given this app's all-top-level-routes structure; it would only become a live-visible bug if a future `navigate.path` target were ever added that resolves *within* the same mounted `SalonTabRoute` (e.g. a same-tab sub-view that doesn't remount), at which point stale `messages`/`voiceError` would leak into the next-opened panel. Worth a one-line defensive fix (call `closeAssistant`-style resets in `followNavigate`/`onNavigate`/`openNativeGuide` too) but not user-visible today, so left undone per this session's "document, don't fix" policy.
- [x] ~~Panel remains open/closed correctly across a route change while open (does navigating away from the assistant close it, or does it float across pages?)~~ — **tested live, works correctly, no bug found: the panel never floats across pages — it always closes and resets.** Opened the assistant on the Home tab, populated a chat message via the "What's the cheapest service?" quick-suggestion chip, then clicked the bottom-nav **Book** tab (`ref` for the nav button, not the assistant) while the panel was still open. Result: the panel closed automatically (confirmed via screenshot and `read_page` — the FAB button reappeared in place of the "Close" button) and the destination page (Services/Book tab) rendered underneath with its own fresh FAB. Reopening the assistant there showed a completely clean state (no leftover "cheapest service" bubble) and page-specific quick suggestions correctly scoped to the Services page ("Who is available tomorrow afternoon for Face Pilling?", etc.), confirming a genuine fresh mount, not a stale cached instance. Root cause read from `App.tsx:81-98`: `home`/`services`/`account`/`results`/`lab-to-book`/`lab-requests` are each their own separate `<Route exact path="/s/:slug/...">` element rendering `<SalonTabRoute page="...">` — switching tabs is a route change between distinct elements in the outlet's `Switch`, not a prop change on one persistent element, so `SalonTabChrome`→`ConsumerAiShell`→`ConsumerBookingAssistant` fully unmounts and remounts on every tab switch (the `key={`salon-tab-${slug}-${page}`}` on `SalonTabRoute.tsx:43`'s `<IonPage>` is consistent with this but not even the deciding factor — the separate top-level `<Route>` match alone already forces it). Same conclusion applies to in-flow navigation (e.g. "Choose a specialist first" from the Services page → `/s/:slug/professionals`, also a distinct top-level route) — there is no navigation target anywhere in this app that keeps `SalonTabRoute`/the assistant mounted, so "does it float across pages" has a clean, structural answer: no, never, by construction. (Incidental test-tooling note, not a bug: one click aimed at the FAB's expected screen position briefly landed on an underlying "Face Pilling" service checkbox instead, due to a stale coordinate assumption from an earlier screenshot; caught and corrected immediately by re-deriving the FAB's exact position via its `ion-button`/`getBoundingClientRect()`, and the accidental selection was undone before continuing — no lasting effect on the test business's data.)

By contrast, `/s/:slug/results` (the `my-results` bucket's real page) does mount the assistant (`hasBookingAssistantText: true`), confirming this isn't a general navigation/timing artifact — it's specifically that these particular routes never render the widget. **Real-world impact**: a real customer on the actual booking-confirmation/checkout screen — arguably the highest-value moment for the assistant's "why do I owe a deposit," "can I pay cash," "why do you need my email" prompts — has no assistant to ask at all; the same is true for gift-card checkout, guest booking-management, multi-service checkout, package confirmation, and the multi-service picker. **Fix direction:** either mount `ConsumerAiShell`/`ConsumerBookingAssistant` on these standalone routes too (mirroring how it's already done for the 6 `SalonTabRoute` pages), or move these flows under the same tab-chrome wrapper if that's architecturally intended; either way, `CONSUMER_PAGE_SUGGESTION_KEYS`'s 8 affected buckets are currently dead code that a future contributor could easily assume are live (they have full copy-catalog entries and even dedicated unit-test coverage in `consumer-ai-page-suggestions.util.spec.ts`, which only exercises the pure string-building function and can't catch "is the assistant even on this page"). — **Fixed (6 of 8 affected pages; `welcome` and the guest-token variant of `manage-booking-guest` left as documented exceptions, see below).** Wrapped each page's already-loaded (`useTenantBootstrap`/`useConsumerCopy`) success-path JSX in `<ConsumerAiShell slug=... profile=... copy=... locale=...>` — the exact same component `SalonTabChrome.tsx` already uses — in: `BookPage.tsx` (`book`), `ManageBookingPage.tsx` (`manage-booking`/`manage-booking-guest`), `MultiServicePickerPage.tsx` (`multi-service-picker`), `GiftCardCheckoutPage.tsx` (`gift-card-checkout`, also had to add `locale` to its `useConsumerCopy` destructure since only `copy` was previously taken), `MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx` (`multi-service-checkout`), and `PackageConfirmPage.tsx` (`package-confirm`). Each of these pages already resolves `slug`/`profile`/`copy`/`locale` locally before its final return (guarded by the same `if (loading/error/!profile) return <...>` pattern `SalonTabRoute.tsx` uses), so no new data-fetching was needed — only the wrap. **`welcome` (`WelcomePage.tsx`, path `/`) intentionally left unfixed**: it renders before any specific business/tenant is selected, so there's no `profile`/`copy`/`slug` for `ConsumerAiShell` to bind to yet — architecturally a different case from the other 7, not a same-fix candidate. Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` in `consumer-app` shows zero new errors (the only errors present — `LoginPage.tsx:66` and `GiftCardCheckoutPage.integration.spec.tsx` — are pre-existing, untouched by this change, confirmed via `git status`). Live-verified end-to-end on the actual dev server: navigated to `/s/:slug/book/<real-service-id>` (the literal checkout page this bug's own test asked for) — `document.body.innerHTML.includes('Booking assistant')` now returns `true` (previously `false`), the FAB renders, and opening it shows exactly the expected `book`-bucket suggestions ("How much do I pay today?", "Pay cash at visit", "Why do you need my email?"). Attempted the same live check on `/gift-cards/checkout` too; that specific business (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`) turned out to have gift-card purchasing disabled (`purchaseEnabled: false, settings: null` from the real API response), so it legitimately hits the pre-existing `!settings` error branch (before the new wrap) rather than exercising the fix — not a regression, just an untestable case in this environment. **Update — the remaining 4 pages were subsequently live-verified too, all correct.** Created real fixtures via the actual public API rather than skipping ahead: a real booking (`POST .../bookings`, Face Pilling with Karo Mazmanyan, `2026-07-20T09:00:00Z`, confirmed against a real `GET .../services/:id/slots` response first) to get a genuine `bookingId`+`manageToken` pair, and used the real "Massage Package" package id from `GET .../packages`. Results: **`ManageBookingPage`** (`/manage?bookingId=...&token=...`) → assistant mounts, `manage-booking` bucket shows exactly "Cancel this appointment" / "Reschedule to next week" / "Send manage link". **`MultiServicePickerPage`** (`/book/any`) → assistant mounts, `multi-service-picker` bucket shows exactly "How long will this take?" / "Find afternoon slot for all services". **`MultiServiceCheckoutPage`** (`/book/multi/checkout?services=...&startTime=...`) → assistant mounts, `multi-service-checkout` bucket shows exactly "Use my subscription" / "Why is total $0?". **`PackageConfirmPage`** (`/book/packages/570ca68d-...`) → assistant mounts, `package-confirm` bucket shows exactly "How many visits in this package?" / "Book first visit now". All four exactly matched their `CONSUMER_PAGE_SUGGESTION_KEYS` bucket, same as the earlier `BookPage` confirmation — the fix is now live-verified on 5 of the 6 wrapped pages (only `GiftCardCheckoutPage` remains unverified live, blocked by this business's gift-cards-disabled config, not by the fix). **One incidental, separate, lower-priority finding surfaced while testing `MultiServiceCheckoutPage` without a `startTime`** (not e2e-bug.172, not fixed, just noted): `MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx:200-201` self-redirects via `history.replace` to `/book/multi/availability` (a different top-level route, `MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx`, which never imports `ConsumerAiShell`) whenever `!hasSchedule`. Landing on that redirected page showed the assistant FAB still visibly present and functional despite that component never rendering it — apparently the just-mounted `ConsumerAiShell` instance from `MultiServiceCheckoutPage`'s own brief initial render (before its `useEffect` fires the redirect) survives the route swap, likely an artifact of `IonRouterOutlet`'s hidden-page-stacking (`animated={false}` in `App.tsx`) combined with a same-tick `history.replace`. Not chased further — re-testing with an explicit `startTime` avoided the redirect entirely and gave a clean read of the actual page.

Not filing this service/provider mismatch as a bug: the checklist item only asks whether real data vs. placeholder is used (confirmed: real), and using "the business's first active service" as a stand-in default is a reasonable, harmless simplification for a one-tap discovery prompt, not a functional defect.

Fixed by passing `business` instead of `business.id`, matching the identical, correctly-written call site 50 lines below it (`public-booking-assistant.service.ts:2376`). Confirmed via `npx tsc --noEmit` (no more errors in this file) and `npx jest --testPathPatterns='src/modules/public-booking/public-booking-assistant'` (41/42 tests pass; the 1 pre-existing failure is an unrelated classifier misroute — `explain_salon_profile` vs `explain_provider_specialty` — with no relation to the business-object parameter touched here). **Secondary, minor, not filed as a separate bug**: the rendered chat bubble also looks like it triplicates the step label ("Step 1 of 3: Step 1" then a step-list showing title "Step 1" / body "Confirm...") — traced this to `ai-product-guide-multiturn.util.ts:269`'s `progressSummary = "Step ${currentIndex+1} of ${totalSteps}: ${currentStep?.title ?? 'Guide step'}"` combined with `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx:316`'s `text: result.summary` and a separate `ConsumerGuideStepList` rendering the same step's `title`/`body` underneath — not a functional bug, just visually redundant because these fixtures' step titles are literally the generic strings `"Step 1"`/`"Step 2"`/`"Step 3"` rather than descriptive titles; would look fine with descriptive step titles.
- [x] Multi-service checkout — select 2+ services, reach the "Confirm your visit" checkout page, then delete one service from the selected list; confirm what happens and why — **found e2e-bug.175: deleting one line item at checkout discards the entire booking draft (specialist, date, time, and any typed contact info) and sends the customer all the way back to the service picker, instead of just recalculating the remaining line.** Live-tested: selected `facemassage` + `full body massage`, matched to specialist Gevorg Gasparyan, picked the 13:30 slot, reached [MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx) showing both services with trash-icon delete buttons and a "Confirm your visit" summary (20/07/2026 13:30-15:05, 95 min, $110 total). Clicked the trash icon on `facemassage` — instead of removing just that row, the app navigated to `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/book/any?services=<remaining-id>`, landing back on the plain multi-service picker page with only `full body massage` still checked; the specialist, the 13:30 slot, and the whole "Confirm your visit" step were gone, forcing a full re-pick. **Root cause**: `removeService` ([MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx:272-279](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx:272)) never updates local component state to drop the one line item — it unconditionally calls `history.push(resolvePathAfterRemovingService(...))`. `resolvePathAfterRemovingService` ([multi-service-booking.ts:379-393](consumer-app/src/lib/multi-service-booking.ts:379)) computes a brand-new route from just the remaining service ids: back to `/book/any` if 0 remain, straight to the single-service page if 1 remains, or to the multi-service availability/confirm step (`?services=<remaining ids>`) if 2+ remain — none of these target paths carry `employeeId`/`startTime`/`lines`, because this page only ever reads specialist/time/contact state from the URL query string and local `useState` (confirmed: no autosave of the guest-contact fields outside of a successful booking). So the navigation isn't a bug in routing logic — it's that this page has no "in-place remove" implementation at all; the delete button's only job is to recompute the URL from the reduced id list and jump there, and everything not encoded in that URL (the chosen specialist, chosen slot, any name/email/phone already typed) is real, silent data loss. No code comment or commit message documents this as an intentional trade-off (checked via `git log -p` on the introducing commit). **Fixed (primary case).** Rewrote `removeService` ([MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx:273-313](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServiceCheckoutPage.tsx:273)): when 2+ services remain after the removal, it now calls `history.replace(buildMultiServiceCheckoutPath(slug, query))` targeting the *same* `/book/multi/checkout` route with a shorter `services` list (plus `startTime`/`employeeId`/`employeeName`, or the per-service `lines` array in `per_service` scheduling mode) instead of navigating away — since the pathname is unchanged and this app's `IonRouterOutlet` has no `<Switch>`, React Router updates the existing `MultiServiceCheckoutPage` in place rather than unmounting it, so the specialist, slot, and any already-typed guest-contact `useState` survive untouched, and `useCheckoutDiscounts`'s existing `deps: [serviceIds.join(',')]` automatically refetches the price quote for the reduced set. Live-verified (3→2 services): specialist, 13:30 slot, and a manually-typed "Your name" value all survived the deletion, staying on the same checkout page with a correctly-recalculated total. When only 1 service remains, this page structurally can't display it (it requires 2+), so it still hands off to the single-service `/book/:serviceId` page, but now carries `slot`/`date`/`employeeId` as query params that `BookPage.tsx`'s existing `resumePrefill` (lines ~312-349) already knows how to consume, instead of dropping those silently as before. **Found a second, separate, pre-existing bug while verifying the 1-remaining case — logged separately as e2e-bug.177 below** — fixing that is out of scope here since it's a deeper router-behavior issue, not something introduced by or fixable within this change.
- [x] Multi-service checkout "Subtotal"/"Due now" both showing $0.00 despite real per-line prices — noticed in passing while testing e2e-bug.175 above, then investigated on its own — **found e2e-bug.176: for a pay-at-venue business, the multi-service checkout quote displays "Subtotal: $0.00" instead of the real service total, because the backend's `subtotal` field is populated from the online-prepayment amount, not the actual service price.** Reproduced live: 2 services (`facemassage` $60 + `full body massage` $50, real total $110) reached "Confirm your visit" showing correct per-line prices but **"Subtotal: $0.00" and "Due now: $0.00"** underneath. **Root cause, precisely traced**: `MultiServiceBookingsService` correctly computes the real total (`totalPrice = $110`) and passes it as `servicePrice` into `checkoutPricingService.calculate(...)` ([booking-payment.service.ts:596-598](backend/src/modules/booking/booking-payment.service.ts:596)), alongside a separately-computed `prepaymentAmount` ([booking-payment.service.ts:590-594](backend/src/modules/booking/booking-payment.service.ts:590), via `sumServicesPrepaymentAmount` summing `calculatePrepaymentAmount(service)` per line — which returns `0` for any service whose `prepaymentMode` is `NONE`/pay-at-venue, the default, and has no fallback to the real price). But [checkout-pricing.service.ts:28-29](backend/src/modules/promo-codes/checkout-pricing.service.ts:28) sets its **local `subtotal` variable to `prepaymentAmount`, not `servicePrice`** — `const subtotal = Math.max(0, Number(input.prepaymentAmount)); const servicePrice = Math.max(0, Number(input.servicePrice));` — and only `subtotal` (not the unused-by-the-UI `servicePrice`, confirmed present in `CheckoutPricingResult` at [checkout-pricing.types.ts:51-52](backend/src/modules/promo-codes/checkout-pricing.types.ts:51) but never read by the frontend) feeds `computeCheckoutTotals` ([checkout-pricing.util.ts:86-96](backend/src/modules/promo-codes/checkout-pricing.util.ts:86)), which derives `amountDue` from that same already-zeroed `subtotal`. The frontend, [ConsumerCheckoutQuoteSummary.tsx:21-22](consumer-app/src/components/ConsumerCheckoutQuoteSummary.tsx:21) (`const amountDue = quote.amountDue ?? quote.subtotal ?? 0; const subtotal = quote.subtotal ?? amountDue;`), renders exactly what it's given — both labels bound to the same mislabeled value, both `$0.00` for any pay-at-venue multi-service booking. **Why single-service checkout doesn't show this**: the single-service pricing path, `resolveCheckoutPricing` ([booking-payment.service.ts:854-856](backend/src/modules/booking/booking-payment.service.ts:854)), has `const unitPrice = prepaymentAmount > 0 ? prepaymentAmount : Number(service.price);` — a full-price fallback the multi-service path's `sumServicesPrepaymentAmount` lacks — which accidentally masks the same underlying `subtotal`/`servicePrice` field-mislabeling for single-service bookings (their `subtotal` just happens to equal the real price). **"Due now: $0.00" is legitimate** for a pay-at-venue business (nothing charged online today); **"Subtotal: $0.00" is not** — the real $110 total is computed correctly server-side (`servicePrice`) but never reaches the field the UI actually displays. **Fixed.** Took the lower-risk of the two documented options: left the entire backend pricing/discount calculator untouched (no change to `checkout-pricing.service.ts`'s `subtotal`/`amountDue` computation, so promo/gift-card/loyalty math and the actual amount charged are byte-for-byte identical to before) and instead changed only the display binding in [ConsumerCheckoutQuoteSummary.tsx:22](consumer-app/src/components/ConsumerCheckoutQuoteSummary.tsx:22) — `const subtotal = quote.servicePrice ?? quote.subtotal ?? amountDue;` (was `quote.subtotal ?? amountDue`) — so the "Subtotal" label now prefers the always-correct, already-returned `servicePrice` field, falling back to the old value only if it's ever absent. Confirmed `servicePrice` is a required (non-optional) field on `PublicCheckoutQuote` ([types.ts:114](consumer-app/src/lib/types.ts:114)) and is populated by all 4 backend call sites of `checkoutPricingService.calculate` (single-service, package, and multi-service), so this fix applies uniformly with no call site needing changes. `amountDue`/"Due now" is completely untouched. Verified via `npx vitest run` across 5 checkout-related spec files (36 tests, all pass) and live re-testing: multi-service checkout (`facemassage` + `full body massage`) now shows **"Subtotal: $110.00"** (was $0.00) with **"Due now: $0.00"** correctly unchanged (pay-at-venue); single-service checkout (`Face Pilling`) re-confirmed unaffected, still correctly shows "Subtotal: $5.00". Separately noticed but out of scope: `CheckoutTaxSummary.tsx:25` has the identical `quote.subtotal ?? quote.amountDue ?? 0` pattern, but that component isn't imported/rendered anywhere in the app (confirmed via repo-wide search) — dead code, not worth touching for this fix.
- [x] Multi-service checkout — deleting a service down to exactly 1 remaining (2→1), discovered while fixing e2e-bug.175 above — **found e2e-bug.177: even though `removeService` computes and pushes the correct target URL (`/s/<slug>/book/<remainingServiceId>?slot=...&date=...&employeeId=...`), the browser ends up on `/s/<slug>/book/any?services=<remainingServiceId>` instead** — the plain multi-service picker page, not the intended single-service `BookPage.tsx`. Root-caused extensively: confirmed via a temporary `window.__debug` instrumentation that the value passed to `history.push` is correct in both the current fix and the original, unmodified pre-fix code (`history.push(resolvePathAfterRemovingService(...))`, no query params) — reproducing the identical misroute with zero query params proves this is a pre-existing bug, not something introduced by the e2e-bug.175 fix. Ruled out: `resolveBookPathCollision` ([multi-service-booking.ts:337-343](consumer-app/src/lib/multi-service-booking.ts:337)) only matches the literal strings `'any'`/`'multi'`, not a UUID; `BookPage.tsx` itself has zero multi-service-related code or redirects (confirmed via grep); a stale mounted `MultiServiceConfirmPage` (ruled out by reproducing in a freshly-reloaded browser session). **Fixed — root cause conclusively pinned down via a `history.pushState`/`replaceState` monkey-patch trace** (not a router-matching quirk after all): both [MultiServicePickerPage.tsx](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServicePickerPage.tsx) (the `/book/any` picker, mounted once at the very start of any multi-service flow) and [MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx) (the `/book/multi/availability` step) each have a `useEffect` that reads the **global** `useLocation().search` to decide whether to self-redirect back to the picker when the cart looks invalid. Because this app's `IonRouterOutlet` has no `<Switch>` and never unmounts previously-visited stack pages, both components stay mounted for the rest of the session, and `useLocation()` is the same singleton for every mounted component regardless of which page is visually active — so these effects kept re-firing on every later, unrelated navigation anywhere in the app. The trace showed the exact sequence: `removeService`'s `history.push('/book/<remainingServiceId>?slot=...&employeeId=...')` fires correctly, then **10ms later** `MultiServicePickerPage`'s stale effect sees the new URL has no `services` query param, falls back to the cart it had just persisted via `persistMultiServiceCart(slug, [remainingServiceId])`, and — since that's a 1-length, non-empty list — fires its own `history.replace('/book/any?services=<remainingServiceId>')`, silently overwriting the correct navigation. Confirmed via `curl`-verified served source and a fresh dev-server restart that this reproduced with the actual code, not a stale cache. **Fix**: added a `location.pathname.endsWith(...)` guard to both effects' bodies (`'/book/any'` in [MultiServicePickerPage.tsx:101](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServicePickerPage.tsx:101), `'/book/multi/availability'` in [MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:110](consumer-app/src/pages/MultiServiceAvailabilityPage.tsx:110)) so each self-redirect effect only acts while its own route is actually the current one — the same defensive pattern this codebase already uses in [BookPage.tsx:398](consumer-app/src/pages/BookPage.tsx:398) for the identical class of Ionic-stack issue. `location.pathname` added to both effects' dependency arrays. #### Conversation mechanics

### e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-online-payment — Deep test case breakdown for online payment / Stripe checkout

Grounded in reading `consumer-checkout-return.util.ts`, `checkout-payment.util.ts`, `activation-payment.util.ts`, and the backend's `PrepaymentMode` enum. Online payment touches 4 distinct purchase kinds (single booking, multi-service, package, gift card) that each independently create a Stripe Checkout session, persist "pending checkout" state locally to survive the app losing focus while Stripe's hosted page is open, and reconcile on return. **All of this was blocked end-to-end by e2e-bug.10 (no Stripe Connect account on the original test business, `gevgas-operations-7c299253`)** — that blocker is now resolvable: a real business with Stripe Connect already linked exists in this database.

**Unblocking business found (user-confirmed): `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8` ("Pollin Clinic").** Queried directly: `settings.integrations.stripe = {connectMode: "oauth", connectCountry: "US", connectAccountId: "acct_1Tdf7aE4QO2K9D1a", connectChargeModel: "destination"}` — a real linked Connect account. Readiness for the cases below:
- 3 services, **all `prepayment_mode: "full"`** (Baby haircut $25, men's haircut $20, girl's haircut $50) — unblocks every "full prepayment" case; **no `deposit`-mode service exists on this business**, so the deposit-math cases (50%-fallback rounding, `Math.min(depositAmount, price)`) still need either a service reconfigured to `deposit` mode here, or a different business.
- `giftCards.purchaseEnabled: true` already — unblocks gift-card checkout cases directly, no settings toggle needed this time.
- 1 employee (Margarita Simonyan) with 300 `scheduling_slots` already generated — bookable immediately, no schedule-seeding required (unlike the original test business).
- 3 real customers already exist in this business, including one under the user's own email — a real, non-synthetic account to test with if preferred over a forged session.
- `settings.businessType: "other"` — despite the name, this is not a clinic-vertical business. **User confirmed: not changing it** — the M13/M14 clinic-only cases stay out of scope for this business; they'd need a genuine clinic-vertical business to unblock, not a type change on this one.
- No `multiService` settings configured — the multi-service and package checkout cases below still need that turned on for this business first, separately from the Stripe Connect unblock.

Not yet executed — recorded here per "we'll think about execution" from the prior turn. When execution starts, this is the business to point at for the online-payment section specifically.

#### Prepayment mode (`PrepaymentMode`: `none` | `full` | `deposit`) — never exercised, this business's services are all `none`

- [ ] A service with `prepaymentMode: 'full'` — confirm `prepaymentDue()` returns the full price and `showCashPaymentOption` correctly returns `false` (cash shouldn't be offered when full online prepayment is required)
- [ ] A service with `prepaymentMode: 'deposit'` and a set `depositAmount` — confirm `Math.min(depositAmount, price)` is used (test with a deposit amount both smaller and larger than price, to hit both branches)
- [ ] A service with `prepaymentMode: 'deposit'` and NO `depositAmount` set — confirm the 50%-of-price fallback (`Math.round(service.price * 50) / 100`) is used, and check rounding on odd prices (e.g. $33.33 → does it round sanely to cents?)
- [ ] Deposit-mode + cash option interaction — code shows cash is hidden specifically `!(dueNow > 0 && prepaymentMode === 'deposit')`, i.e. deposit-mode services can't use cash at all if a deposit is due; confirm this exact rule holds in the UI, since it reads as a deliberately narrow exception worth a dedicated case
- [ ] `onlinePaymentEnabled: false` on a service — confirm `prepaymentDue()` short-circuits to 0 regardless of prepayment mode, and that the online payment method option is hidden/disabled entirely for this service

#### Payment method selection (cash vs. online)

- [ ] `acceptCashPayments: true` at the business level with an eligible (non-full, non-deposit) service — confirm both payment method options render and switching between them updates the displayed "due now" amount correctly
- [ ] `acceptCashPayments: false` — confirm cash option never appears regardless of service prepayment mode
- [ ] Selecting cash — confirm the booking still completes and is recorded with the correct payment status (should skip Stripe checkout entirely, going straight to booking creation — this path IS already confirmed working from earlier sessions, but worth a dedicated regression case tied to the mode-interaction rules above)

#### Checkout session creation (per purchase kind, once Stripe Connect exists)

- [ ] Single-service checkout (`createPublicBookingCheckout` → redirect to Stripe) — session creation, correct amount/currency, correct line-item description
- [ ] Multi-service checkout (`createPublicMultiServiceCheckout`) — correct combined amount across services

- [ ] Gift-card checkout (`createPublicGiftCardCheckout`) — **must retest after e2e-bug.6's fix**, since this is the exact flow that currently infinite-loops before checkout can even be reached
- [ ] Subscription-plan checkout (via `createPublicBookingCheckout` with a `purchasePlanId`) — first-ever full run of this, previously blocked

#### Return-flow reconciliation (the most complex, least-tested part of this whole area)

- [ ] **Successful payment return** for each of the 4 kinds — confirm `parseCheckoutReturnRoute` correctly recognizes both the native-app URL pattern (`/s/:slug/...`) and the web URL pattern (`/book/:slug/...`) for the same purchase kind, and that `confirmPublicBookingPayment` is called with the right `sessionId` extracted from the return URL
- [ ] **`session_id` query param present** vs. **`paid=1` query param present** — `isCheckoutPaymentReturnQuery` treats these as two independent signals; confirm both actually occur in practice (which does Stripe's `success_url` template use, and does the custom `optischedule://` URL scheme use the other?) and that both are handled identically downstream
- [ ] **Return without any query param but with pending-checkout state still in storage** — `hasPackageCheckoutPaymentReturn`/`hasMultiCheckoutPaymentReturn`/`hasSingleCheckoutPaymentReturn` all fall back to checking local pending-checkout storage even with no URL signal at all; confirm this correctly resumes an abandoned-then-reopened checkout, and does NOT falsely trigger for a genuinely fresh, unrelated visit to the same checkout page
- [ ] **Stale/expired pending-checkout state** — what happens if a customer starts checkout, does nothing for days, then reopens the app to the same page? Is there any TTL/expiry on the pending-checkout storage, or does it persist and reconcile indefinitely?
- [ ] **Query-param merge on return** (`mergePackageCheckoutReturnQuery`/`mergeMultiCheckoutReturnQuery`) — reconstructing `lines`/`services` from pending-checkout storage when the return URL itself doesn't carry them; confirm this correctly restores the exact original selection (services, employee, times) rather than a stale or empty cart
- [ ] **Native custom URL scheme** (`optischedule://book/:slug/packages/:packageId/checkout`, `.../multi/checkout`, `.../gift-cards/checkout`) — these are 3 of the 4 kinds; notably **no native-scheme pattern exists for single-service checkout** in `readCheckoutReturnFromUrl` (only `webSingle` — the `/book/:slug/checkout` **web** pattern requiring a `serviceId` query param — is handled; there's no `optischedule://` branch for single-service at all). Worth confirming whether single-service Stripe returns are actually handled via a different mechanism on native, or whether this is a genuine gap where a native single-service payment return could fail to route back into the app correctly.
- [ ] **Cancelled/abandoned checkout** (user closes Stripe's hosted page without paying) — confirm the app correctly detects "no payment happened" rather than assuming success, and that the pending-checkout state either clears or remains resumable as appropriate
- [ ] **Double-confirmation** — call `confirmPublicBookingPayment` twice with the same `sessionId` (e.g., user double-taps back into the app, or a retry fires) — confirm idempotent handling, not a duplicate booking or duplicate charge

#### Payment failure / edge cases (Stripe test-mode card numbers make these directly testable once Connect exists)

- [ ] Card decline (Stripe's `4000000000000002` test card) — confirm the failure surfaces a sane message, not a raw error (cross-check against the e2e-bug.3 pattern — this is a very plausible 7th instance)

- [ ] Cancel a paid-online booking where the service has already been used/partially delivered — confirm `ineligible` status surfaces with a clear explanation, not a generic failure

- [ ] Subscription refund — same, specifically for the "any usage ledger CONSUME entry, even if later restored" permanent-ineligibility rule already implemented

### e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-payment-cases — All payment test cases, including AI-assistant-driven payment

Combines and extends the two prior deep-dives (`e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-online-payment` and `e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-ai-assistant`) at the user's request to cover "all payment cases including payment with AI assistant." Grounded in reading `backend/src/modules/ai/ai-payments.util.ts`/`ai-payments.logic.ts`/`ai-cash-payment-checkout.util.ts` and `consumer-app/src/lib/public-assistant-checkout.util.ts`/`consumer-gift-card-assistant-prefill.util.ts`.

**Blocking dependency, restated and sharpened:** the backend defines **18 distinct customer-facing payment intents** (`CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS_INTENTS` in `ai-payments.util.ts:116-134`) — every one of them routes through the same `/public/:slug/assistant` endpoint that **e2e-bug.1** crashes on the first hit. This bug is more consequential than previously scoped: it doesn't just block "chat with the assistant," it blocks an entire parallel payment-intent surface (quote-by-conversation, pay-by-conversation, receipt lookup by conversation) that has nothing to do with the regular checkout-page flows already covered.

**Execution note:** for the online-payment-specific cases (Stripe checkout, prepayment modes), use `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8` per the prior session's finding (real Stripe Connect account, all-`full`-prepayment services, gift cards enabled). For the pure conversational/classifier cases (does the assistant recognize the right intent for a given prompt), the original test business works fine once e2e-bug.1 is fixed, since those don't need real payment infrastructure — just a `sessionId`/quote to talk about.

#### The 18 customer payment intents — one section per intent

- [ ] **`check_providers_for_service`** — "who's available for a haircut" — read-only, not really payment but gates entry into a paid booking; confirm it correctly surfaces prepayment-required info per provider/service if relevant
- [ ] **`book_nearest_slot`** — "book me the soonest opening" — confirm the resulting booking correctly carries prepayment requirements into the subsequent checkout step, for a `full`-prepayment service specifically (this is the ideal case to test with `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8`'s services, all `full`-mode)
- [ ] **`get_booking_quote`** / **`get_package_quote`** / **`get_multi_service_quote`** — three parallel "how much would this cost" intents; confirm each returns the correct `amountDue` matching what the equivalent REST quote endpoint (already sweep-tested in API sweep M4/M5/M6) would return — this is a good spot to catch a conversational-layer amount-calculation drift from the REST layer
- [ ] **`choose_payment_method`** — "what payment options do I have" / "can I pay online with card" / "do you accept cash" (real example prompts from `CASH_PAYMENT_CHECKOUT_PROMPTS`) — confirm it correctly reflects THIS business's actual `acceptCashPayments` + per-service `prepaymentMode`, not a generic answer; test once against a `full`-mode service (should say online-only) and once against a `none`-mode service with cash enabled (should offer both)
- [ ] **`pay_online`** — explicit card-payment selection mid-conversation
- [ ] **`pay_cash_at_visit`** — "I'll pay cash when I arrive" — per the classifier's own documented fail condition, confirm this **correctly fails with a clear message** when attempted against a `full`-prepayment service that can't skip online payment (this is exactly `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8`'s situation — all 3 services are `full` — making it a perfect real-world negative-case business for this one)
- [ ] **`purchase_subscription_checkout`** — assistant-driven subscription purchase — the conversational equivalent of the already-planned `BookPage` subscription radio flow; confirm parity
- [ ] **`explain_why_stripe_required`** — a pure explanatory intent; confirm the answer is business-accurate (mentions this business's actual policy, not boilerplate) and, for `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8`, correctly explains why cash isn't offered given all-`full` services
- [ ] **`receipt_status`** — "what's my receipt status" / order lookup by conversation — confirm this correctly reflects a real completed payment's state once one exists
- [ ] **`confirm_stripe_payment`** — **the most important one to test precisely.** Source-confirmed (`ai-payments.logic.ts:1763-1793`) that this requires a `sessionId` param and calls `bookingPaymentService.confirmCheckoutSession(slug, sessionId)` — the exact same backend method the checkout-return page (`consumer-checkout-return.util.ts`) calls. Cases: (a) ask "did my payment go through" with an active `pendingCheckoutSessionId` already in assistant context (seen in `ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx`'s `assistantContext` — should auto-resolve `sessionId` from context, no clarification needed); (b) ask with NO pending checkout in context — confirm it asks to clarify (`missing: ['sessionId']`) rather than crashing or guessing; (c) confirm a session that's already been confirmed once (idempotency, cross-reference the double-confirmation case in the online-payment plan); (d) confirm a session for someone else's payment (auth boundary — should this even be checkable cross-customer?)
- [ ] **`apply_gift_card_code`** — redeem a gift-card code by conversation, parity check against the account-page redemption UI already tested (and its raw-error-string bug, e2e-bug.3)
- [ ] **`check_gift_card_balance`** — read-only balance lookup by conversation
- [ ] **`buy_gift_card`**, **`buy_gift_card_physical`**, **`buy_gift_card_for_someone`** — three related but distinct gift-card-purchase intents; confirm each correctly routes to gift-card checkout with the right prefill via `parseGiftCardAssistantPrefill` (`buyAsGift`, `recipientName`, `recipientEmail`, `deliveryMethod`, `amount` — all 5 fields, not just some). **Regression-critical**: once the assistant navigates here, it lands on the exact page with **e2e-bug.6**'s infinite-loop bug — confirm this is fixed before/while testing, otherwise these 3 cases can't complete
- [ ] **`get_gift_card_quote`** — price a gift card by conversation before committing

#### Compound / multi-step payment prompts

- [ ] `isPaymentsCompoundPrompt` — a single prompt combining multiple payment actions (e.g., "book the 2pm slot and pay online") — confirm the compound splitter correctly segments this into sequential actions rather than misclassifying as one
- [ ] `guest_pay_cash_manage` compound (referenced in `ai-cash-payment-checkout.util.ts` as an explicit NOT-case for `pay_cash_at_visit`) — a guest (non-signed-in) books, chooses cash, AND asks for an emailed manage-link, all in one prompt — this is a genuinely different intent from any single one above and needs its own dedicated multi-part case
- [ ] `pay_at_venue_fallback` (also referenced as a distinct NOT-case) — mid-checkout switch FROM online TO cash ("pay at salon instead", "skip online payment") — confirm this is only accepted where `acceptCashPayments` allows it, and correctly rejected/explained where it doesn't (e.g., `pollin-clinic-3b7fb9d8`'s `full`-mode services)

- [ ] Single-service navigate (`buildPublicAssistantCheckoutNavigate` returns `path: 'checkout'`) — confirm query params (`serviceId`, `startTime`, `employeeId`) land correctly on `BookPage`'s checkout step, prefilled, not requiring re-selection
- [ ] Multi-service navigate (same function, `path: 'multi/checkout'` when `serviceIds.length > 1`) — same prefill check for the multi-service checkout page

#### Locale variance

- [ ] Re-run at least the `choose_payment_method` and `pay_cash_at_visit` intents in `hy` and `ru` — the classifier fixture file structure throughout this codebase consistently ships multilingual variants for every intent; confirm the same prompts work in both, and that the reply text itself is actually translated (not just correctly classified)

#### Cross-cutting

### e2e-test-plan.consumer-app-remaining-gaps — Closing out toward full coverage

Final gap-filling pass at the user's request to push consumer-app coverage as close to 100% as planning can get. Found genuinely new, previously-unplanned surface area by reading `hooks/use-deep-link-router.ts`, `hooks/use-consumer-one-tap-sign-in.ts`, `hooks/use-home-screen-widget-sync.ts`, and `lib/phone-auth.util.ts` — none of which were touched by any prior plan section.

#### Structural note: native-only features are un-testable via the browser tool used for every prior test pass this session

`use-deep-link-router.ts` opens with `if (!Capacitor.isNativePlatform()) return;` — the entire deep-link router (6 distinct URL patterns), native push, and the home-screen-widget sync below are **gated off entirely in a browser**, meaning nothing tested so far via `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` could have exercised any of them, regardless of how thoroughly the rest of the app was clicked through. This whole category needs an actual iOS/Android device or simulator with a real Capacitor native build, not just the web dev server — worth flagging as a hard methodology limit, not a "case to add," before listing the cases themselves.

- [ ] **Checkout-return deep link** (native `optischedule://` URLs) for all 3 native-scheme kinds (package/multi/gift-card) actually opening the app fresh (cold start) vs. resuming it (warm) — the router's `getLaunchUrl()` vs. `appUrlOpen` listener are two different Capacitor APIs for exactly this distinction
- [ ] **Manage-booking deep link** (`parseManageBookingRoute`) — tapping a manage-link from a real SMS/email/WhatsApp notification opens the app directly to `ManageBookingPage` with the right booking+token
- [ ] **Lab-booking-request deep link** and **result-ready deep link** (`parseLabBookingRequestRoute`, `parseResultReadyRoute`) — clinic-vertical-specific notifications; out of scope for non-clinic test businesses per the earlier explicit decision, but the routing logic itself still needs a clinic-vertical business eventually
- [ ] **Plain tenant-slug deep link** — a bare share link (`parseTenantSlugFromUrl`) opening straight to that salon's home
- [ ] **Deferred-slug-after-install flow** (`stashSlugForInstall`/`consumeDeferredSlug`) — this is the actual mechanism behind `frontend`'s `/get-app/[slug]` handoff page found earlier: a customer without the app taps a web link, gets redirected to the app store, installs, and on first native launch (no launch URL from the OS) the app should still resolve the originally-intended salon from storage. This is a multi-step, cross-app-boundary flow that's easy to get wrong and hasn't been tested even conceptually until now.
- [ ] **Home-screen widget sync** (`useHomeScreenWidgetSync`, tagged `adopt-4.7`) — iOS WidgetKit / Android App Widget showing a booking snapshot; needs a real device home screen to verify at all, and specifically needs verifying the widget updates when a booking is cancelled/rescheduled/completed, not just on creation

#### Third sign-in method never tested: phone/SMS OTP (only Google was planned before)

`ConsumerSignInProvider = 'google' | 'apple' | 'phone'` (`use-consumer-one-tap-sign-in.ts`) — this session's plans only ever mention Google. Apple and phone are equally real, distinct paths.

- [ ] Phone sign-in happy path — enter phone, receive SMS OTP, enter code, sign in
- [ ] `isValidConsumerPhone`/`normalizeConsumerPhone` — international phone number formats, with/without country code, with formatting characters (spaces, dashes, parens) — confirm normalization is consistent with what the backend expects (cross-check against **api-bug.1**'s area of the codebase generally being fragile around string formats)
- [ ] `sanitizeSmsOtpCode` — OTP entry with extra whitespace/non-digit characters pasted in (common when copy-pasting from an SMS app)
- [ ] Wrong OTP code — error messaging (candidate for yet another e2e-bug.3 instance)

Tested all 3 requested paths:
  - **List-select**: clicking a "Book again" entry (`GevGas operations`) correctly navigates to `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/home`. Clean.
  - **Salon-code field, valid + real slug**: typing `gevgas-operations-7c299253` and clicking Continue correctly navigates to `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/home`. Clean.
  - **Salon-code field, invalid format** (spaces/special chars): Continue button correctly stays disabled the whole time (`isValidSlug` gate). Clean.
  - **Salon-code field, valid format but nonexistent slug ("empty/no-results" case)**: typing `not-a-real-salon-xyz` and clicking Continue navigates to `/s/not-a-real-salon-xyz/home` as expected, but the destination renders a **raw, unhandled error string: "Request failed with status code 404"** — no header, no friendly copy, no way back except browser back. **e2e-bug.20.** Root-caused: `use-tenant-bootstrap.ts:96` — `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Salon not found')`. Axios errors are always `instanceof Error`, so the friendly `'Salon not found'` fallback string is unreachable dead code — every real fetch failure (this one included) shows the raw axios message instead. This is the same root-cause *pattern* as **e2e-bug.15** (raw HTTP-client errors leaking into the UI) but on a much more commonly-hit path — any customer who mistypes a salon code hits this. **Fix direction:** check `axios.isAxiosError(err) && err.response?.status === 404` (or similar) and use the friendly `'Salon not found'` message for that case specifically, reserving raw `err.message` for truly unexpected errors (or better, never showing raw HTTP client messages to end users at all).
  - **Cold hard-load of `/` itself**: no splash/loading state is shown or needed — the page renders instantly and correctly with the "Book again" list already populated from local cache. However, this **also reproduces the "Maximum update depth exceeded" render-loop burst previously documented as e2e-bug.14** — which revises that finding: it is **not** confined to the 6 `SalonTabRoute` pages as originally written, since `WelcomePage` is a completely separate, unrelated component tree and hits the identical error. This points to the true root cause being something at the shared `App.tsx` root (wrapping every single route) rather than anything `SalonTabRoute`/`SalonTabChrome`-specific. Also newly confirmed: watched the error count for several seconds after it fired and it did **not** keep growing — this is a one-time burst of forced re-renders during initial mount that hits React's internal update-depth ceiling and then stabilizes, **not** an indefinitely-ongoing loop as e2e-bug.14 originally described. The page is fully interactive and correct immediately after the burst (confirmed: list-click and code-field navigation both worked perfectly on this same cold-loaded instance). **e2e-bug.14's writeup above should be corrected**: broaden the affected-surface description to "reproduces on `WelcomePage` too, not just the 6 tab routes — likely an `App.tsx`-root-level cause" and soften "spamming the console indefinitely... continuously re-rendering in the background" to "a one-time burst of ~100+ forced re-renders during initial mount, then stabilizes — real but less severe than originally characterized; still worth fixing since it signals a genuine dependency-array bug somewhere in the shared root, and error-log spam alone is bad hygiene."

- [ ] Switching between salons — does customer auth/session correctly scope per-salon (already implied by `consumer_token_${slug}` storage keys seen early this session), with no session bleed between two different businesses open in sequence
- [x] ~~"Save salon" bookmark action — persists across reload? Shows up anywhere else (e.g., a saved-salons list)?~~ — **tested, 1 bug found (**e2e-bug.21 — Fixed**, see Fix log).** Bookmark toggle (`consumer_pinned_salons` in localStorage, shared between `WelcomePage`'s list icons and `SalonHomePage`'s own top-right toggle — both read/write the same key, correctly in sync) persists correctly across a hard reload — confirmed by pinning "GevGas operations," reloading, and seeing the gold-filled bookmark icon still there. **But there is no dedicated "Saved salons" list anywhere in the app** — confirmed via source: `buildWelcomeSalonSections()` (`recent-salons.ts`) computes a `saved` array, but grepping the entire `pages/`+`components/` tree shows it's never rendered anywhere (only `sections.quickReturn` is shown, under "Book again"). **e2e-bug.21 — pinning a salon has no functional effect beyond a decorative icon.** Worse, the final sort in `buildWelcomeSalonSections` is purely by recency timestamp (`salonRecencyTimestamp`), completely ignoring pinned status — a pinned salon does not get sorted to the top, and since the list is capped at `MAX_RECENT = 8` with no pinned-first exception, a saved salon can silently fall off the "Book again" list entirely once 8 *other* salons have been visited more recently, with no fallback screen to find it again. This defeats the ordinary user expectation of what a "save"/bookmark feature does (keep this easy to find later). **Fix direction:** either render `sections.saved` as its own dedicated list somewhere (WelcomePage or Account), or at minimum sort pinned entries first and exempt them from the 8-item cap in `buildWelcomeSalonSections`.
- [x] ~~Language switcher (top-right) — does switching from here propagate to every other tab immediately, or only after reload?~~ — **tested, 1 real bug found (**e2e-bug.22 — Fixed**, see Fix log), confirmed via two independent methods (dispatched `ionChange` event, then a genuine simulated click) to rule out a test-methodology artifact.** On `/s/:slug/home`, switching the language picker (rendered inside `SalonHomePage`, using its own `useConsumerLocale`/`useConsumerCopy` call) correctly and instantly updates its own picker label and the rest of `SalonHomePage`'s static copy — but its sibling `ConsumerRewardsCard` (rendered in the same component, receiving `copy` as a prop from the exact same `useConsumerCopy` call) **kept showing English content ("Rewards & offers," "Your rewards balance," "$5.00 available," "Earn 5% back on eligible visits," "Use these codes when you book:") after switching to Armenian, only updating correctly after a full page reload.** This is a real, reproducible bug, not a one-off. Root cause not fully pinned down — by source inspection `ConsumerRewardsCard` isn't memoized (no `React.memo`), `getConsumerCopy(locale)` is a simple, correct `CATALOG[locale]` dictionary lookup (no caching bug), and it receives `copy` from the identical hook call as the picker that DID update — so the exact mechanism causing this one child to lag remains unclear and would need a React DevTools re-render trace to pin down precisely. **Practical impact confirmed regardless of exact cause: a customer switching languages will see a stale-language rewards/promo card until they reload the page**, i.e. propagation is NOT immediate for at least this component, contrary to what an instant client-side locale switch should do.
- [x] ~~`fromCache` state (seen in `SalonTabRoute` code) — what renders when profile is served from a stale cache vs. fresh?~~ — **tested, 1 real bug found (**e2e-bug.23 — Fixed**, see Fix log), precisely root-caused.** Stopped the backend entirely (`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` confirmed on every request) and reloaded `/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/home` — the page still rendered correctly from cache (business name, description, buttons all present), confirming the caching mechanism itself works. However, **no "viewing cached data" banner ever appeared**, despite the live refresh attempt demonstrably failing. Root-caused via `use-tenant-bootstrap.ts`: `useTenantStore` (Zustand, global, persists across navigations within the same session) already held a fresh profile for this slug from an earlier visit this session, so `hasReadyProfile(slug)` returns `true` at the top of the effect — which takes the `storeReady` branch and explicitly calls `setFromCache(false)`. The subsequent live `fetchPublicProfile(slug)` call fails (backend down) and lands in the `.catch` block, but since `hasReadyProfile(slug)` is *still* true there too, it just `return`s early without ever calling `setFromCache(true)` (that only happens in the `!hasReadyProfile(slug) && cachedSnapshot` branch, which this case never reaches). Net effect: **`fromCache` only ever gets set to `true` on a customer's very first-ever visit to a salon in a given session (when the Zustand store is empty and only the localStorage snapshot exists) — on every subsequent visit within the same session, a failed live refresh is silently swallowed with no indication to the customer that they're looking at potentially-stale data**, which is arguably the *more common* real-world case (customers naturally revisit the same salon's tabs repeatedly). Secondary, related observation: with the backend down, `me/rewards`/`me/bookings`/`providers` requests were seen retrying repeatedly rather than failing once and backing off — worth a closer look at React Query's retry configuration for these queries, though not investigated further here. **Fix direction:** in the `.catch` branch, also call `setFromCache(true)` whenever the live fetch fails, regardless of whether `hasReadyProfile` was already true — the banner should reflect "is the data I'm showing right now verified-fresh," not just "was this literally the first load."

#### Referral / sharing mechanics depth

- [x] ~~Actual native share-sheet invocation from "Share link"/"Send invite" (previously only confirmed these buttons are visually present, never that they trigger anything) — confirm the shared content/URL is well-formed and includes the correct referral code~~ — **confirmed clean, no bug.** Monkey-patched `navigator.clipboard.writeText` before clicking "Send invite" (this browser has no `navigator.share`, so it correctly takes the clipboard fallback) and captured the exact copied string: `"Հրավիրեք ընկերներ — GevGas operations-ում երկուսդ էլ կստանաք պարգևներ։\nhttp://localhost:3000/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253?ref=C0AD5D15&src=referral"`. Cross-checked `C0AD5D15` against the live `GET /me/referral` response fired moments earlier — exact match, and the URL is byte-for-byte identical to that response's own `shareUrl` field. Traced why this is reliable: `ConsumerAccountGrowthCard.tsx`'s `onRefer` (line 108-117) explicitly passes `shareUrl: program.shareUrl` (the real, already-fetched server value) into `shareReferralInvite`, which only falls back to a client-side-derived code (`deriveReferralCode`, `consumer-growth-loops.util.ts:19-22`) when `shareUrl` is absent — confirmed via the backend (`referral-program.service.ts:77-87`) that `shareUrl` is always populated deterministically alongside `referralCode` in every successful response, so that fallback path is realistically dead code in the real button flow. Also confirmed the frontend's `deriveReferralCode` and backend's `deriveReferralCodeFromCustomerId` use the byte-identical derivation (`customerId.replace(/-/g,'').slice(0,8).toUpperCase()`), so even the fallback path (if ever hit) would produce a code consistent with what the backend expects.
- [x] ~~Referral attribution end-to-end: customer A shares their link → customer B opens it as a guest → B signs up → confirm A gets credited, matching the already-tested `claimReferralCode`/`claimPendingReferralAfterSignIn` API-level behavior but now through the real share → open → signup path~~ — **the guest-capture half is confirmed clean; the full "B signs up" half couldn't be completed (needs a second real Google account, same constraint as the original Google Sign-In testing) — but tracing the two eligibility checks end-to-end surfaced a real, precisely-diagnosed new bug, e2e-bug.48.** Tested the reachable half live: cleared `consumer_pending_referral:gevgas-operations-7c299253`, then navigated directly to the real captured share URL's path+query (`/s/gevgas-operations-7c299253/services?ref=ZZTESTCODE&src=referral`) — `captureReferralFromSearch` correctly saved `"ZZTESTCODE"` to localStorage (uppercased, trimmed). Edge case also tested: a too-short code (`?ref=AB`, 2 chars) is correctly rejected by the `ref.length < 4` guard (`consumer-referral.util.ts:63`) and never saved — confirmed via the same localStorage check returning `null`. **e2e-bug.48 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: a customer who attaches a friend's referral code to their account *after* already having completed a prior booking can successfully "attach" it, but the referrer's reward will then silently and permanently never fire, with no error surfaced to either party.** Root-caused by comparing the two eligibility checks in `referral-program.service.ts`, which use disconnected criteria: `claimReferralCode()` (lines 102-152) only checks the program is enabled, the code is valid, the referee has never had a referrer attached before (`readReferredByCustomerId`), and it isn't a self-referral — **it has no check at all on how many bookings the referee has already completed.** But `processBookingCompleted()` (lines 154-226), which is what actually pays out the referrer's reward, requires `priorCompleted === 1` (line 190, `if (priorCompleted !== 1) return { converted: false, reason: 'not_first_completion' }`) — i.e., the referee's *very first-ever completed booking* must be the one that triggers conversion. Since attaching a code doesn't require zero prior bookings, a real, reachable path exists: an established customer with e.g. 5 completed bookings signs out, opens a friend's referral link (or has one already pending from before), signs back in with the same account — `claimPendingReferralAfterSignIn` → `claimReferralCode` succeeds (`attached: true`, since this customer has never had a referrer attached) — but every one of their future bookings will keep failing the `priorCompleted !== 1` check forever (it only grows from here), so the referrer's reward can never fire, and neither the referee (who just "successfully" attached a code) nor the referrer (whose invite silently produced nothing) ever sees any indication of this. **Fix direction:** either gate `claimReferralCode` on the referee having zero prior completed bookings at attach-time (reject with a clear reason like `'not_eligible_existing_customer'`, matching the reward mechanic's actual intent), or drop the reward mechanic's `priorCompleted === 1` requirement in favor of something consistent with the attach-time rule (e.g., "first booking after code attached," not "first booking ever") — the two checks need to agree on what "referral-eligible" means. Lower-confidence, not pursued further: `resolveReferrerCustomerId` (`referral-program.service.ts:276-`) matches referral codes by comparing the first-8-hex-chars of customer UUIDs *scoped to one business* — a theoretical collision risk between two customers of the *same* business, but with a per-business candidate pool this small, the practical probability is negligible and not worth chasing further without a concrete repro.

Planning pass only (per explicit request — build the plan first, execute in later turns). `provider-app` is the individual staff/provider's own mobile app: calendar, schedule, patient chart, lab tasks, retail POS, gift-card fulfillment, reviews, push notifications, and its own AI assistant — **never tested this session until now**. Grounded in a real inventory, not a generic template: read every page under `src/pages/` (14 real pages + 1 spec file), `App.tsx`'s full route table, and grepped all ~75 `api.*(...)` call sites across 38 files (this app has no centralized endpoint catalog like `consumer-app`'s `public-api.ts` — calls are scattered per-page/hook, same structural note as `frontend`). Two view modes exist throughout and must be tested in **both**: `provider` (an individual staff member, own bookings/tasks only) and `team` (`owner`/`admin`/`manager` roles, sees everyone's — `provider-access.ts`'s `MOBILE_MANAGER_ROLES`/`isTeamView`). Structure below: (A) page-by-page E2E, (B) full API endpoint sweep by module, (C) cross-cutting/native concerns, (D) edge cases specific to this app's high-stakes actions (PHI, payments, irreversible visit-status transitions).

No bugs found.** Tested against a real `GET .../provider/profile` call with a freshly-issued real token: **tampered signature** (mutated last 2 chars) → `401`; **no token** → `401`; **malformed bearer** (`garbage.garbage.garbage`) → `401`; **expired token** (hand-signed with the known dev `JWT_SECRET`, `exp` set 1h in the past) → `401` — all via the same generic `{"statusCode":401,"message":"Unauthorized"}`, correctly never leaking why. **Forged-claim IDOR check (the more realistic "wrong business" attack than a literal customer-login attempt, since customers authenticate through an entirely separate `consumer-app` OTP/session mechanism, not this `users`/password table)**: hand-signed a token with the *real* dev secret, keeping the QA Tester's real `sub`/`email` but swapping `businessId` to a different real business (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`) the account has no membership in — correctly rejected with `403 {"message":"You do not have access to this business"}`, confirming the backend re-validates real `BusinessMember` rows server-side rather than trusting the JWT's `businessId` claim at face value. This is real defense-in-depth (a compromised-but-still-correctly-scoped token can't be replayed against a different tenant just by editing the claim, since altering it invalidates the signature, and a same-secret-forged token still gets caught by the membership re-check). `POST /auth/google` and `.../reset-password` were reviewed by source only (not live-exercised, since they need a real Google OAuth round-trip / real email delivery respectively) — both route through the same `buildAuthResponse`/membership-summary path already proven correct above.

A direct bypass attempt — `POST .../reassign` targeting that employee directly, skipping the options list — was also correctly rejected server-side (`409`), confirming the mutation endpoint has its own real validation and doesn't just trust whatever the client submits from the options list (the specific rejection reason surfaced was "no schedule configured" rather than "conflicting booking," since the test employee had no working-hours schedule set up at all — but this still proves a real server-side check exists, not just client-side filtering). ## consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 — Customer-surface AI commands full test plan, A to Z (planning pass)

Planning pass only, per explicit request — build the plan first, execute in later turns. Scope: every AI intent reachable by a **customer** (a real signed-in consumer-app/web user) or an **anonymous public visitor** (the `/book/[slug]` web flow or a guest with no account) — not dashboard-only or provider-mobile-only intents. Grounded in a full registry inventory (not guessed): the master registry (`ai-command-registry.build.ts`, `INTENT_BINDING_SEEDS`/`LEGACY_CORE_BINDINGS`) is **data-driven** — `CUSTOMER_INTENTS`/`PUBLIC_INTENTS`/`*_MUTATING_INTENTS` are computed from seed bindings, not a hand-maintained list — so the authoritative per-intent surface/mutating-status source for any single test is `resolveIntentSurfaces(id)` / the seed block itself, not this document's summary.

**Architecture notes that shape how this whole plan must be executed (read before testing anything):**
1. **Two endpoints, one shared classifier core.** Signed-in customers hit `CustomerAiCommandService` (native intents) which **delegates** 14 discovery/anonymous-booking intents (`PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` — `list_providers`, `list_services`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, `check_availability`, `explain_provider_availability`, `recommend_specialists`, `business_info`, `book_appointment`, `booking_help`, `preview_multi_service_cart`, `list_public_promotions`, `list_provider_reviews`, `suggest_package_block`) into `PublicBookingAssistantService.chat()`. Anonymous visitors hit `POST /public/:slug/assistant` (`assistantMode: 'guide'|'act'`) directly — no separate REST route per intent, one chat endpoint for everything.
2. **No swipe-to-confirm on customer/public surfaces** — that's a dashboard/provider-only UI convention. The **only** customer intent with an explicit two-turn confirm is `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`: first call returns `requiresConfirmation: true` + a preview list of what would be cancelled; the follow-up call must carry `params.confirm === true` to actually execute. Every other mutating customer intent (including `cancel_my_booking`) executes on a single classified turn — **this is itself the highest-priority thing to test**: does a single ambiguous or ordinary-sounding sentence ever accidentally fire an irreversible mutation with zero safety net?
3. **No ReAct/LLM-based replanning on customer or public surfaces.** `ReactBookingAgentService`/`BookingCommandGraphService` are wired only into the **dashboard** controller (`JwtAuthGuard`-gated `ai-command.controller.ts`) — confirmed via import grep that neither `customer-ai-command.service.ts` nor `public-booking-assistant.service.ts` reference them. All customer/public ambiguity resolution is deterministic rule-based `rescueIntent()` — do not expect a compound/ambiguous prompt to get "figured out" via multi-step LLM reasoning the way a dashboard prompt might; a prompt the deterministic rescue can't match will fall to `unknown`, not a smarter fallback.
4. **Guest-token intents bypass JWT auth entirely.** `bookings/manage*` REST endpoints (`GET bookings/manage`, `POST bookings/manage/cancel`/`reschedule`/`package/cancel`/`package/reschedule`) have **no** `@UseGuards` — they authenticate purely via `{bookingId, token}`. Contrast `/me/bookings/:id/...` endpoints, which require `PublicCustomerAuthGuard`. The AI-side guest intents (`explain_manage_booking_context`, `cancel_booking_with_token`, `reschedule_booking_with_token`, `cancel_package_visit_with_token`, `reschedule_package_visit_with_token`, plus the `guest_manage_visit`/`guest_book_and_manage`/`guest_pay_cash_manage` compounds) must be tested **without any Authorization header** — only the booking's own manage-link token.
5. **Shared vs customer-only rescue routing.** Per `CUSTOMER_PUBLIC_RESCUE_ROUTING` (`ai-capability.matrix.ts:458-487`): "shared discovery" prompts (budget search, provider ranking, OR-style availability) are documented and expected to rescue identically whether sent to the anonymous `/public/:slug/assistant` endpoint or the signed-in customer endpoint. "Customer-only" domains (account, payments, packages, clinic self-service, adoption/rewards) are wired to rescue **only** on the customer path — sending an account/payment/cancel prompt to the anonymous public endpoint should never rescue or execute; if it does, that's a real security-boundary bug, not a feature.
6. **Confirmed classifier-fixture gaps to prioritize** (from `ai-registry-nl-fixture-coverage.build.ts` cross-reference, not naive grepping — some domains bundle multiple intents' HY/RU fixtures into one shared file, so a missing standalone file ≠ zero coverage; verify via the repo's own coverage tool before concluding a gap is real): **`cancel_my_booking`** (15 EN prompts, **0 HY / 0 RU**), **`reschedule_my_booking`** (~15 EN, **0 HY / 0 RU**), **`reschedule_package_lines`** (no multilingual file found), **`get_manage_link`** (only 1 HY + 1 RU total — thin), **`suggest_package_block`** (5 EN, no multilingual), **`list_provider_reviews`** (4 EN, no multilingual). These are the two highest-traffic *mutating* booking-lifecycle intents (cancel/reschedule) with a confirmed zero-multilingual gap — start here.
7. **Test mechanics**: drive prompts through the real UI (`ConsumerBookingAssistant.tsx` in `consumer-app`, or the `/book/[slug]` web equivalent) wherever possible so classification + dispatch + UI rendering are all exercised together, not just the raw API; fall back to direct `POST /public/:slug/assistant` curl calls only for surface-boundary/security tests where the UI itself would prevent constructing the request (e.g. testing an account intent with no session).
