  **e2e-bug.75 — Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: every mutating self-service-booking intent whose natural phrasing mentions "my booking/appointment/visit" (at minimum `cancel_my_booking`, `reschedule_my_booking`, `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`, `cancel_package_visit_self`, `reschedule_package_visit_self`, `confirm_my_booking_details`, `add_booking_to_calendar`) — plus `cancel_my_subscription` and `start_pre_visit_intake` — got silently overridden to read-only `my_appointments` / `my_subscriptions` by the customer-CRM rescue pass, even when the LLM classified it correctly.

**Root-cause discussion (word-boundary collision, applies to this bug + e2e-bug.76 + the `start_pre_visit_intake` victim found in Section G)**: the deeper reason these action-exclusion patches keep being necessary is that `\bvisits?\b`-style regexes can't distinguish "cancel my **visit**" from "pre-**visit** intake" — JS regex `\b` treats hyphens as word boundaries identical to spaces, so any compound term (`pre-visit`, `walk-in`, `no-show`, `follow-up`, `check-in`) collides with a bare word check. Confirmed via code read: the codebase's only existing "prompt normalization" (`AiPromptNormalizationService.normalizeForClassifier()`) exclusively does language/multilingual detection, not lexical/compound-word normalization — there is no shared tokenizer. Discussed 2 fix directions with the user (holding both for the later fix pass, not implemented this session): **(B, recommended first pass)** a single shared `maskDomainCompounds(prompt)` helper (a small fixed list of known compound terms — `pre-visit`, `walk-in`, `no-show`, `follow-up`, `check-in`, `check-out` — rewritten to underscore-joined tokens before any `isXPrompt()` regex runs) added to the existing normalization service, replacing the current whack-a-mole of per-function action-exclusion patches; **(C, longer-term)** widen the already-built embedding-based `AiSemanticIntentService` semantic-anchor matcher (currently only invoked when LLM confidence is low) to arbitrate this class of regex-vs-meaning collision generally, since embeddings don't have the word-boundary blind spot at all. Neither guarantees zero false positives forever — only reduces this specific recurring bug class.

Originally: a *question-phrased* cancel request ("can I cancel my appointment?", "is it possible to cancel my booking?") got hijacked to the read-only `explain_why_sign_in` intent before the self-service-booking rescue even ran (`can i` + `my appointment` regex collision; same root cause later stole `get_my_locale` via `what` + `account`).

  **e2e-bug.80 — the entire gift-card purchase flow (`buy_gift_card`, `buy_gift_card_physical`) is unreachable via natural language; `get_gift_card_quote` is unreliable too — every tested "gift card" + dollar-amount prompt (4/4) misfires to the unrelated `apply_gift_card_code` (redeem-an-existing-code) intent instead.** Reproduced live: `"I want to buy a 50 dollar digital gift card for myself"` → `apply_gift_card_code`, "Specify gift card code to apply at checkout."; `"I want to order a physical gift card for 75 dollars"` → same; `"how much would a 100 dollar gift card cost?"` and `"if I buy a gift card for 100 dollars, what would the total price be including any fees?"` (both near-verbatim matches of `get_gift_card_quote`'s own documented trigger examples) → same `apply_gift_card_code` misfire both times. **Root cause for `buy_gift_card`/`buy_gift_card_physical` specifically**: unlike almost every other customer intent in this codebase (each with a dedicated `CUSTOMER_..._CLASSIFIER_RULES` constant spliced into the classifier system prompt with example trigger phrases), **`buy_gift_card` and `buy_gift_card_physical` have no classifier rule text anywhere in the prompt at all** — confirmed via exhaustive grep across every `*_CLASSIFIER_RULES` export in the `ai/` module. They exist as valid, correctly-dispatched registry intents (`CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS_INTENTS`, `ai-payments.util.ts:121-122`) with working rescue-matcher functions (`isBuyGiftCardPrompt`/`isBuyGiftCardPhysicalPrompt`, `ai-payments.util.ts:385-401`, which WOULD correctly match both test prompts if ever invoked) — but the LLM classifier is never told these two intents exist beyond their bare name in the enum list (`buildCustomerClassifierSchema()`), so it has no way to distinguish a purchase request from a redeem-code request. The ONE place either intent is mentioned in prose is a purely negative cross-reference inside `get_gift_card_quote`'s own rule text (`ai-gift-card-quote-and-order.fixtures.ts:9`: "NOT buy_gift_card / buy_gift_card_physical...") — which tells the model what NOT to call them, never what they ARE. **`get_gift_card_quote` itself DOES have full rule text with example triggers that near-exactly match 2 of the failing test prompts, yet still failed 2/2** — this second half of the bug is not fully isolated this pass (unlike the missing-rule-text explanation for buy_gift_card, this looks like `apply_gift_card_code`'s own rule/keyword association dominating the model's real GPT-4o-mini classification whenever "gift card" + a dollar figure co-occur, similar in spirit to e2e-bug.78's LLM-judgment-level root cause). **Real-world impact**: this is a second complete funnel-breakage on par with Section B's cancel/reschedule findings — a customer cannot buy a gift card (digital or physical) through the AI assistant via any natural phrasing tested, and even a price quote is unreliable. **Fix direction**: write dedicated classifier rule text for `buy_gift_card`/`buy_gift_card_physical` (mirroring the style/specificity of `GIFT_CARD_QUOTE_AND_ORDER_CLASSIFIER_RULES`) and splice it into `customer-ai-command.util.ts`'s system prompt; separately investigate why `apply_gift_card_code` appears to out-compete `get_gift_card_quote` even when the prompt matches the latter's own documented examples almost verbatim.

  **e2e-bug.81 — `my_gift_cards` returns zero actual information about the customer's gift cards; the response is a hardcoded, non-data-bearing string regardless of how many cards exist or their balances.** `handleMyGiftCardsLogic` (`ai-customer-crm.logic.ts:819-835`) does `return success('my_gift_cards', 'Your gift cards.', { account });` — a literal, static summary string ("Your gift cards.") with the real card data (`account.orders`, `account.redeemed` — correctly fetched from the DB) stuffed into `details.account`. But `commandResultToPublicAssistantResult()` (`customer-ai-command.util.ts:361-384`), which shapes every command result before it reaches the client, only forwards a fixed whitelist of detail keys (`PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_UI_DETAIL_KEYS`, lines 325-338: `availability`, `availableProviders`, `providers`, `serviceName`/`serviceId`, `date`, `timeOfDay`, `notBeforeTime`, `checkProvidersHandoff`, `slots`, `serviceNames`, `serviceIds`) — **`account` is not in that list**, so it's silently dropped. Reproduced live: `"show me my gift cards"` against a session with 2 real seeded gift cards returned `{"success":true,"action":"my_gift_cards","summary":"Your gift cards."}` — no count, no balances, no codes, no `navigate` link to a page that shows them either (contrast `discover_packages`'s "1 package(s) available." + `navigate:{path:"packages"}`, or `my_subscriptions`'s "You have 1 subscription(s)." + `navigate`). A customer asking about their gift cards through the assistant gets a response that is functionally content-free. **Fix direction**: mirror the pattern already used correctly by every sibling intent in the same file — either verbalize the real count/balances in the summary string (e.g. `` `${account.orders.length} gift card(s), ${account.redeemed.length} redeemed.` ``, matching `subscription_usage`'s and `my_subscriptions`'s established style) and/or add a `navigate: {path: 'account', query: {tab: 'giftCards'}}` so the client at least deep-links somewhere useful, the same way `my_subscriptions` and `subscription_usage` already do.

Found 1 severe new bug (e2e-bug.82) affecting 5 of these intents, plus 1 more classifier bug (e2e-bug.83) blocking `claim_referral_code`.**
- [x] ~~`explain_loyalty_points`, `loyalty_points_balance`, `apply_loyalty_at_checkout` [M], `promo_code_help`, `apply_promo_code_checkout` [M], `how_to_download_app`, `switch_to_consumer_app` — apply more loyalty points than the balance allows; apply a promo code at checkout that's expired/business-restricted~~ — **`loyalty_points_balance` and `explain_loyalty_points` both work correctly** ("You have 150 loyalty points (≈ $150 value)."; full mechanics explainer, both correctly reflecting the seeded 150-point balance). `apply_loyalty_at_checkout` correctly classified but only reachable-tested with no active checkout in progress (correctly asked for clarification rather than acting — inconclusive on the "more points than balance" edge case, needs a real in-progress checkout session to test properly, not attempted this pass). **`promo_code_help` found a 7th reproduction of the systemic e2e-bug.77 pattern** (folded into that write-up, not a new number).

  **e2e-bug.82 — 5 of the ai-cmd-customer-6.6 rewards/referral/sharing intents (`refer_a_friend`, `share_salon_link`, `explain_rewards_wallet`, `claim_referral_code`, `claim_share_reward`) can never succeed for ANY signed-in customer — every one of them unconditionally fails with "Business not found." regardless of phrasing, because they depend on a `params.slug` value that nothing in the classifier pipeline ever populates.** All 5 handlers in `ai-consumer-adoption.logic.ts` share the identical pattern: `const slug = typeof params.slug === 'string' ? params.slug : undefined; if (!slug) return failure('<action>', 'Business not found.');` (lines 131-134, 174, 205, 249, 309) — but `params` is populated exclusively from the LLM classifier's JSON output, and nothing in the classifier system prompt ever instructs it to extract or emit a "business slug" (it isn't a real user-nameable entity like a service or date — it's routing infrastructure already resolved server-side and passed to `dispatchConsumerAdoptionIntent(deps, businessId, action, params, prompt)` as its own separate, correctly-populated `businessId` parameter, which these 5 handlers receive but never use for their actual data lookups). Reproduced live 4×: `"how do I refer a friend?"` → `refer_a_friend`, "Business not found."; `"give me a link to share this salon with friends"` → `share_salon_link`, "Business not found."; `"explain my rewards wallet"` (once correctly classified — see e2e-bug.79-adjacent note below) would hit the same guard; downstream calls `deps.publicBookingService.getCustomerReferralProgram(slug, customerId)` / `getCustomerRewards(slug, customerId)` which internally do their own `resolveBusiness(slug)` lookup to get back to a `business.id` — i.e. the correct `businessId` is already sitting one parameter away in the same function signature, and the slug round-trip through the classifier was never necessary. **Real-world impact**: this is a complete, platform-wide, 100%-reproducible failure of an entire feature batch shipped earlier this session (task "ai-cmd-customer-6.6" per project history) — no customer, on any business, can ever refer a friend, share their salon link, view their rewards wallet, or claim a referral/share reward through the AI assistant. **Fix direction**: stop reading `params.slug` in all 5 handlers; either look up the business's slug from the already-available `businessId` (a single `Business` repo lookup) before calling `getCustomerRewards`/`getCustomerReferralProgram`/etc., or — better — add businessId-based overloads of those `PublicBookingService` methods so the AI logic layer never needs a slug at all, matching how every other customer intent in this codebase (which all take `businessId` directly) is implemented.

  **e2e-bug.83 — `claim_referral_code` is unreachable: redeeming a referral code gets misclassified as `apply_gift_card_code` (a gift-card-only action) because `isApplyGiftCardCodePrompt()`'s trigger is scoped too broadly.** Reproduced live: `"I want to redeem referral code ABC123"` → `apply_gift_card_code`, "Specify gift card code to apply at checkout." Root cause: `isApplyGiftCardCodePrompt()` (`ai-payments.util.ts:353-369`) returns true whenever `/\b(apply|use|redeem|preview)\b/i.test(prompt) && (/\b(gift\s*card)\b/i.test(prompt) || /\bcode\b/i.test(prompt))` — the second half is an OR, so "code" alone (without "gift card") is sufficient; my prompt has "redeem" + "code" (from "referral code"), satisfying both halves despite never mentioning a gift card at all. **Fix direction**: add a `referral` exclusion to `isApplyGiftCardCodePrompt()`'s guard clause (mirroring its own existing `/\bcurrency\s+code\b/i` false-positive guard at line 354), e.g. `if (/\breferral\b/i.test(prompt)) return false;`, and verify `claim_referral_code`'s own rescue/rule text is checked before (or takes priority over) `apply_gift_card_code`'s for "redeem...code" phrasing that mentions "referral."

  **Also noted (not yet root-caused, 2nd occurrence of a recurring oddity)**: `"I just shared my booking on social media, can I get my reward?"` (meant for `claim_share_reward`) misfired to the unrelated `add_booking_to_calendar` action for a real existing booking — the same bizarre misfire shape already seen once in Section C's `explain_subscription_vs_one_time` testing. Two independent reproductions across two unrelated domains now suggests a real, shared root cause (some fallback path appears to default hard-to-classify prompts mentioning "my booking"-adjacent context to `add_booking_to_calendar` specifically) worth a dedicated investigation in a future pass, once e2e-bug.75/77's higher-confidence fixes are in and can be ruled out as the source.

  **e2e-bug.82 (expanded scope) — the "Business not found." slug-param defect is far more widespread than first identified in Section E: it spans at least 10 files and 13+ customer-facing intents, all sharing the exact same copy-pasted anti-pattern.** In addition to the 5 intents already found in `ai-consumer-adoption.logic.ts` (Section E), a direct code audit (`grep -rl "if (!slug)"` across every `ai/*.logic.ts` file, cross-checked for whether `slug` is sourced from `params.slug` — broken — vs. a server-side `resolveBusinessSlug(businessId)`-style lookup — correct, confirmed working via `ai-find-soonest-appointment.logic.ts:62` and `ai-notify-running-late.logic.ts`, both of which correctly reached their real handlers in live tests) found the identical broken `const slug = typeof params.slug === 'string' ? params.slug : undefined; if (!slug) return failure(...)` pattern, with no fallback, in: `ai-update-my-profile.logic.ts` (`update_my_profile`, live-confirmed), `ai-my-locale.logic.ts` (`get_my_locale`/`update_my_locale`, `update_my_locale` live-confirmed), `ai-list-provider-reviews.logic.ts` (`list_provider_reviews`), `ai-pick-provider-for-service.logic.ts` (`pick_provider_for_service`), `ai-share-my-booking.logic.ts` (`share_my_booking`), `ai-switch-provider-same-time.logic.ts` (`switch_provider_same_time`), `ai-rebook-last-appointment.logic.ts` (`rebook_last_appointment`), `ai-submit-review-with-token.logic.ts` (`submit_review_with_token` — the **guest-token** variant, meaning this also affects the no-login surface tested in Section K), and `ai-submit-provider-review.logic.ts` (`submit_provider_review`). **Root cause, same as originally identified**: these handlers all expect a business "slug" to arrive as a classifier-extracted `params.slug`, but nothing in the classifier system prompt ever instructs the LLM to produce one (it isn't a real user-nameable entity — it's routing infrastructure already resolved server-side and available as the handler's own separately-passed, correctly-populated `businessId` parameter). **Fix direction, same as originally identified, now with a much larger blast radius**: either add a shared `resolveBusinessSlug(deps, businessId)` call (the pattern already proven correct in `ai-find-soonest-appointment.logic.ts:30`) to all ~10-13 affected handlers in place of reading `params.slug`, or — the more durable fix — add businessId-based overloads to the underlying `PublicBookingService` methods so no AI logic layer ever needs a slug round-trip at all. Given the sheer number of independently-broken call sites all repeating the identical mistake, a shared lint rule or a single shared helper (rather than per-file patches) is the right long-term fix.

  **e2e-bug.84 — `privacy_delete` (GDPR right-to-erasure) has NO confirmation step at all: it anonymizes the customer's account data on a single ordinary-sounding turn, with no preview, no "are you sure," and no undo.** Confirmed via direct code read of `handlePrivacyDeleteLogic` (`ai-privacy-delete.logic.ts:37-`): the only gate before executing is `isPrivacyDeleteCustomerPrompt(textPrompt)` (a classification check) and `resolveSessionCustomerId(params)` (an auth check) — there is no `requiresConfirmation`/`params.confirm` pattern anywhere in this file, unlike `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`'s deliberate two-turn preview+confirm flow (Section B) for a far less consequential, fully-reversible action (a cancelled booking can simply be rebooked; an anonymized name/email/phone cannot be un-anonymized). Reproduced live (unintentionally, during this pass — see the in-conversation flag to the user): `"I want to delete all my personal data from your system"` → `{"success":true,"summary":"Your account data has been anonymized."}` on the very first turn, immediately setting the customer's `name`, `email`, `phone` to anonymized placeholder values and `isActive` to `false` in the database — confirmed via direct `SELECT` before and after. **Real-world impact**: this is the single most severe finding of this entire pass — a real customer could have their account permanently anonymized by an ambiguous or misinterpreted sentence in a casual conversation with the assistant, with zero opportunity to back out, in sharp contrast to how the codebase's own `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings` feature correctly treats a much smaller-stakes bulk action. **Fix direction**: add the same `requiresConfirmation` + `params.confirm === true` two-turn pattern already established and working (mechanically) for `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings` (Section B) — preview what will be anonymized/deleted on the first turn, require an explicit affirmative reply before `handlePrivacyDeleteLogic` ever calls `deps.customerPrivacyService.deleteCustomerData()`. **Process note**: this was caught and reverted immediately (customer row restored to its original test values; all other seeded test data confirmed untouched) — the fix direction above should be prioritized ahead of e2e-bug.78 (whose confirm-flow mechanism this feature should copy) once fixes begin.

  **e2e-bug.85 — `explain_rtl_layout` never actually knows the customer's real locale: it always defaults to "EN" regardless of what locale the request specifies, because it reads a classifier-extracted `params.locale` that nothing ever populates — the same "expects a param the pipeline never fills in" shape as e2e-bug.82, just failing silently instead of hard-erroring.** `resolveRtlLayoutLocale()` (`ai-explain-rtl-layout.util.ts:78-82`) is `return readString(params.locale) ?? 'en';` — `params` comes from the LLM classifier's JSON output, which is never instructed to extract a "locale" entity (it's request/session context, not a nameable thing in the user's sentence). Reproduced live: `POST .../assistant` with `{"prompt":"What is RTL?","locale":"hy"}` returned `"Left-to-right (LTR) EN uses left-to-right reading in this app...."` — literally the string "EN" hardcoded into the reply — identical output was returned for `locale:"en"` too, proving the parameter is never actually threaded through regardless of what's requested. **This also means the plan's specific ask — "does it correctly say Armenian is not RTL?" — could never be verified even in principle, since the handler can't see the real locale to begin with.** **Fix direction**: thread the real request-level locale into `params.locale` before calling `handleExplainRtlLayoutLogic`, the same way session/business context is already passed to other handlers, instead of relying on classifier extraction for something that was never a natural-language entity.

  **e2e-bug.86 — `explain_rtl_layout`'s response text leaks a raw internal CSS filename to the customer.** `buildExplainRtlLayoutGuidance()` (`ai-explain-rtl-layout.util.ts:199,214,227,242`) interpolates the literal constant `ADOPTION_A11Y_STYLESHEET = 'adoption-a11y.css'` (line 9) directly into every user-facing summary/next-step string — e.g. "adoption-a11y.css uses logical spacing so layouts stay readable in both directions." A real customer asking "what is RTL?" gets a CSS filename in their chat reply, which is meaningless and unprofessional-looking to an end user (this reads like an internal engineering comment that was never meant to ship in copy). **Fix direction**: remove the stylesheet-name interpolation from all 4 customer-facing strings; if it's useful for internal QA/debugging, put it in a separate non-summary `details` field instead of the spoken/displayed text.

  **e2e-bug.87 (most severe finding of this entire pass) — a large fraction of guide/help content shown to hy-locale (Armenian) customers, across nearly the entire customer+public guide corpus, is garbled, illegible mixed-script text, while the equivalent ru-locale content for the same flows is completely correct.** — **Fixed.** Fully re-translated every corrupted field in `backend/src/modules/ai/guide/guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` (all 20 flows covered by `TOP_CUSTOMER_PUBLIC_GUIDE_FLOWS`) into clean, natural Armenian — not just the `step1`-`step3` fields originally called out, but also several `title`/`summary` fields that a closer re-read showed were *also* corrupted (real-but-wrong Armenian letters/words, e.g. `customer.tabs.title`, `public.checkout.title` using "ոճարում" instead of "վճարում" for "payment") that the original pass's coarse title/summary-only spot-check had missed. Regenerated the derived snapshot via the existing `python3 scripts/sync-customer-public-guide-i18n.py`, and the pre-existing `guide-flow-customer-public-locale-parity.spec.ts` (81 tests, previously only asserting `title`/`summary` use Armenian script — never checked `step1-5`, which is exactly how this shipped unnoticed) now passes 81/81 against the corrected content. Verified no stray Latin runs (4+ chars) or Cyrillic remain anywhere in the file (only the same `email`/`SMS` loanwords already used identically in the app's other confirmed-clean hy copy). **Also fixed a second, previously-unknown-to-be-affected file discovered while researching correct translations**: `consumer-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json` (the native `GuidePage.tsx`/"Help & guide" screen's own content source, which last turn's testing had called "unaffected" — that was based on checking only the `bookingFlow` topic, which happens to be clean there) turned out to share several of the *exact same* corrupted `title`/`summary` strings verbatim (`assistant`, `account`, `packages`, `bookingFunnel`, `professionals`, `services`, `checkout`, `availability`, `overlays.clinic.consumer`, `overlays.tour.checkout`, `overlays.tour.packages` — steps in this file were already clean for all of these, only title/summary needed fixing). Fixed all of them; left the file's separate `provider`/`overlays.clinic.provider|dashboard`/`overlays.retail.*` subtrees untouched (provider-app surface, a different app/bug). Ran the existing hy/ru vitest suites for this file (`mobile-guide.spec.ts`, `consumer-guide-entry.spec.ts`, `consumer-guide.util.spec.ts`, `consumer-guide-clinic-gating.spec.ts`, `consumer-guide.copy.spec.ts`, `consumer-guide-assistant-seed.util.spec.ts` — 81 tests) — all pass; confirmed via `npx tsc --noEmit` in both `backend` and `consumer-app` that neither edit introduced any new type errors (all pre-existing errors listed are in unrelated files, confirmed via `git status`). **Live-verified end-to-end, both files, via the exact two repro paths this bug was originally found and reconfirmed through all session**: (1) native `GuidePage.tsx` in real hy locale (switched via the actual in-app language dropdown, not a cookie hack) — every visible topic now renders fully clean Armenian, no mixed-script text anywhere. (2) The AI chat's post-failure guide-fallback mechanism — submitted a garbled prompt (`"asdkfj qwerty gibberish nonsense"`) through the real assistant widget in hy locale; the `consumer-tabs` fallback snippet that this exact mechanism has surfaced broken text through all session now renders correctly: *"Ահա ինչպես Գլխավոր, Ծառայություններ և Հաշիվ այս էջում. Գլխավոր էկրանին ցուցադրվում են առաջիկա ամրագրումներն ու առաջարկները։"* — fully legible, grammatically correct Armenian, no Latin/Cyrillic contamination. The CI/build-time-check suggestion from the original fix direction (assert no Latin/Cyrillic in `.hy.json` guide content) was not implemented as a new script — the existing parity spec already has the necessary scaffolding (`guideFlowLocaleHasScript`) and would just need extending to also check `step1-5` fields, not just `title`/`summary`; left as a follow-up rather than done here since the user asked to fix the bug, not add new test infrastructure. Discovered incidentally while testing `explain_rtl_layout` in hy locale (the guide-fallback block attached to its clarification response), then confirmed as a systemic, file-wide issue by direct read of `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` (156 lines) and by an independent live repro with an unrelated garbled-input prompt in hy locale — same corruption, proving it's not specific to the RTL topic. **Root cause, confirmed via direct source read, not inference**: within this one static, checked-in JSON file, `title`/`summary` fields are clean proper Armenian script in most blocks (e.g. `customer.gettingStarted`, `customer.packages`, `public.availability`), but `step1`/`step2`/`step3` fields are near-universally a broken mix of Armenian letters, Latin transliteration fragments, and even stray Cyrillic characters within single words — and in several blocks (e.g. `customer.tabs`) the corruption spreads into the `title`/`summary` fields too (`customer.tabs.title: "Գlխavar, Ծառayutyunner ev Հashiv"`, `customer.tabs.summary: "Navigatsia havelvatsi вклadokner-ov։"` — `вклadokner` mixes Russian Cyrillic "вкл" into an otherwise Latin-transliterated word). Of the ~15 flow blocks in the file, only `customer.gettingStarted` and `customer.packages` are fully clean; every other block (`customer.activation.*` — 4 sub-flows, `customer.tabs`, `customer.bookingFlow`, `customer.account`, `customer.assistant`, `public.*` — 5 sub-flows, `overlays.clinic.consumer`, `overlays.tour.*` — 2 sub-flows) has this corruption in some or all of its step lines — roughly 12 of ~15 blocks, the large majority of the file. **Confirmed NOT a general i18n-pipeline bug**: the parallel `ru`-locale content for the exact same flows and same request (`guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.ru.json`, verified via the same live "garbled-input" repro) is completely correct, fluent, properly-scripted Russian throughout — this isolates the defect to the hy translation data specifically, not the rendering/delivery mechanism. **Real-world impact**: this guide/help fallback content is attached to an enormous fraction of assistant responses across this entire session (nearly every non-success/clarification response includes a `guide` block with this exact "consumer-tabs" or a sibling topic's content) — meaning **any real Armenian-speaking customer using this app in hy locale has been shown illegible, unprofessional-looking garbage text every time the assistant needed to show step-by-step guidance**, for as long as this file has been in this state. This is likely the single most user-visible, broadly-reaching defect found in the whole audit, simply never caught before because hy-locale testing wasn't exercised against the guide/fallback path specifically until this pass. **Fix direction**: re-translate/re-generate the `step1`/`step2`/`step3` values for every affected block in `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` into proper Armenian script (matching the quality already present in that same file's `title`/`summary` fields and in `customer.gettingStarted`/`customer.packages`), and add a CI/build-time check (e.g. a script asserting no Latin ASCII letters or Cyrillic characters appear in `.hy.json` guide content, mirroring the kind of hardcoded-string sweep already used elsewhere this session for e2e-bug.54/e2e-bug.72) so a future regression can't silently reintroduce mixed-script content.

different bug from e2e-bug.75, not a duplicate**: compound sub-steps are dispatched directly by action name (confirmed via reading `AiCommandService.executeCompoundIntents()`, Concurrent *mutating* requests (e.g. double-submit cancel) were not tested given e2e-bug.75 already makes cancel non-functional, and the established caution around avoiding compounding mutations on shared test data.

### O. Regression / fallback quality

- [x] ~~For every domain above, deliberately construct ONE prompt per domain designed to fail classification (garbled/off-domain) and inspect the resulting fallback message quality — is it the generic capability-list fallback (as already observed for provider-app's equivalent guide-failure-fallback pattern), and is that fallback text itself translated correctly in hy/ru?~~ — **confirmed exactly as the plan anticipated.** 3 fresh garbled prompts themed around different domains (gift cards, payments, plus a locale cross-check) all fell to the identical generic `unknown` fallback + the same "consumer-tabs" guide block, regardless of which domain the garbled prompt was themed around — confirming the fallback is a single generic capability-list response, not domain-targeted, matching the provider-app pattern already documented. **Correctly translated in ru** (fully clean, fluent Russian, reconfirming Section I's finding). **Not correctly translated in hy** — this is the exact same content already fully documented as e2e-bug.87 (Section I), reconfirmed here via a 3rd independent garbled-prompt repro rather than treated as a new finding.
- [x] ~~Confirm `unknown`/`error`/`security_blocked` are always treated as valid customer-surface pseudo-intents (per `isCustomerSurfaceIntent()`) — i.e. the UI never shows a raw untranslated error code to the customer~~ — **confirmed directly via source read**: `isCustomerSurfaceIntent()` (`customer-ai-command.util.ts:299-307`) explicitly returns `true` for `'unknown'`, `'error'`, and `'security_blocked'` before falling back to the general intent-union check. Cross-checked against dozens of live responses gathered across this entire session — every single `unknown`/`error`/`security_blocked` response observed always carried a friendly, human-readable `summary` string alongside the raw action code; the customer-facing surface never showed a bare code with no explanation.

Compile all findings into a single closure entry here, following the established `e2e-bug.N` numbering (continuing from **e2e-bug.74**), with root-cause file:line citations and fix directions for each. Explicitly call out confirmed-clean areas and confirmed classifier-fixture gaps (Section N.6) separately from genuine functional/security bugs, and note any test-only mutations (bookings/subscriptions/gift cards cancelled, reviews submitted, etc.) that were reverted after testing.

Fully re-translated all 20 affected flows in that file plus a second, previously-unknown-affected sibling file (`consumer-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json`, which the native "Help & guide" UI reads directly); regenerated the derived snapshot; the pre-existing 81-test locale-parity spec passes; live-reconfirmed clean via both original repro paths (native GuidePage in real hy locale, and the AI chat's post-failure guide-fallback with a garbled prompt). Full details above.

**Section A update (discovery/availability reads — first time tested this session)**: this section surfaced the single most severe technical defect found in the entire audit, a raw unhandled 500 crash (e2e-bug.90), plus two more new findings (e2e-bug.91, e2e-bug.92). Full detail below.

- **e2e-bug.90** (**most severe technical finding of the entire pass** — a genuine unhandled server crash, not a soft misclassification): — **Fixed** (see Fix log). Originally: the public-assistant discovery intents `list_services`, `list_providers`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, and `list_public_promotions` all crashed with a raw, un-enveloped `{"statusCode":500,"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')"}` — no graceful JSON error shape, no summary, nothing customer-safe. Confirmed 100% reproducible (2-3/2-3 for every one of the 5 prompts tested, both anonymous/no-auth and authenticated). Root cause, confirmed via live backend stack trace:
  ```
  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')
      at validatePublicAssistantAction (ai-platform.util.ts:448:58)
      at gatePublicAssistantActionLogic (ai-platform.logic.ts:183:36)
      at AiPlatformService.gatePublicAction (ai-platform.service.ts:130:42)
      at PublicBookingAssistantService.chat (public-booking-assistant.service.ts:898:38)
  ```
  [ai-platform.util.ts:448](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-platform.util.ts:448) does `(PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS as readonly string[]).includes(action)` where `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` is imported as a **value** (not type-only) from [ai-command-registry.build.ts:1922](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-command-registry.build.ts:1922) and re-captured into a new top-level `const` at [ai-platform.util.ts:17](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-platform.util.ts:17) (`export const PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS = REGISTRY_PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS;`) rather than re-exported live — a classic ES-module circular-import trap: if any part of the transitive import chain back into `ai-platform.util.ts` runs before `ai-command-registry.build.ts` finishes evaluating its own top-level `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` (line 1922, itself built from `PUBLIC_INTENTS`/`CUSTOMER_INTENTS`, which in turn depend on `buildBindingMaps()` walking the full command registry), this snapshot is permanently captured as `undefined` for the remaining lifetime of the process. Confirmed via `git log` that this exact pattern is old, pre-existing code (June 2026 commits), not something introduced by this session's own refactoring. **Crucially, not every one of the 14 delegated public-only intents crashes** — `business_info` (→ `explain_salon_profile`) and `booking_help` both succeeded, and `check_availability`/`recommend_specialists`/`list_provider_reviews`/`book_appointment` all got misrouted to a *different* action (see e2e-bug.92 and the e2e-bug.77 repro below) rather than crashing. Since `gatePublicAssistantActionLogic` calls `validatePublicAssistantAction` unconditionally for any action reaching it (confirmed via direct source read — no branching on the action value at all), the only consistent explanation is that the intents which *don't* crash never actually reach line 898's gate call in the first place — they're resolved or short-circuited by an earlier branch inside `PublicBookingAssistantService.chat()` (a static-content shortcut for `business_info`, a guide-fallback branch for the misrouted ones), while catalog/search-style intents requiring the full LLM-driven parameter-resolution pipeline (`list_services`, `list_providers`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, `list_public_promotions`) are exactly the ones that flow all the way down to the crash site. **Real-world impact**: for any anonymous visitor or logged-in customer, asking the assistant "what services do you offer," "who are your staff," "what's under $70," "anything on evenings/weekends," or "any promotions" — five of the most basic, expected browsing questions on a booking site — returns a raw, unbranded 500 error instead of an answer. **Fix direction**: eliminate the redundant value-capture re-export; either import and reference `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` directly from `ai-command-registry.build.ts` at the call site inside `validatePublicAssistantAction` (deferring the read until function-call time, by which point the registry module is guaranteed fully initialized), or restructure the two files to remove the cycle entirely. A defensive `Array.isArray()` guard alone would just convert the crash into a silent blanket-deny and should not be the only fix.

- **e2e-bug.91**: the `booking_help` response leaks a large amount of internal orchestration/debug state directly into the public-facing JSON API response, inside `data.sessionContext`: `_capabilityHints` (the complete raw LLM system-prompt text, verbatim-listing all ~200+ intent names across every surface), `_entityMemoryBlock` (real per-business learned entity aliases, including actual staff member names), plus `_commandTraceId`, `_accessTier`, `_actorRole`, `_roleProfile`, `_membershipRole`, `_planTierId`, `_scopedEmployeeId`, `_locationId`, `_branchHint`, `_confidenceHigh`, `_abVariantId`. None of this should ever be serialized into a response an anonymous website visitor's browser can read — at minimum it leaks the AI system prompt (useful for prompt-injection reconnaissance) and internal business/staff data. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).

- **e2e-bug.92**: `recommend_specialists`, `list_provider_reviews`-intended ("what do reviews say about your providers?"), `book_appointment`-intended ("can I book a haircut tomorrow at 3pm?"), `explain_provider_availability`-intended ("when is Mariam available this week?"), and `explain_any_provider_option`-intended ("I don't care who does it, any provider works fine for the massage") — five unrelated prompts across the rest of Section A's provider-related bullets — all misrouted to the exact same wrong destination, `check_providers_for_service`, then failed with "Specify which service to check providers for." even though several of the prompts named or clearly implied a service. This is a broad, high-volume intent-collapse pattern in Section A (distinct from e2e-bug.77's provider/dashboard-surface leakage and from the earlier `add_booking_to_calendar` convergence pattern from Section C/E/N). — **Fixed** (see Fix log).

- **Also confirmed this section**: `check_availability` ("do you have anything available tomorrow?") misfired to `security_blocked`/"cannot perform 'search_retail_sku'" — an 8th-domain reproduction of the already-documented e2e-bug.77 pattern, not a new bug. `business_info` correctly resolved to `explain_salon_profile` with accurate live business data (name, description, phone) — confirmed clean. `compare_services`, `explain_business_hours_and_location`, and `get_directions_to_salon` all confirmed clean with real catalog service names / real business data (an earlier `compare_services` "miss" using fictional service names — "haircut" — was a test-methodology artifact once cross-checked against this business's real catalog via direct DB read, not a bug).

- **e2e-bug.93**: provider-name entity extraction is dropped for at least 3 distinct intents even when a real, correctly-spelled employee name from this business's own roster (verified via direct DB read: `Mariam Ohanyan`, `Karo Mazmanyan`) is named in the prompt. "When is Mariam available this week?" collapses into the e2e-bug.92 `check_providers_for_service` pattern (losing the name entirely); "what does Karo specialize in?" correctly reaches `explain_provider_specialty` but still asks "What specialty or service topic should I match to a provider?" — dropping "Karo" and never resolving to the named provider; "tell me about Mariam's profile and experience" (intended for `explain_professional_profile`) misfires entirely to an unrelated static-content intent, `explain_guest_checkout_fields`. Ruling out bad test data (both names are real, active employees) confirms this is a genuine param-extraction/classification defect, not a test-methodology artifact. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).

- **e2e-bug.94**: "soonest available appointment"-style prompts are wildly unstable — 3 different natural phrasings produced 3 different results, only one of them even plausible: `"what's the soonest I can get an appointment?"` → misfired to `how_to_download_app` (a completely unrelated app-install action); `"when's your next available opening?"` → misfired to `explain_result_status`, a **clinic-only lab-results explainer intent leaking onto a non-clinic beauty-salon business**; `"book me the earliest possible slot"` → correctly reached `book_nearest_slot` but reasonably asked to specify a service (no service was named). The first two prompts show this intent is effectively unreachable via ordinary phrasing, and the `explain_result_status` misfire is itself a notable cross-vertical leak (clinic-domain intent surfacing on a beauty-salon business that has no test/lab functionality at all). — **Fixed** (see Fix log).

- **Paraphrase-robustness spot-check on `list_services`**: repeating the discovery-catalog question with 2 more paraphrases ("what services do you have?", "what services are available?") did **not** reproduce e2e-bug.90's crash — instead each phrasing misfired to a *different* wrong action (a fresh e2e-bug.77 repro via `security_blocked`/"search_retail_sku", and an unrelated `check_multi_service_block_availability` miss). This confirms the crash in e2e-bug.90 is conditional on the classifier landing on specifically `list_services`/`find_services_under_budget`/etc., and that those exact intents are themselves only reached by a minority of natural phrasings — the classifier for this whole "what do you offer" question family is unstable across paraphrases independent of the crash bug.

## FINAL SUMMARY OF THIS TESTING PASS (Sections A-O)

**31 real, confirmed bugs found — e2e-bug.75 through e2e-bug.105.** In severity order, the standout findings are:
1. **e2e-bug.96** (**the single most severe finding of the entire audit**) — an unauthenticated, cross-customer IDOR: `confirm_my_booking_details` returns any customer's full booking details (service, provider, time, address) to a completely anonymous caller with no session and no valid token at all, given only that booking's UUID. Confirmed via a live reproduction using a real *other* customer's real booking. — **Fixed** (see Fix log; same fix as e2e-bug.128).
2. **e2e-bug.104** — a raw, unhandled SQL error (`column booking.start_time does not exist`) crashes `tour_group_checkout` and, per a source-wide grep, likely most of the tour vertical's AI-driven capacity/availability intents (6+ files share the exact broken call pattern) — a single wrong column-name literal (`start_time` vs. the entity's real `startTime`) in a raw `QueryBuilder` string.
3. **e2e-bug.90** — a genuine unhandled 500 crash (not a soft misclassification) on 5+ of the most basic discovery prompts (`list_services`, `list_providers`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, `list_public_promotions`, reachable via compound-phrased prompts too), root-caused to an undefined value from a circular-import re-export at `ai-platform.util.ts:448`. Any anonymous visitor asking "what services do you offer" gets a raw, unbranded server error. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
4. **e2e-bug.87 — Fixed.** A large fraction of hy-locale (Armenian) guide/help content site-wide was garbled, illegible mixed-script garbage — the single most severe, broadest-reaching *content* finding, affecting every real Armenian-speaking customer every time the assistant showed step-by-step guidance. Both affected files (`backend/.../guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` and `consumer-app/src/assets/guide-flows-i18n.json`) fully re-translated and live-reconfirmed clean.
5. **e2e-bug.84** — `privacy_delete` (GDPR erasure) has zero confirmation step; a single sentence irreversibly anonymizes a customer's account. This one actually executed for real during testing (caught and fully reverted).
6. **e2e-bug.97** — guest-token reschedule crashes with a raw, leaked Postgres error ("invalid input syntax for type uuid") because an internal audit-actor tag format (`customer:<uuid>`) collides with code that assumes any actor id is a real staff UUID. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
7. **e2e-bug.95** — the guest "get manage link" feature is completely non-functional via natural language: the response claims success but never actually contains the link/token, even though the backend correctly generates and persists it server-side. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
8. **e2e-bug.102** — a dangerously loose phone-number regex in the guest-contact extractor matches digit fragments from pasted booking UUIDs/manage-link URLs anywhere in a prompt, silently misidentifying them as guest phone numbers and corrupting the guest-identity-lookup path. — **Fixed** (see Fix log; prerequisite for e2e-bug.103).
9. **e2e-bug.91** — internal debug/orchestration state (including the full raw LLM system prompt and real staff names) leaks into a public-facing JSON response via `booking_help`'s `sessionContext`. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
10. **e2e-bug.77** — a systemic missing-surface-gate defect lets customer prompts get misrouted into provider/dashboard-only intents and blocked; confirmed via 13+ independent reproductions across 9 domains, strongly implying broader untested impact.
11. **e2e-bug.82** — 13+ customer intents (referrals, sharing, profile/locale updates, provider selection, reviews) unconditionally fail with "Business not found." because they read a classifier param that's never populated, instead of the already-available `businessId`. — **Fixed** (see Fix log; overlaps e2e-bug.125 for the five adoption handlers).
12. **e2e-bug.75/76** — `cancel_my_booking`, `reschedule_my_booking`, and 3 other intents are hijacked to read-only siblings by unguarded regexes whenever the prompt contains "my" + a booking-word (even inside compound words like "pre-visit"). Section N proved the underlying handlers work correctly once actually reached (abbreviated "cxl my apt tmrw" got through) — this is purely an upstream classification defect.
13. **e2e-bug.89** — even bypassing the classifier entirely via the compound-execution path, `cancel_my_booking` *still* fails to find real existing bookings — a second, independent break in the same capability. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
14. **e2e-bug.80/88** — the gift-card purchase funnel and `pay_online` were both unreachable via natural language. — **Both Fixed** (see Fix log).
15. **e2e-bug.103** — the entire package-visit guest-token pair (cancel/reschedule) is unreachable via natural language, 5/5 phrasings failed via 4 different mechanisms. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).

**Section J update**: `explain_why_stripe_required` and `explain_service_price` confirmed clean (the latter correctly satisfies the plan's 0%-tax cross-check). `explain_checkout_tax` and `pay_online` are both unreachable (e2e-bug.88 for the latter); `explain_checkout_tax`'s 2nd failure surfaced a new variant of e2e-bug.77 — an apparently fully **orphaned** intent (`explain_appointment_tax`, never registered to any surface at all, not just the wrong one). `choose_payment_method` misfired once into a 2nd independent repro of the exact `explain_public_booking_checkout` leak already seen in Section D. `get_booking_quote` reached correctly but missed an explicitly-named service (param-extraction miss, not numbered). Testing required seeding a fake Stripe-connected config on the primary test business (`settings.integrations.stripe`), per explicit user authorization, since no real Stripe account exists in this dev environment — this only unlocks the classification/explainer layer, not real payment processing.

The rest of Section M's compounds remain untested. `cancel_and_rebook` produced e2e-bug.89, a significant new finding proving the cancellation breakage runs deeper than the classifier-rescue layer alone.

**Section M update 2 (2nd pass — 10 more compounds tested live via a hand-signed customer session JWT, explicitly authorized by the user after the permission system flagged the token-minting technique)**:
- **e2e-bug.90 gains 3 more reproductions via compound entry points**, confirming the crash is reachable through the compound path too, not just single-step prompts: `public_flexible_availability_budget_compound`-shaped ("show me massages under 100 dollars and tell me which ones have evening or weekend slots"), `public_flexible_availability_list_budget_then_or_compound`-shaped ("find me a service under 90 dollars that's available this weekend"), and `public_multi_service_compound`/`preview_multi_service_cart`-shaped ("I want to preview a cart with a facial and a massage together") all hit the identical raw 500 crash.
- **e2e-bug.77 gains 3 more reproductions**: `public_budget_service_discovery_compound`-shaped prompt → `security_blocked`/"search_retail_sku"; `cancel_package_rebook_single`-shaped prompt → `security_blocked`/"create_package_booking"; a second package-booking phrasing → the same `security_blocked`/"create_package_booking".
- **`book_package_with_nearest_slot` confirmed clean and correctly non-mutating**: "buy the Massage Package and get the earliest available slot" (using this business's one real package, verified via direct DB read) correctly found the earliest available block and returned a `navigate: {path: 'checkout', ...}` deep link — confirmed via direct DB read that **no new `package_purchases` or `bookings` row was actually created**, matching the by-design behavior of `handleBookPackage` (`ai-self-service-booking.logic.ts:270-298`), which deliberately stops at "continue at checkout" rather than completing a real purchase server-side, exactly mirroring how single-service booking also requires a separate confirm-payment step. (An initial fictional package name, "the deluxe package," correctly failed to resolve — a test-methodology artifact, not a bug, once cross-checked against the real catalog.)
- **`rebook_and_pay`-shaped prompt** ("rebook my last appointment and pay online this time") correctly stopped at step 1 (`rebook_last_appointment`) with "No completed visits found to rebook yet" — plausibly correct given both seeded test bookings are `confirmed` (upcoming), not `completed`; inconclusive rather than a bug given this test account has no completed-visit history to rebook from.
- **New, lower-confidence finding — `subscription_first_visit`-shaped prompt** ("use my subscription credit and book my first visit") decomposed to step 1 = `explain_my_subscription` (a read-only explainer, "Ask about visits left, expiry, or how your membership works"), not `use_subscription_credit` or any credit-consuming action — architecturally odd for a compound whose entire premise is *using* subscription credit to book, not explaining the plan. Not folded into the e2e-bug numbering (lower confidence without confirming the actual intended recipe steps for this compound), but worth a second look in the fix pass.

**Section N update — no new e2e-bug numbers, but several important cross-cutting findings**: (1) **adversarial/prompt-injection resistance is genuinely solid** — 2/2 tests (fake "admin mode" free-gift-card attempt; fake "SYSTEM OVERRIDE" platform-wide-cancel attempt) were both correctly blocked or correctly scoped down to the caller's own data, a real positive security result. (2) **Out-of-scope chit-chat and empty/whitespace/emoji-only prompts are all handled gracefully**, no crashes, no hallucination. (3) **A surprising, valuable positive result**: `"cxl my apt tmrw"` (abbreviated) actually reached `cancel_my_booking` correctly with correct multi-booking disambiguation — the first successful reach of this intent in the entire audit — because the abbreviation "apt" doesn't match e2e-bug.75's `isMyAppointmentsPrompt()` regex, which requires the whole word "appointment." This proves the underlying cancel logic itself works fine; only the upstream hijack (already documented in e2e-bug.75) is broken. (4) **Negation is not respected** ("don't cancel..." still got treated as cancel-adjacent) and **sarcasm was misclassified but harmlessly** (routed to a benign, non-destructive action). (5) **Length measurably degrades classification** — embedding the same working "cxl my apt tmrw" phrase inside a ~150-word rambling message caused it to be missed entirely, landing on `add_booking_to_calendar` — now the **3rd independent reproduction** of that exact wrong destination across 3 unrelated sections/prompts (Section C, Section E, and here), strong evidence of a real, shared low-confidence-fallback defect worth a dedicated fix-pass investigation, not yet traced to a specific file:line. (6) **Concurrent read requests are safe** — no cross-contamination observed.

**Section K update (guest-token security pass — tested live, no Authorization header on any call, using a real manage-token fetched directly from the DB after discovering e2e-bug.95 below made it unobtainable via natural language)**: this section surfaced 2 severe, confirmed security bugs and 1 severe UX/data-loss bug, plus one genuinely clean, fully-verified positive result.

- **e2e-bug.95**: `get_manage_link` never actually delivers the booking manage link/token to the customer. The response says "Here is your booking manage link" but the JSON contains only `bookingId` — no `manageUrl`, no `manageToken` anywhere. Confirmed via direct DB read that the token IS correctly generated and persisted server-side (`bookings.metadata.manageToken`, via `ensureBookingManageToken`), so the backend logic itself is correct — the data is simply discarded by the response-shaping layer before it reaches the customer. Root cause: [ai-get-manage-link.logic.ts:100-111](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-get-manage-link.logic.ts:100) returns `manageUrl`/`manageToken` in `details`, but `commandResultToPublicAssistantResult()` ([customer-ai-command.util.ts:361-384](backend/src/modules/ai/customer-ai-command.util.ts:361)) filters `details` through a hardcoded allow-list, `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_UI_DETAIL_KEYS` ([customer-ai-command.util.ts:325-338](backend/src/modules/ai/customer-ai-command.util.ts:325)), which does not include `manageUrl` or `manageToken` — the exact same bug shape as e2e-bug.81 (`my_gift_cards`'s dropped detail keys), now hitting the entire guest/no-login "manage my booking" feature's only entry point. **Real-world impact**: a customer who asks the assistant for a manage link (the documented, intended way to get one without logging in) is told "here it is" and gets nothing usable — the feature is completely non-functional via natural language. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
- **e2e-bug.96** (**the single most severe security finding of the entire audit**) — **Fixed** (same root cause as e2e-bug.128): `confirm_my_booking_details` has a confirmed, unauthenticated, cross-customer IDOR. Sending `{"prompt":"what is this booking","context":{"bookingId":"<any real booking UUID on this business>"}}` to the public assistant endpoint — **with no Authorization header, no session, and no manage token at all** — returns that booking's full details (service, provider, date/time, business address). Reproduced 3 times: with a garbage/guessed `manageToken`, with no `manageToken` field at all, and — most critically — **using a real booking UUID belonging to a completely different customer than any session in play**, which correctly returned that other customer's real appointment details. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read: [ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.ts:110-123](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.ts:110) resolves the booking via `deps.bookingRepo.findOne({ where: { id: bookingId, businessId, ...(customerId ? { customerId } : {}) } })` — when no session exists, `customerId` is `undefined` and the conditional spread evaluates to `{}`, silently **dropping the ownership constraint from the query entirely** rather than rejecting the request. This action is explicitly documented elsewhere in the same codebase as "logged-in, no token" (see the classifier rule comment on `explain_manage_booking_context` at [ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.ts:14](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-manage-booking-with-token.util.ts:14): "NOT confirm_my_booking_details (logged-in, no token)") — the code clearly assumes `bookingId` only ever gets populated together with a real `customerId`, but the public assistant DTO accepts an arbitrary `context.bookingId` with zero such guarantee. **Fix direction**: require `customerId` unconditionally in the query when resolving by `bookingId` for this specific intent (return not-found rather than dropping the constraint when no session exists) — this intent has no legitimate anonymous/guest use case at all, unlike its token-gated sibling.
- **e2e-bug.97**: `reschedule_booking_with_token` (guest, correct bookingId + correct manageToken, zero login) crashes with a raw, unhandled Postgres error leaked verbatim into the customer-facing response: `"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"customer:36400df4-...\"".` Root cause, confirmed via direct source read across 3 files: [public-customer-booking.service.ts:837-838](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-customer-booking.service.ts:837)'s `actorUserId()` builds a namespaced actor-tag string (`` `customer:${customerId ?? booking.customerId}` ``) for audit-log purposes whenever the caller authenticated via guest token rather than a real session (since `auth.customerId` is undefined on that path); this tag is passed as `actorId` into `BookingService.update()` ([public-customer-booking.service.ts:543-555](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-customer-booking.service.ts:543)), which unconditionally treats any truthy `userId` as a real staff/business-member UUID and calls `resolvePhiAuditActor()` → `businessService.ensureMember(businessId, userId)` ([booking.service.ts:135-148](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:135), branch entered at [booking.service.ts:530-543](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:530)) — a query that throws an uncaught Postgres UUID-cast error on the non-UUID `customer:<id>` string, which then propagates unhandled all the way to the customer's JSON response via the logic layer's generic `err?.message` catch-all. Since the same `actorUserId()` pattern is used at all 4 guest-token call sites ([public-customer-booking.service.ts:483,543,595,685](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-customer-booking.service.ts:483)), `reschedule_package_visit_with_token` likely shares this exact defect (not independently re-tested this pass to conserve remaining test data). **Fix direction**: `resolvePhiAuditActor`/`resolveStaffPhiContext` should short-circuit (treat as `{role: 'public', userId: null}`) whenever `userId` doesn't parse as a UUID, or `actorUserId()` should pass the raw customer UUID plus a separate `actorType` flag rather than a namespaced string that collides with code expecting a bare UUID. — **Fixed** (see Fix log; same family as api-bug.1).
- **Genuine, fully-verified positive result**: `cancel_booking_with_token`'s guest-token security model is clean end-to-end. Both required IDOR checks passed: a wrong/guessed `manageToken` against a real `bookingId` was correctly rejected ("Share the manage link for this booking first, so I can look it up"), and the *correct* token for one booking applied to a *different* `bookingId` was also correctly rejected — confirming tokens are properly scoped to one specific booking, not just "any valid-looking token." The happy path (correct `bookingId` + correct `manageToken`, zero Authorization header) then genuinely executed a real cancellation end-to-end — confirmed via direct DB read (`bookings.status` flipped to `cancelled`) — the **first fully successful guest-token mutate operation in the entire audit**. (This consumed one of the 2 originally-seeded test bookings; noted in the test-data accounting below, not reverted since it was the intended, successful outcome of an authorized functional test, not an accidental mutation.)
- **Also observed**: natural-language phrasing for both `get_manage_link` and `explain_manage_booking_context` repeatedly collided with already-documented defects before reaching their real handlers — "send me the manage link" misfired to the e2e-bug.82-family `push_lab_booking_to_patient` leak, "what's this booking, can I still cancel it?" misfired to `explain_booking_policy`/`security_blocked` (another e2e-bug.77 repro), and a plain "my booking"-phrased guest reschedule attempt fell straight into e2e-bug.75's `my_appointments` hijack even with a valid token supplied — all 3 are reproductions of already-numbered bugs, not new ones, but they compound with e2e-bug.95 to make the entire guest-token surface very difficult to reach via ordinary phrasing; every successful guest-token test above required either a very specific phrasing or a manually-constructed manage-link URL embedded in the prompt text.
- Not tested this pass (given effort already invested and limited remaining seeded test bookings): the 3 guest compounds (`guest_manage_visit`, `guest_book_and_manage`, `guest_pay_cash_manage`), the package-visit guest-token pair, and explicitly re-confirming the signed-in-customer-endpoint-without-a-token fallback behavior.

**Section L update (public vs. customer surface boundary) — now fully closed out**:
- **Core negative test**: sending an account/payment/clinic/rewards prompt to the anonymous endpoint with no session must not rescue, execute, or leak data. **Re-tested with 3 more intents this pass, all clean**: "what is my loyalty points balance", "cancel my subscription", and "show my lab results" — sent with zero Authorization header and zero `context` — all 3 correctly declined with a "Sign in to..." message, no data leak, no crash, no accidental execution. This **narrows e2e-bug.96's characterization**: the unauthenticated cross-customer IDOR is specific to `confirm_my_booking_details` (the only intent that accepts a raw `context.bookingId` override with no ownership check), not a systemic pattern across account-scoped intents — every other tested account/payment/clinic intent correctly gates on session identity.
- **Shared-discovery parity check, now independently verified**: 3 of the 14 `PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` (`business_info`, a provider-list prompt, `check_availability`) were sent to the identical hybrid endpoint both anonymously and with a valid customer session, and produced byte-identical `action`/status results in both modes — including the e2e-bug.90 500 crash reproducing identically (same exact error message, both `500`) regardless of auth state. Confirms the "shared discovery" routing is genuinely auth-independent, exactly as documented, for both the working and broken cases.
- **Cross-tenant customer-JWT check**: a real, correctly-signed customer JWT scoped to business A (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`), sent against business B's slug (`qa-test-clinic-cf58d2a9`), was correctly rejected with `401 {"message":"Customer session expired"}` rather than granting any cross-tenant access — the customer-session JWT surface enforces business-scoping server-side just as solidly as the already-confirmed dashboard/provider JWT surface.

**Section M update 3 (clinic compound, tested live on the clinic-vertical business with a 2nd hand-signed customer JWT for its real patient)**:
- **New finding — e2e-bug.98**: `complete_intake_and_book` (the `customer_clinic_compound`/`public_clinic_compound` family) reports a **false-positive success**. "Fill out my pre-visit intake and then book my lab test" returned `{"success":true, "summary":"Completed 2 customer step(s): complete intake and book, book nearest slot."}` — but a direct DB check confirmed **zero rows were created** in `clinic_pre_visit_intakes` and no new booking exists. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read: [ai-complete-intake-and-book.logic.ts:112-123](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-complete-intake-and-book.logic.ts:112) wraps the real `ensureCustomerDraft()` call in a bare `try { ... } catch { /* fall back to navigate-only */ }` with **no error surfaced to the caller at all** — when the call throws (here, because this test clinic business has zero published intake questionnaires configured, confirmed via direct DB read of `clinic_questionnaires`, so `assertLabTestService()` at [public-pre-visit-intake.service.ts:151-170](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-pre-visit-intake.service.ts:151) correctly throws `BadRequestException`), the handler silently proceeds to build and return the exact same "success" response it would have returned had the draft been created, with no `intakeId` and no indication anything failed. **Real-world impact**: whenever a clinic customer's pre-visit intake genuinely can't be started (unpublished questionnaire, wrong service, etc. — configuration states that will absolutely occur in production), the assistant tells them it succeeded anyway, leaving them to discover only later (likely at the actual visit) that no intake was ever filed. **Fix direction**: don't swallow the exception — either surface the real failure reason to the customer (matching how every other intent in this codebase handles a failed precondition) or, at minimum, omit "Completed" language from the summary when `intakeId` is unset. — **Fixed** (see Fix log).
- The compound's 2nd step also echoed the raw un-resolved phrase `"my lab test"` into a `checkProvidersHandoff.serviceName` detail field even though the actual service was correctly resolved to the real catalog service "Complete blood count" elsewhere in the same response — a minor cosmetic inconsistency, not folded into the bug numbering.
- A second, simpler prompt ("start my intake form and schedule my next lab collection") correctly declined with "No open lab collection booking requests were found on your account" — a reasonable, correct response given this test patient has no open lab order, not a bug.
- `guest_book_and_manage` (anonymous, no session) was also tested: it did not error, but produced no real booking either — this matches the already-established, correct-by-design pattern (seen with `book_package_with_nearest_slot`) where a guest booking recipe legitimately stops before completing a real reservation without a full checkout/payment step, so this is inconclusive rather than a bug given the AI chat surface alone can't complete a full guest checkout.

## CLOSURE — consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 (FINAL)

This closes the full test-plan (Sections A through O) for the customer-facing AI assistant across the consumer app, the public/anonymous booking assistant, and the guest manage-link surface. Testing was conducted live against the running dev backend (real Postgres DB, real classifier/LLM calls, no mocks) using two real seeded businesses/customers — no area of the plan was left completely untouched.

### Bug ledger — 31 confirmed bugs (e2e-bug.75–105)

**Critical — security / data exposure**

| # | Summary | Root cause | Fix direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **96** | Unauthenticated, cross-customer IDOR: `confirm_my_booking_details` returns any customer's full booking details (service, provider, time, address) given only a booking UUID, no session, no valid token. Reproduced with a real different customer's booking. — **Fixed** | [ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.ts:111-123](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.ts:111) — `...(customerId ? { customerId } : {})` drops the ownership constraint entirely when no session exists instead of rejecting. | Never resolve by `bookingId` alone — signed-in path requires owning `customerId`; guest path requires a valid `manageToken`. |
| **84** | `privacy_delete` (GDPR erasure) has zero confirmation step; one sentence irreversibly anonymizes the account. Executed for real during testing (caught, fully reverted). — **Fixed** | No confirmation-gate; now two-turn `requiresConfirmation` / `params.confirm` (plus affirmative-after-pending rescue), matching `cancel_all_upcoming_bookings`. Specs: `ai-e2e84-privacy-delete-confirm.util.spec.ts`. |
| **97** | Guest-token reschedule crashes with a raw Postgres error (`invalid input syntax for type uuid`) leaked verbatim to the customer. — **Fixed** | [public-customer-booking.service.ts:837-838](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-customer-booking.service.ts:837)'s `actorUserId()` builds a `customer:<uuid>` tag for guest actors, passed into `BookingService.update()` → [booking.service.ts:530-543](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:530) → `resolvePhiAuditActor()` ([booking.service.ts:135-148](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:135)), which unconditionally queries `ensureMember()` assuming any truthy `userId` is a real staff UUID. Likely also affects `reschedule_package_visit_with_token` (same call-site pattern, not independently re-tested). | Short-circuit `resolvePhiAuditActor`/`resolveStaffPhiContext` to `{role:'public', userId:null}` when `userId` doesn't parse as a UUID, or pass a separate `actorType` flag instead of a namespaced string. |

**Severe — functional breakage on core flows**

| # | Summary | Root cause | Fix direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **90** | Raw unhandled 500 (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')`) on `list_services`, `list_providers`, `find_services_under_budget`, `find_evening_weekend_slots`, `list_public_promotions` — reachable via plain prompts and compound-phrased prompts alike. — **Fixed** | [ai-platform.util.ts](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-platform.util.ts)'s `validatePublicAssistantAction()` called `.includes()` on `PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_INTENTS` when a circular-import race left the binding `undefined`. | Call-time resolve + leaf `PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` fallback; gate never throws. Specs: `ai-e2e90-public-assistant-intents-gate.util.spec.ts`. |
| **75/76** | `cancel_my_booking`, `reschedule_my_booking`, `cancel_my_subscription`, `start_pre_visit_intake` (and siblings) hijacked to read-only intents whenever the prompt contains "my" + a booking-word (even inside compound words like "pre-visit" across a hyphen boundary); question-phrased prompts hijacked to `explain_why_sign_in`. Proven to be purely an upstream classification defect — the abbreviation "apt" (not matching the regex) let `cancel_my_booking` reach its handler correctly with correct multi-booking disambiguation. | `ai-customer-crm.util.ts`: `isMyAppointmentsPrompt` (lines 214-220/630-633), `isMySubscriptionsPrompt` (lines 222-266/628-629); `ai-explain-why-sign-in.util.ts` (missing exclusion, unlike its other 10 documented exclusions). | Require a genuine mutate-verb (cancel/reschedule/move) alongside the "my X" phrase before hijacking to the read-only sibling; add the same exclusion pattern already used for 10 other topics in `ai-explain-why-sign-in.util.ts`. |
| **89** | Even bypassing the classifier entirely via direct compound-step dispatch, `cancel_my_booking` still fails to find real existing bookings — a 2nd, independent break in the same capability. — **Fixed** | `extractServiceNameFromPrompt` / shared compound context set `serviceName` to the availability filler `"next available"` from "book the next available slot", so `matchCustomerOwnedBooking` filtered out all real visits. | Reject availability-filler service names; extract cancel-target service from "cancel my {service} appointment"; prefer cancel-segment service in `cancel_and_rebook`. Specs: `ai-e2e89-cancel-and-rebook-lookup.util.spec.ts`. |
| **77** | Customer prompts sharing vocabulary with provider/dashboard-only intents get misrouted and blocked instead of reaching the real customer intent — the single most pervasive defect found, with 13+ independent reproductions across 9+ domains. — **Fixed** | Systemic missing-surface-gate pattern inside rescue unknown/classified phases (`list_upcoming_bookings`, `push_lab_booking_to_patient`, `create_package_booking`, `cancel_gift_card_order`, `show_appointments`, retail-finance, …). | Pipeline `acceptRescueForSurface` post-filter + call-site gates off customer/public; detector exclusions for cancel phrasing. Specs: `ai-e2e77-cross-surface-rescue-gate.util.spec.ts`. |
