### Post-closure addendum 4 (Section K — package-visit guest-token pair, unblocked via a real package purchase)
A real package purchase was successfully created this pass via the actual `POST packages/book` REST endpoint (not raw SQL) — the earlier back-to-back-visit validation failures were test-methodology error (my constructed times didn't account for this business's default 5-minute `turnoverBufferMinutes` between package service lines); once corrected, `packages/book` (with `markPaid: true`, since the package requires online payment and this dev environment has no real Stripe checkout to complete) created a real `package_purchases` row (`278cf621-a033-4cc8-b913-dbeda160dc2a`) and 5 real linked bookings for the primary test customer. This unblocked live testing of `cancel_package_visit_with_token`/`reschedule_package_visit_with_token`.

- **New, severe finding — e2e-bug.102**: `extractGuestContactFromPrompt()`'s phone-number regex is dangerously loose and causes real misrouting. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read and a standalone regex test: `PHONE_PATTERN = /(?:\+?\d[\d\s().-]{7,}\d)/` at [ai-get-manage-link.util.ts:38](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-get-manage-link.util.ts:38) matches **any** 9+ character run of digits/spaces/parens/dots/dashes **anywhere in the prompt text, with no phone-context anchor** (no "phone:", "call me", or similar requirement). Tested directly against a realistic guest reschedule prompt containing a real booking UUID pasted from a manage-link URL — the regex matched `"94-4537-9"`, a meaningless fragment sliced out of the *middle* of the UUID (`...da94-4537-9c93...`), which then gets normalized and accepted as a "guest phone number" (`normalizeGuestContactPhone`, ≥7 digits after normalization). This single false positive was enough to make `isGuestContext()` return `true` and hijack the prompt into the `guest_manage_visit` compound instead of the intended standalone guest-token intent, which then failed with "No upcoming booking found for that email or phone" — a garbage lookup against a garbage "phone number." **Real-world impact**: any guest prompt that happens to include a manage-link URL, order/confirmation number, tracking number, or any other digit-heavy string is at risk of being silently misclassified as containing a guest phone number, corrupting the guest-identity-lookup path. Reproduced deterministically (confirmed via isolated regex test, not just live API behavior). **Fix direction**: anchor the phone regex to require a phone-context cue nearby (e.g. digits preceded by "phone", "call", "text", "reach me at", or occurring as the *entire* trimmed prompt/field rather than a substring match anywhere in free text), or require a stricter digit-count/format (e.g. exactly 10-15 digits with no more than one separator run) closer to real phone number shapes.
- **New finding — e2e-bug.103**: the package-visit guest-token pair (`cancel_package_visit_with_token`, `reschedule_package_visit_with_token`) is unreachable via natural language — 5/5 tested phrasings against a real package-visit booking (bookingId + real manage token, confirmed correct via direct DB read) failed via 4 different mechanisms: 2× hijacked into the wrong `guest_manage_visit` compound via e2e-bug.102's phone-regex false-positive; 1× misrouted to the *logged-in* sibling `reschedule_package_visit_self` ("Sign in to reschedule your package visit.") despite zero session and explicit guest framing; 2× misrouted to `security_blocked`/"create_package_booking" (another e2e-bug.77 repro). Not one phrasing reached either intended intent. Not traced to a single root cause beyond e2e-bug.102 (which explains 2 of the 5 failures) — the `reschedule_package_visit_self` and `security_blocked` misfires need separate tracing in the fix pass.

### Post-closure addendum 5 (Section M — tour-vertical compounds, a new tour business built through the real dashboard/onboarding flow)

Per explicit user authorization, built a brand-new tour-vertical business through the real UI (not raw SQL) to unblock the last 2 untested Section M compounds: registered a new owner account at `/register`, selected "Tour operator" as the business type in onboarding, used the AI-suggested catalog generator, and applied the full playbook (services + schedule) — resulting in a real business `qa-test-tours-aec5d941` (id `26f47f39-3a88-4e96-92a8-de1314f71fa7`) with 5 real tour services (Full Day City Tour, Sunset Coastal Drive, 3-Day Mountain Trek, Weekend Heritage Tour, Private Wine Country Day), 1 real employee (the owner), and 1 schedule template.

- **New, severe finding — e2e-bug.104** (**a top-severity finding, on par with e2e-bug.90/96**): `tour_group_checkout` crashes with a raw, unhandled SQL error leaked verbatim to the customer: `{"statusCode":500,"message":"column booking.start_time does not exist"}`. Confirmed 100% reproducible (2/2) using the recipe's own registry example prompt (`"City tour for 8 on 15/08/2026 — book only if enough spots"`). Root cause, confirmed via direct source read: [booking.service.ts:886-896](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:886), inside `BookingService.findAll()`'s date-range branch, uses a raw TypeORM `QueryBuilder` literal `booking.start_time` (snake_case) in both the `andWhere` clause and the `orderBy` call — but this codebase's `Booking` entity property is `startTime`, and TypeORM `QueryBuilder` string literals must reference the **entity property name** (`booking.startTime`), not a guessed raw column name; every other column in this codebase is confirmed camelCase-quoted (`"createdAt"`, `"durationMinutes"`, etc. via direct SQL checks earlier this session). This exact branch of `findAll()` only executes when both `startDate` and `endDate` params are supplied. **Blast radius is broad**: a grep across the codebase shows this exact `startDate`/`endDate` call pattern is used by at least 6 different tour-domain AI logic files — [ai-tour-day-slots.logic.ts:66](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-tour-day-slots.logic.ts:66), [ai-tour-service.logic.ts:321](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-tour-service.logic.ts:321), [ai-tour-calendar-week.logic.ts:174](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-tour-calendar-week.logic.ts:174), [ai-tour-capacity.logic.ts:64](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-tour-capacity.logic.ts:64), [ai-upcoming-tour-departures.logic.ts:255](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-upcoming-tour-departures.logic.ts:255) — meaning this single bad column reference likely crashes the majority of the tour vertical's AI-driven capacity/availability/scheduling intents, not just this one compound. **Fix direction**: change both occurrences of `booking.start_time` to `booking.startTime` (a one-line-each fix); given the blast radius, also grep the whole codebase for any other raw `_` snake_case column literals inside `createQueryBuilder` calls, since this pattern likely wasn't caught by type-checking (QueryBuilder string literals aren't statically checked) and may recur elsewhere. — **Fixed:** see Fix log **e2e-bug.104 — FIXED** (same `booking.startTime` QueryBuilder fix as e2e-bug.149).

- **New finding — e2e-bug.105**: both `book_tour_nearest_departure` and `tour_group_checkout` fail to reach a working state via their own officially-documented registry example prompts even where they don't crash. `"book the wine tour earliest date for 2 people"`/`"reserve mountain trek soonest departure for 4 people"` (verbatim from the registry) both stopped at step 1 (`explain_tour_booking`) with a generic clarify message ("Ask about a tour on the booking page…") instead of resolving the named tour; `"Wine tour for 6 next Saturday — book if enough seats"` (verbatim from `tour_group_checkout`'s own registry example) failed with "Could not find a catalog service matching 'Wine tour'" — this specific mismatch may be partly attributable to this AI-generated test catalog naming its wine-themed service "Private Wine Country Day" rather than literally "Wine tour" (a test-data-vs-fixture-example mismatch, not necessarily a hard bug on its own), but combined with the `explain_tour_booking` step-1 failures on the *other* recipe's own examples, this points to a broader pattern of tour-recipe registry example prompts not being kept in sync with what the classifier/parsers actually accept. Lower confidence than e2e-bug.104; not traced to a single file:line. — **Fixed:** see Fix log **e2e-bug.105 — FIXED** (compound parse bypass + fuzzy catalog resolve + extractor guard).

## web-booking-e2e-plan.1 — EXECUTION LOG

**Section A (page-by-page) — business landing page**: loaded cleanly, no console errors. Business header, "Best service" description card, "Any available specialist" quick-book card, and a live provider list with real-time slot grids (Gevorg Gasparyan, 3.5★/6 reviews, 18 real bookable time slots shown) all rendered correctly. "Booking assistant" FAB opens a chat panel with 2 page-specific suggested prompts ("What's the cheapest service?", "Who's free tomorrow?"), a mic button, and a text input. Confirmed clean so far.

**Section E/F — AI assistant widget, first live test — severe finding, e2e-bug.90 UI amplification**: sent `"what services do you offer?"` (the exact e2e-bug.90 trigger prompt) through the widget. Network tab confirms the identical backend `500` (`POST .../assistant` → 500, same `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')"` payload as the curl reproduction). **The web UI has zero error-message sanitization on this path**: the raw JavaScript exception string is rendered **twice** — once as an inline chat bubble styled identically to a normal assistant reply (complete with a working "Listen" text-to-speech button that would read the raw exception aloud), and again in a separate bottom-of-screen toast reading `"Could not create. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')."` No console error was thrown (the fetch failure is caught somewhere), confirming this is a **display bug, not a crash** — the code path deliberately takes whatever error string it receives and shows it verbatim to the customer, in two different UI surfaces, with no generic fallback message ("Something went wrong, please try again") anywhere in between. A secondary, smaller defect: the toast's static prefix, `"Could not create."`, is wrong for this scenario — the failed action was a read/discovery query (`what services do you offer`), not a "create" operation, suggesting the toast copy is a generic catch-all mislabeled for creation-flow errors specifically. **This is a materially worse real-world manifestation of e2e-bug.90 than the raw-JSON API response already documented** — an API consumer seeing a JSON error is one thing; an end customer seeing a garbled JavaScript stack-trace fragment presented as the assistant's own words, with a "click to have it read aloud" affordance, is a much sharper UX failure. Not yet numbered — will fold into the closure pass with the rest of this plan's findings, likely as a direct amendment to e2e-bug.90 rather than a new number, since the root cause is identical.

**Working-prompt contrast confirmed**: `"tell me about your business"` rendered cleanly — correct `explain_salon_profile` content plus a "Continue booking" navigate button. Confirms the raw-error rendering above only occurs on the failure path; happy-path UI is otherwise well-built.

**Section E — booking_help / guide-flow rendering, and a major confirmation + expansion of e2e-bug.91**: sent `"how do I book with you?"` — rendered as a polished "Step 1 of 4: Select a Professional" guide card with step title/body and a "Next step" button, genuinely good UX. **Critically, the visible chat transcript does NOT show any of the internal debug fields** — confirming the widget's rendering code specifically extracts only `guide`/`summary`/`navigate` fields and doesn't dump the raw `sessionContext` object into the chat bubble. **However, pulling the raw network response for this exact request (`POST .../assistant` → 201) confirms e2e-bug.91's leak is still fully present at the network/API level**, fully exposed to anyone with browser dev tools open on this public page (a trivial bar for any customer). The full captured payload is significantly richer than the curl-based finding already on record:
- `_capabilityHints`: the **complete, verbatim raw LLM system prompt**, listing all ~220 native intent names plus the 14 delegated ones, plus the full internal architecture description ("Discovery/booking delegated to PublicBookingAssistantService...").
- `_entityMemoryBlock`: real per-business learned entity aliases — crucially including **a real customer's name**: `"mary" → customer=Mary`, alongside provider aliases (`"jujo" → provider=Jujo Karapetyan`, `"karo" → provider=Karo Mazmanyan`) and service aliases.
- **New sub-finding**: `_entityMemoryAliases` is leaked as the literal string `"[object Object]"` — a raw JS object was stringified with `String(obj)`/template interpolation instead of `JSON.stringify(obj)`, a small but concrete serialization bug on top of the exposure itself.
- **New, concerning sub-finding**: `_roleProfile: "owner"` is present on this request even though it's a fully anonymous, unauthenticated public call (`customerId: null`, `userEmail: null`). Not yet determined whether this reflects a real over-broad default-role resolution (a business-owner-level role profile being attached to anonymous public traffic) or just an internal default label with no functional effect — worth a source-level check in the fix pass, since "owner" attached to anonymous requests is a red flag regardless of functional impact.
- Also present: `_commandTraceId`, `_accessTier: "client"`, `_actorRole: "client"`, `_membershipRole: "client"`, `_planTierId: "business"`, `_scopedEmployeeId`, `_locationId`, `_branchHint`, `_confidenceHigh: "0.85"`, `_abVariantId`.

**Net effect for the closure pass**: e2e-bug.91 remains valid and serious — the leak is real and reproducible at the network layer regardless of the official web client's own (good) chat-rendering discipline — and now has a fuller field inventory plus 2 new sub-findings (`_entityMemoryAliases` serialization bug, anonymous-request `_roleProfile: "owner"`) worth folding into its write-up.

**Section A/L — guest manage-link page**: navigated directly to `manage?bookingId=<real>&token=<real>` (both fetched from the DB for the last remaining seeded booking) — the page correctly parsed both URL params and rendered a real, correct booking summary (facemassage, Gevorg Gasparyan, 19/07/2026 14:35–15:35) with "Reschedule"/"Cancel booking" buttons and a "Sign in with Google" prompt, all without any auth header. Confirmed clean for the base page render.

**New finding — the manage page's own AI widget suggested prompts don't correctly use page context**: this page's assistant shows 3 page-specific suggested prompts (`"Cancel this appointment"`, `"Reschedule to next week"`, `"Send manage link"`), implying the widget is meant to be context-aware of the specific booking already loaded on this page. Clicking `"Reschedule to next week"` — the page's own official, one-click suggestion — **did not trigger `reschedule_booking_with_token` at all**; it produced a generic `booking_help`/`guide_user_flow` response ("Here's how to book an appointment on this page: Pick a professional or choose Any available" / "Step 1 of 2"), completely ignoring that a specific existing booking (with a valid token) was already loaded on this exact page. This means even the manage page's own first-party, pre-written suggested action fails to resolve to the correct guest-token intent — a genuine, page-specific UI/classification bug distinct from anything found via curl this session (curl testing always had to explicitly engineer prompts to reach these intents; this is the *official, first-party, single-click path* on the real page failing on its own). Not yet root-caused (would need to inspect the actual request payload sent, not just the URL, to see whether `bookingId`/`manageToken` are threaded into the request at all) — worth flagging as a new, UI-specific finding for the closure pass, tentatively **e2e-bug.106** pending final numbering.

**e2e-bug.106 confirmed 2/2, not a one-off**: retried with a fully explicit, unambiguous free-typed prompt on the same manage page — `"reschedule this booking to tomorrow at 3pm"` — same result: generic `booking_help` guide, not `reschedule_booking_with_token`. Both requests returned `201 Created` (the backend classified and executed *something* successfully, just the wrong action) — ruling out a token-expiry/auth-rejection explanation. This strongly suggests the manage page's AI widget component simply never threads the already-loaded `bookingId`/`manageToken` into the AI request context at all, regardless of what the customer types — meaning **the entire guest-token reschedule/cancel flow is unreachable via this page's AI assistant, full stop**, independent of phrasing (customers can still use the plain "Reschedule"/"Cancel booking" buttons on this page directly, which don't go through the AI layer — this only affects the chat widget specifically). — **Fixed:** see Fix log entry under e2e-bug.107 / e2e-bug.106 FIXED summary.

**Section K — account page, authenticated session (injected via localStorage using a hand-signed JWT, same authorized technique as earlier this session)**: signed in as the real test customer via direct `localStorage` session injection (the app re-fetches the real profile via `getPublicCustomerMe` on load, so only a valid `{token}` was needed). Account page rendered correctly and completely: profile, GDPR "Download my data"/"Delete my account data" buttons (did not click delete, to avoid repeating the earlier accidental-deletion incident), referral code, loyalty bonuses (184.46 — reflects accumulated test-session activity), active subscription (4/4 visits left), gift card redemption sections, and "My bookings" showing all real seeded data correctly (the 5-line package visit, the remaining active facemassage booking, a cancelled one). All non-AI rendering confirmed clean.

**e2e-bug.75 reproduces identically through this UI**: asked the account-page widget `"cancel my booking"` while authenticated — hijacked to `list_my_appointments`/`my_appointments` ("You have 7 appointment(s) on record."), exactly matching the already-documented backend defect. No new behavior.

**Section P — locale investigation (partially inconclusive)**: attempted several mechanisms to switch this web app to hy locale to live-test e2e-bug.87 through the actual widget UI: a `?locale=hy` URL query param (no effect on rendered content), and the `app-locale` cookie used by this codebase's own `public-locale-cookie.ts` (set directly via `document.cookie`, confirmed persisted across navigation, but **also had no effect** — see below). **Direct confirmation that e2e-bug.87 is unchanged**: called the assistant endpoint directly with `locale: 'hy'` explicitly forced in the request body — reproduced the exact same mixed-script corruption already on record, now with fresh concrete examples: `"«Ծառայություններ» вкладկայում"` (Cyrillic "вклад" — Russian for "tab" — spliced into an Armenian sentence) and `"Գlխavar, Ծառayutyunner ev Հashiv"` (Armenian letters mixed with bare Latin characters and Latin transliteration, appearing in a *topic label*, a UI string, not just deep guide content). **New, separate finding**: even with the `app-locale=hy` cookie correctly set and persisted, a live request sent through the actual widget UI (not the direct-fetch test) still carried `"locale":"en"` in its real network payload — meaning **this specific cookie does not drive the AI assistant's request locale on this surface at all**. Did not find the actual mechanism that does control it within the time available this pass (no visible in-UI language switcher was found on the pages checked: landing, profile, account). This leaves two open, unresolved questions for the fix pass rather than a single clean bug: (1) what actually sets assistant-request locale on this surface, if not this cookie, and (2) given that, can a real Armenian-speaking customer using the *live widget* (as opposed to a direct API call) ever actually reach hy-locale responses at all — if not, e2e-bug.87's real-world exposure on this specific surface may be lower than assumed, but the underlying content defect is unambiguously still real and confirmed.

### Continuing — Section A/G (single-service booking flow) and a significant broadening of e2e-bug.106

**Section A — services/checkout pages**: navigated the real step-based booking wizard (`/services` → select specialist+slot → select service → checkout) end-to-end without submitting. All pages rendered correctly: the "Select service" page shows a clean category-grouped catalog with real prices/durations and inline "Ask the assistant" suggested prompts specific to the selected service; the checkout page ("Booking details") correctly showed the real selected provider/time/service/total ($60.00, "You will earn 3 points after your visit"), a promo/gift-card code field, and its own inline AI suggestions. Did not click "Confirm booking" to avoid creating an unnecessary extra test booking. No bugs found in the non-AI rendering.

**e2e-bug.106 significantly broadened — this is a systemic pattern, not a manage-page-specific bug**: the checkout page's own official inline suggested prompt, `"Pay cash at visit"`, and a second explicit free-typed prompt, `"how much do I pay today?"` — both sent while a fully-configured booking (provider, time, service, $60 total) was already loaded on this exact checkout page — **both fell to the identical generic "Here's how to book an appointment on this page: Pick a professional or choose Any available" guide**, exactly the same failure mode already found on the guest manage page. This confirms the AI widget's failure to thread already-established page/booking context into its requests is **not isolated to the manage page** — it reproduces on the checkout page too, and by extension is likely a defect in the shared widget component/context-provider used across every specialized page on this surface, not a per-page integration bug. This substantially raises e2e-bug.106's real-world severity: the AI assistant is effectively unable to answer "about this" questions anywhere a customer has already made progress through a flow (checkout, manage-booking), consistently falling back to a generic first-step tutorial instead — actively unhelpful exactly when a customer would most want a quick, contextual answer (e.g. "how much do I pay today?" while looking at their own checkout total).

**Bonus, well-isolated finding on the locale question from before**: the checkout page's own success/status toast rendered in genuine Armenian (`"Հաջողությամբ ստեղծվեց:"` — "Successfully created:"), confirming the `app-locale=hy` cookie **does** correctly drive this app's general i18n system. This cleanly isolates the earlier locale finding: **general app UI strings correctly respect the locale cookie, but the AI assistant widget's own request-locale resolution does not** — it independently defaults to `'en'` regardless of the cookie, a narrower and more precisely diagnosable defect than originally suspected (not "locale switching doesn't work on this app" but specifically "the assistant widget's locale-sourcing is disconnected from the rest of the app's locale system").

**Section P correction — the "disconnected locale" conclusion above was a testing artifact, not a real defect; e2e-bug.87 is now proven live and directly visible in the real widget UI.** Found the actual in-UI locale switcher this pass: a native `<select>` (English / Հայերեն) at the bottom of every `/book/[slug]/*` page, wired to `I18nProvider`'s `setLocale()` (`frontend/src/i18n/I18nProvider.tsx:83-90`), which updates React state immediately *and* writes the `public`-scoped cookie via `writePublicCookieLocale()`. Using this real dropdown (not raw `document.cookie` mutation) correctly switched the entire page to Armenian, and — critically — the assistant widget's own header/suggested-prompts also rendered in Armenian. Root cause of the earlier "always en" finding: `I18nProvider` only reads the locale cookie once, in a `useState` lazy initializer (`I18nProvider.tsx:68-73`) — writing `document.cookie` directly after the provider has already mounted never updates its in-memory `locale` state (no listener re-reads the cookie), so the already-mounted widget kept sourcing the stale in-memory value. The dropdown's `setLocale()` call, by contrast, updates the state directly and doesn't rely on the cookie being re-read. **This is a testing-methodology correction, not a product bug** — traced the actual caller chain and confirmed `public-booking-assistant.tsx:206` passes `locale` straight from `useI18n()` into `sendPublicAssistantMessage()`, i.e. the widget's request-locale sourcing was never actually disconnected from the app's i18n system.

**Live proof, via a `window.fetch` interceptor installed in the real page (not a direct API call)**: after switching to Armenian via the dropdown and asking the widget `"ինչպե՞ս ամրագրել"` ("how do I book?"), the captured outgoing request body confirmed `"locale":"hy"` was genuinely sent by the live widget. The captured **response** body (and the on-screen chat transcript, which renders it verbatim) contained:
- `"summary":"Step 1 of 4: Քայլ 1"` — an untranslated English `"Step 1 of 4:"` prefix concatenated directly in front of the Armenian `"Քայլ 1"` ("Step 1"), shown as one sentence in the customer-facing chat bubble.
- `"voiceSummary":"Ընտրեք ծառայություն կամ «Որքան էլի_hasaneli»։"` — the same corruption family as e2e-bug.87's original finding, now with a literal underscore-joined Latin fragment (`_hasaneli`, a broken transliteration of «հասանելի» = "available") embedded mid-sentence in an otherwise-Armenian guide step, rendered directly in the visible guide card body.
- `"sources":[{"label":"Ամragreլ ayc", ...}]` — a topic label mixing Armenian letters with bare Latin fragments (`ragre`, `ayc`) in a single 3-word string, intended to read something like "Ամրագրման այց" ("Booking visit").

This **definitively upgrades e2e-bug.87's confirmed real-world exposure**: this is not a defect a customer could only hit via direct API access — it is reached through the single, standard, prominently-placed locale switcher every Armenian-speaking customer would naturally use, and the garbled text is rendered as-is directly in the visible chat transcript (with a working "Listen"/text-to-speech button reading the broken `voiceSummary` aloud). The open questions from the original Section P note are now resolved: (1) the mechanism is `I18nProvider`'s `setLocale()` → React context → `useI18n().locale`, correctly threaded by the widget; (2) yes, a real Armenian-speaking customer trivially reaches hy-locale responses through the live widget — e2e-bug.87's severity should be read as **confirmed, live, and directly customer-visible on this surface**, not merely a latent content defect.

### Section A/multi-service — multi-service picker + availability page, and a new non-AI i18n bug (e2e-bug.108)

**Multi-service picker page** (`/multi/availability`, still in hy locale from the locale investigation above): renders cleanly — package card, category-grouped individual services, correct checkbox selection state, correct running total/duration in the sticky footer. Selected two individual services (Face Pilling $5, Face Plasma $120) and continued to the block-availability step; no bugs in the picker itself.

**e2e-bug.108 (new, non-AI): a raw, untranslated English backend error string is shown to hy-locale customers on the multi-service availability page, silently overriding an existing, correct Armenian translation.** With no valid same-day block available for the selected services, the page displayed, verbatim inside an otherwise fully-Armenian page: `"No available block found for the selected services"`. Root-caused via source read: `frontend/src/components/public-booking/multi-service-availability-client.tsx:237` — `setError((err as Error)?.message || t('public.findAvailableBlockFailed'))` — prefers the raw thrown error's `.message` over the translated fallback string. The backend (`backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2472`) always throws a `BadRequestException` with a hardcoded English `.message`, so the `||` fallback is dead code for this exact error path — the perfectly good Armenian translation (`hy.ts:4301`, `"Չհաջողվեց գտնել հասանելի բլոկ"`) never has a chance to be used, even though it exists and is wired up correctly. Same root-cause *pattern* as e2e-bug.90's UI-layer finding (raw backend `.message` preferred over a local translated fallback) but a distinct call site/file — worth fixing together. **Fix direction**: drop the `(err as Error)?.message` branch (or gate it to dev-only/English-locale display) and always use the translated `t('public.findAvailableBlockFailed')` string for this and any sibling `catch` blocks in the same file following the identical `err.message || t(...)` pattern (line 165 has the same shape for `loadAvailableTimesFailed`, confirmed also affected — `hy.ts:4300` has a correct, currently-unreachable Armenian translation for it too — and should be fixed together).

**e2e-bug.106 reproduces a 3rd time, on a 3rd distinct page type**: with a real 3-service, $185 booking loaded on the multi-service availability page, asked the widget `"how much do I pay for this booking?"` — fell to the identical generic first-step guide fallback yet again, same failure mode as the manage page and checkout page. Confirms this is a page-agnostic defect in the shared widget/context layer, not tied to any specific route.

**e2e-bug.87 — new evidence of a worse corruption variant**: this response's guide content was for a *different* flow than the earlier repro (`"ՔԱՅԼ 1/2"`, a 2-step flow, vs. the earlier 4-step `consumer-booking-flow`) and its corruption is more severe — not mixed-script, but **entirely un-transliterated Latin text with zero Armenian characters** in the step body: `"Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»:"` (should read `"Ընտրեք մասնագետ կամ «Որքան էլի հասանելի»"` — "Select a specialist or 'however available'"). The preceding sentence in the same bubble is a mixed case of the already-documented pattern: `"Ահա ինչպես ամրագրել ayc այս էջում."` — fully Armenian except for one stray Latin word `ayc` (should be «այց», "visit") stranded mid-sentence. This confirms the hy-locale corruption in `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` isn't a single consistent failure mode — different blocks in the file are corrupted differently (mixed-script splicing in some, full Latin transliteration with no Armenian script at all in others), consistent with the file having been machine-translated in an inconsistent, never-reviewed pass rather than hand-authored.

### Section A/H — package detail page — new, severe, non-AI functional bug

Navigated to the real package detail page for this business's one real package (`Massage Package`, 5 lines, 365 total minutes, $344.25). The page itself renders correctly (full line-item breakdown, per-service savings, correct total), but the date/time picker shows **"Total visit duration (365 min) exceeds the 180 minute limit"** and **"No available times on this day"** for every day. Network inspection confirms this isn't a display-only warning — the underlying endpoints (`GET packages/:id/suggest-block`, `GET packages/:id/block-slots`) both return a real `400 Bad Request` with this exact message, for every date tried.

**New, severe finding — e2e-bug.107**: this business's one real, published package is **completely unbookable through the normal public web UI**, yet the exact same package **was successfully purchased earlier this session via the direct `POST packages/book` API endpoint** (see the "Post-closure addendum 4" package-purchase test in the closure section above, id `278cf621-...`) — a genuine, confirmed backend inconsistency, not a UI-only cosmetic issue. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read: [public-booking.service.ts:2076-2090](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2076) (`suggestPackageBlock`/`getPackageBlockDaySlots`, used by the customer-facing slot picker) delegate to the shared multi-service block-finder, which enforces `settings.maxDurationMinutes` (this business's configured cap, 180 minutes) via [multi-service-booking.util.ts:180-184](backend/src/common/utils/multi-service-booking.util.ts:180) — but [public-booking.service.ts:2128-2172](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2128) (`bookPackage`, the actual booking-creation endpoint) only calls `validatePackageSameDayBlock()` ([public-booking.service.ts:2164-2169](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2164)), which checks same-day/same-provider/back-to-back ordering but **never checks `maxDurationMinutes` at all**. The two code paths for the same package enforce different rules. **Real-world impact**: any package whose total duration exceeds a business's configured multi-service duration cap can be created and sold by the business (via onboarding/dashboard, with no warning that it will be unbookable), will display normally with full pricing on the public site, but a real customer using the actual booking flow can never find an available time slot for it and can never complete a purchase — while the exact same package remains purchasable via direct API integration or possibly a different client. **Fix direction**: either add the same `maxDurationMinutes` check to `bookPackage()` (reject creation consistently, matching the slot-finder), or — more likely the intended fix — exempt package bookings from the general multi-service duration cap entirely (since packages are pre-defined, business-curated bundles the owner explicitly chose to sell, unlike ad hoc multi-service carts a customer assembles themselves) and remove the check from `suggestPackageBlock`/`getPackageBlockDaySlots`. Either way, the two code paths must agree.

**Gift-cards page — confirmed clean, not a bug**: `/gift-cards` returns a genuine, intentional Next.js `notFound()` (404) for this business — confirmed via direct DB read that `businesses.settings.giftCards = {"purchaseEnabled": false}` for `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, and via direct source read of `gift-cards/page.tsx:16-18`, which explicitly calls `notFound()` whenever `!catalog.purchaseEnabled`. This is correct, deliberate gating, not a routing bug. **Useful clarifying context for e2e-bug.80** (the already-documented finding that `buy_gift_card`/`buy_gift_card_physical` are unreachable via the AI classifier): this confirms that even if the classifier were fixed, this specific test business wouldn't support gift-card purchase at all today — e2e-bug.80's classifier defect remains independently valid (zero trigger text exists regardless of business config), but any live re-test of the fix should use a business with `purchaseEnabled: true`, or the fix verification will hit this same, unrelated, correct 404.

### Section K priority — does the real client ever construct e2e-bug.96's IDOR-shaped request, and e2e-bug.109 (new)

Tested the originally-flagged priority question: as a fully anonymous (no session, no localStorage token) visitor, does the real widget UI ever naturally send a `confirm_my_booking_details`-shaped request without customer scoping? Installed a `window.fetch` interceptor and asked two prompts in sequence: a vague `"can you confirm the details of my booking?"`, then an explicit `"confirm the details for booking ID 12345"`. **Neither prompt caused the client to include a `bookingId`/`customerId`/any identifying param in the request body** — the client only ever sends `{prompt, history, context, locale}`; all param extraction happens server-side from free text. Both prompts fell to the identical generic fallback guide content (the same `guideFlowId` as e2e-bug.106's fallback), meaning the classifier never routed either prompt to `confirm_my_booking_details` at all in this session. **Conclusion**: casual/naive use of the real UI does not trivially reproduce e2e-bug.96's IDOR — the classifier's phrasing-matching for this intent didn't trigger even with an explicit "booking ID 12345" in the prompt. This narrows but does not eliminate real-world risk: e2e-bug.96 remains a fully confirmed backend vulnerability reachable via direct API (already proven earlier this session) and via any client phrasing that *does* match the intent's trigger patterns — this session's classifier-matching attempts were not exhaustive enough to rule that out, just two casual phrasings.

**e2e-bug.109 (new): the assistant widget silently drops part of the assistant's reply text whenever a guide block is attached to the same message.** The first prompt above returned a `summary` (confirmed via the request `history` echoed back on the next turn) of `"Sign in to view your appointments.\n\nԱհա ինչպես ամրագրել ayc այս էջում. Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»:"` — a real, meaningful status line ("Sign in to view your appointments.") explaining *why* the assistant couldn't answer, prepended to the generic guide text. The rendered chat transcript showed only the guide text; **"Sign in to view your appointments." never appeared anywhere in the page**, confirmed via a direct DOM query for any element containing "Sign in" (zero matches), not just a scroll/viewport artifact. Root cause, confirmed via source read: [public-booking-assistant.tsx:467-482](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx:467) — when `hasPublicAssistantGuideSteps(msg.guide)` is true, the component renders `<PublicAssistantGuidePanel guide={msg.guide} .../>` **instead of** `<p>{msg.text}</p>`, an either/or branch. Since `msg.text` is set from the full `result.summary` ([public-booking-assistant.tsx:215](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx:215)) and the "Sign in..." sentence is not part of `msg.guide`'s own fields, it is silently discarded any time a response carries both a plain-text prefix and a guide block. **Real-world impact**: any assistant response that combines an informational/status sentence with a fallback guide (which, per e2e-bug.106, happens very often given how frequently requests fall back to generic guide content) loses that informational sentence entirely — customers who aren't signed in and ask about "their" booking are shown a generic tutorial with no visible explanation that signing in is what's actually needed. **Fix direction**: render `msg.text` (when non-empty and distinct from the guide's own summary) above the guide panel rather than replacing it, e.g. `{msg.text && <p>{msg.text}</p>}{hasPublicAssistantGuideSteps(msg.guide) && <PublicAssistantGuidePanel .../>}`.

### Section K — account page (signed-in, real session) and a new missing-translation bug (e2e-bug.110)

Signed back in as the real test customer (Mary Torgomyan) via the same authorized `localStorage` JWT-injection technique used earlier this session. Account page rendered correctly in hy locale: profile, GDPR buttons, gift-card activation/redemption sections (both correctly empty — "No gift cards yet"), subscriptions section correctly empty ("No subscriptions yet" — this customer's earlier active subscription from prior testing appears to have been cancelled/expired since), and "My bookings" showing 2 real confirmed bookings with correct provider/time/status and a translated cancellation-window notice.

**e2e-bug.110 (new): a whole sentence in the referral section renders in raw, untranslated English on an otherwise fully-Armenian page**, because the message key it uses was never added to the hy/ru locale catalogs. Root-caused via source read: [public-account-growth-section.tsx:71-77](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-account-growth-section.tsx:71) picks between two i18n keys depending on whether the business has a dynamic reward summary configured (`program.referrerRewardSummary`) — `t('public.referralSectionBodyDynamic')` if so, else `t('public.referralSectionBody')`. This business has a dynamic reward summary, so the dynamic variant is selected — but `referralSectionBodyDynamic` exists only in [en.ts:4019](frontend/src/i18n/messages/en.ts:4019); it was never added to `hy.ts` or `ru.ts` (confirmed via grep — only the non-dynamic `referralSectionBody` has hy/ru entries, at `hy.ts:4452`/`ru.ts:2221`), so `t()` falls back to raw English for this key regardless of locale. **Fix direction**: add `referralSectionBodyDynamic` translations to `hy.ts` and `ru.ts`, matching the phrasing/placeholder pattern already used for the sibling `referralSectionBody` key in those files.

### AI Sections H/I/J — subscriptions, gift cards, rewards (signed-in customer)

Tested via the widget while signed in as the real test customer, with the response-logging interceptor capturing both request and response for each turn:
- `"what's my loyalty points balance?"` → correctly classified `loyalty_points_balance`, clean response ("You have 0 loyalty points (≈ $0 value)."). No bug.
- `"what subscription plans do you offer?"` → correctly classified `discover_subscription_plans`, clean response ("1 membership plan(s) available."). No bug.
- `"check my gift card balance"` → correctly classified `gift_card_balance`, but with no code in the prompt the backend replied `"Gift card not found."` (arguably should ask the customer to provide a code rather than claim "not found", but not pursued further as a separate bug) — **and e2e-bug.109 reproduces here too, in a more consequential form**: this response also carried a `guide` block, so per the same either/or render bug, `"Gift card not found."` never appeared anywhere in the DOM (confirmed via direct query, 0 matches) — the customer sees only a generic, unrelated guide card with no indication their balance check actually failed or why. This is a more damaging instance of e2e-bug.109 than the original "Sign in..." case: it hides direct negative feedback about the customer's own request, not just a peripheral status note.

### Section N — reviews, and a new classifier bug (e2e-bug.111)

Tested `leave_visit_review` via the widget while signed in, twice: `"I want to leave a review for my last visit"` and (retried with more explicit wording) `"leave a 5 star review for my facemassage visit"`. **Both times, reproducibly, the request was misclassified as `confirm_my_booking_details`** and failed with `"I could not find an upcoming booking to summarize. Finish checkout or pick an appointment from your account."` — a doubly-wrong response, since (a) the intent itself is wrong (the customer asked to leave a review, not to confirm booking details) and (b) even taken at face value the error is nonsensical: this customer has completed *past* bookings that are exactly what a review targets, but the wrong handler only looks for *upcoming* bookings.

**e2e-bug.111 (new)**: static analysis of the rescue logic suggests this should not happen. [ai-leave-visit-review.util.ts:343-353](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-leave-visit-review.util.ts:343) (`rescueLeaveVisitReviewIntent`) is wired into the classification pipeline's unconditional rescue stage ([command-understanding-pipeline.service.ts:109](backend/src/modules/ai/command-understanding-pipeline.service.ts:109) → `stageRescue`, called after every classification regardless of the classifier's chosen action or confidence), and its gating regexes — `REVIEW_CUE` (matches "review"), `CUSTOMER_OWNERSHIP_CUE` (matches "my") — both match the test prompts, and neither of the two early-exit cues (`EXPLAIN_REVIEW_PROMPT_CUE`, `REPORT_PROBLEM_CUE`) match either. Tracing the regexes by hand indicates `isLeaveVisitReviewPrompt()` should return `true` for both prompts, meaning `rescueLeaveVisitReviewIntent()` should reclassify them to `leave_visit_review` — yet live testing shows the misclassification winning 2/2. The discrepancy between the static rescue logic and observed live behavior was not fully root-caused this pass (candidates: a different/earlier rescue or the public-surface request path may bypass or short-circuit before reaching `stageRescue`, or another item earlier in the same rescue chain may be intercepting first without actually changing the final `action` — needs a source-level trace of the *public* assistant request path specifically, as this may differ from the customer-session path already covered by this rescue's existing unit tests). **Real-world impact**: `leave_visit_review` appears effectively unreachable via natural phrasing on this web surface — a real customer trying to leave a review through the AI assistant gets a confusing, wrong-domain error instead. **Fix direction**: add a live integration-level regression test (not just the existing unit tests on the util functions in isolation) asserting these exact two prompts classify to `leave_visit_review` end-to-end through the real public assistant endpoint, then trace/fix wherever the live pipeline diverges from the static rescue logic.

### Section O — support, and a 3rd reproduction of e2e-bug.109

`"I need help, contact support please"` → correctly classified `contact_support`, correctly surfaced the known "Zendesk is not configured for this business" status (matching the already-documented finding that this is genuinely correct behavior for this test business). **But e2e-bug.109 reproduces a 3rd time**: this response also carried a `guide` block, so — per the same either/or render bug — "Zendesk is not configured for this business" never appeared in the DOM (confirmed via direct query, 0 matches), leaving the customer with only a generic guide card and zero indication support is unavailable or why. Between this, the gift-card-balance case, and the original "Sign in..." case, e2e-bug.109 now has 3 independent reproductions across 3 different intents (`gift_card_balance`, `contact_support`, and the original vague `confirm_my_booking_details` fallback), all sharing the same root cause and all losing meaningful, distinct informational content — this is a systemic rendering defect, not a one-off.

### Section waitlist — join_waitlist, and a new params-extraction bug (e2e-bug.112)

`"put me on the waitlist for Gevorg Gasparyan tomorrow"` (a provider name only, no service mentioned) → correctly classified `join_waitlist`, but the confirmation text read: **`"You're on the waitlist — we'll notify you if something opens for Gevorg Gasparyan with Gevorg Gasparyan on 18/07/2026."`** — the provider's name appears twice, once as the service and once as the provider.

**e2e-bug.112 (new)**: root-caused the *rendering* half precisely — [customer-waitlist.util.ts:145-150](backend/src/common/utils/customer-waitlist.util.ts:145) (`buildJoinWaitlistSuccessSummary` → `formatCustomerWaitlistPreferenceSummary`) is working exactly as designed, joining `request.serviceName` and `` `with ${request.employeeName}` `` — the bug is that both fields were populated with the identical string `"Gevorg Gasparyan"` upstream, before this formatter ever runs. Since only a provider name was mentioned in the prompt, `serviceName` should have been left unset (which this formatter already handles gracefully — it only pushes fields that are truthy). This points to param extraction (likely the classifier's own entity-matching, given this business has a learned alias `"gevorg" → provider=Gevorg Gasparyan` from its `_entityMemoryBlock`, seen in earlier session testing) incorrectly duplicating a resolved provider-name match into the `serviceName` slot as well. Did not fully trace the exact extraction call site this pass (likely LLM/classifier-side entity resolution rather than a single deterministic regex util, given the classifier-rules comment for this intent — `ai-customer-waitlist.fixtures.ts:12` — describes `serviceName`/`employeeName` as "set... when mentioned" without a dedicated parser function found via grep). **Real-world impact**: any waitlist request naming only a provider (a very natural phrasing) produces a visibly broken, duplicated confirmation message. — **Fixed:** (1) `extractWaitlistServiceName` no longer treats proper names as services; `extractWaitlistEmployeeName` + `sanitizeWaitlistPreferenceNames` promote provider-only "for Gevorg Gasparyan" into `employeeName`. (2) Stop inheriting greedy `buildSharedBookingContextFromPrompt` serviceName into waitlist enrich. (3) Formatter + `resolveWaitlistPreferences` drop `serviceName` when it duplicates `employeeName`. Specs: `ai-customer-waitlist.util.spec.ts` (`E2E112_PROVIDER_ONLY_WAITLIST_SCENARIOS`), `customer-waitlist.util` summary dedupe.

### Section M — payments/checkout AI, and a new classifier bug (e2e-bug.113)

Tested two related deposit-policy prompts while signed in:
- `"why do I have to pay a deposit to book?"` → misclassified `explain_checkout_currency`, answering entirely about currency ("Prices... shown in US dollars") — a completely wrong domain, not even payments-adjacent.
- `"explain the deposit forfeiture policy if I cancel late"` → misclassified `explain_why_stripe_required`, answering about why Stripe/card payment is required generally — payments-domain-adjacent but still not the actual forfeiture-on-late-cancellation question asked.

**e2e-bug.113 (new)**: neither prompt reached `explain_deposit_forfeiture`, a dedicated intent that demonstrably exists (referenced via `tryRescueExplainDepositForfeiture` in the same rescue chain examined for e2e-bug.111, `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:1001-1005`). Two independently-phrased, clearly deposit/forfeiture-themed prompts both landed on different wrong intents rather than the one that's actually designed to answer this exact question — one wildly off-domain (currency), one adjacent-but-wrong (generic Stripe-requirement explainer). This wasn't root-caused to a specific regex/classifier gap this pass (unlike e2e-bug.111, time didn't allow tracing `tryRescueExplainDepositForfeiture`'s own gating conditions), but the pattern — two natural phrasings, two different wrong answers, zero hits on the right one — indicates `explain_deposit_forfeiture` is difficult to reach via natural language on this surface. — **Fixed:** (1) Broadened `isExplainDepositForfeiturePrompt` for `forfeit(?:ure)?` and `"why … pay a deposit to book?"`; kept named-service / booking-page `"why is there a deposit"` on why-stripe. (2) Stopped `rescueExplainPrepaymentIntent` / `isExplainWhyPrepaymentPrompt` from overwriting deposit-forfeiture (the real steal for the late-cancel prompt — public rescue ran deposit first, then prepayment remapped to `explain_why_stripe_required`). Specs: `ai-explain-deposit-forfeiture.util.spec.ts` + fixtures (`e2e-bug.113`).

### Section Q — compound intents (signed-in customer), and a new severe classifier bug (e2e-bug.114)

Tested a natural two-step compound request while signed in: `"cancel my facemassage booking and rebook it for next Friday instead"`. This is structurally the same kind of compound the already-shipped `guest_manage_visit` compound (documented earlier this session, `ai-guest-manage-visit-compound.util.ts`) handles for anonymous guests — but that compound is explicitly guest-only (`isGuestContext()` requires no `sessionCustomerId`/`customerId`). No equivalent signed-in-customer compound was found via earlier code review this session.

**e2e-bug.114 (new, severe)**: the result wasn't merely "compound not supported, falls back to a generic guide" (the pattern established for e2e-bug.106) — it was classified as **`pay_at_venue_fallback`**, a completely unrelated cash-payment intent, which then failed with `"Cash pay-at-venue is not enabled — this business requires online card checkout."` (`success: false`). Nothing about cancelling, rebooking, "facemassage", or "Friday" is reflected anywhere in the response — this is a wild, high-confidence misclassification to a totally unrelated domain, worse than a graceful fallback. **No real mutation occurred** (the wrong intent failed before touching the booking), so no test-data cleanup is needed from this specific test. **e2e-bug.109 reproduces a 4th time** on this same response — it also carried a `guide` block, so "Cash pay-at-venue is not enabled..." never appeared in the DOM (confirmed via direct query, 0 matches). **Real-world impact**: a customer trying to reschedule via a natural "cancel and rebook" phrasing gets sent down a completely unrelated payment-method dead end, with the actual failure reason hidden from them by e2e-bug.109 on top of that. — **Fixed:** (1) `INSTEAD_CUE` in `ai-pay-at-venue-fallback.util.ts` no longer matches bare `\binstead\b` without payment/venue/online context; booking cancel/rebook/reschedule prompts are excluded. (2) Dated cancel+rebook (`cancel … and rebook … for next Friday`) routes to `reschedule_my_booking` (not cancel→book-nearest, not pay-at-venue). (3) Public assistant rescues that phrasing before `pay_at_venue_fallback`, dispatches `reschedule_my_booking` / `cancel_my_booking` via `AiSelfServiceBookingService`, and exposes those actions in `public-booking-classifier.schema.ts`. Specs: `ai-pay-at-venue-fallback.util.spec.ts`, `ai-cancel-and-rebook-compound.util.spec.ts`, `ai-reschedule-my-booking.util.spec.ts` (`e2e-bug.114`).

### Progress summary and remaining scope
Substantial ground covered this pass: e2e-bug.106 is now a well-evidenced, broad, 4x-reproduced finding (manage page ×2, checkout page ×2, multi-service availability ×1) with a precise mechanism hypothesis (shared widget component doesn't thread page-level context into AI requests); the locale question is fully resolved — e2e-bug.87 is confirmed live and directly customer-visible via the real locale switcher, with the earlier "disconnected" finding corrected as a testing-methodology artifact; e2e-bug.107 is a new, severe, precisely-root-caused, non-AI backend inconsistency making this business's one real package completely unbookable via the public website; e2e-bug.108 and e2e-bug.110 are new non-AI i18n bugs (raw English text overriding/missing working Armenian translations, in two unrelated files); e2e-bug.109 is a new UI bug (assistant silently drops informational text whenever a guide block is attached) now confirmed 3x across 3 different intents (`gift_card_balance`, `contact_support`, and the original vague-`confirm_my_booking_details`-fallback case); e2e-bug.111 is a new, reproducible (2/2) classifier bug where `leave_visit_review` prompts are misclassified to `confirm_my_booking_details` despite static rescue-logic analysis suggesting they should route correctly; the Section K priority question (does the real client construct e2e-bug.96's IDOR shape) was tested and found **not** trivially reproducible via casual UI phrasing, narrowing but not eliminating that risk; loyalty/subscription-discovery AI intents (H/J) tested clean; e2e-bug.112 is a new params-extraction bug where a provider-only waitlist request duplicates the provider's name into the service-name slot too, producing a visibly broken confirmation message; e2e-bug.113 is a new classifier-accuracy finding where two independently-phrased deposit/forfeiture questions both missed the dedicated `explain_deposit_forfeiture` intent, landing on two different wrong answers instead; e2e-bug.114 is a new, severe compound-intent finding — a natural "cancel and rebook" phrasing while signed in doesn't decompose into two steps (no signed-in equivalent of the guest compound exists) and, worse, gets classified with high confidence into a completely unrelated intent (`pay_at_venue_fallback`) rather than falling back gracefully, with e2e-bug.109 compounding the damage by hiding the resulting error text (4th reproduction); and the gift-cards page 404 was confirmed as correct, deliberate behavior (not a bug). Robustness/fallback-quality (Section R/S) is considered adequately covered by this pass's cumulative evidence — every misclassification found (e2e-bug.111, .113, .114) degraded to *some* response rather than crashing, and the earlier-session finding that 3 independent garbled/off-domain prompts all fell to the same generic `unknown` fallback still stands unchallenged. This pass's session total: 9 new confirmed bugs (e2e-bug.106 broadened + e2e-bug.107 through e2e-bug.114) plus one major correction (e2e-bug.87's real-world reachability). Remaining scope: Section B (full API sweep — much of this already covered via the consumer-app plan's parallel API sweep, M1-M20, but not yet re-verified through this specific web surface) and Section C/D (cross-cutting/edge cases: auth/IDOR, cross-tenant, responsive layout, concurrency) — both lower-priority, infrastructure-style sweeps rather than likely sources of new distinct bugs given the density of findings already surfaced through direct feature testing.

- **e2e-bug.34 — FIXED.** Multi-service visits rendered as N standalone Account cards with no whole-visit cancel/reschedule UI because `multiServiceGroupId` never reached the client. - **e2e-bug.35 — FIXED.** Multi-service Stripe Checkout fulfillment never merged `stripePaymentIntentId` into `bookMultiService` (unlike `package_purchase`), so cancel always skipped auto-refund. `fulfillDraft` now threads Connect/PI/session metadata; `bookMultiService` stamps those ids on every line + the group (not only index 0 pricing meta). - **e2e-bug.36 — FIXED.** Package-visit reschedule picker (`ConsumerPackageVisitActions`) swallowed `suggestPackageBlock` / `fetchPackageBlockSlots` failures with empty catch blocks, leaving a blank calendar and a disabled Confirm button with no explanation (worse than raw-axios siblings). - **e2e-bug.39 — FIXED.** BookPage rendered every submit-time `message` through `ConsumerNetworkErrorCard` with a "Try again" button — including client-side validation (missing contact / subscription plan) that retry cannot fix.
